examples.en: Social media is flooded with abusive comments too vile to look at.
examples.ja: SNSには、見るに堪えない誹謗中傷のコメントがあふれている。

examples.en: Having received warm support from so many people, I cannot express how grateful I am.
examples.ja: 多くの方々から温かいご支援をいただき、感謝の念に堪えない。

examples.en: The lawmakers' exchange of jeers, painful to listen to, drew sighs from the public gallery.
examples.ja: 議員同士の聞くに堪えないやじの応酬に、傍聴席からため息がもれた。

records.formation: V辞書形(見る・聞く・読む) + に堪えない / N(感謝・遺憾・痛恨) + に堪えない
records.meaning: too awful to …; cannot contain (one's gratitude, regret)
records.nuance: Formal. With perception verbs it condemns something as unbearable to watch, hear or read; with emotion nouns it is a ceremonial way of saying a feeling is overwhelming, used in speeches, letters and official apologies.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に堪える: the positive counterpart, 'worth / able to stand up to'
〜てたまらない: casual, personal 'can't stand / so much'
〜に忍びない: cannot bring oneself to do something, out of pity or guilt

similar: 〜に堪える: the positive counterpart, 'worth / able to stand up to'
〜てたまらない: casual, personal 'can't stand / so much'
〜に忍びない: cannot bring oneself to do something, out of pity or guilt

examples.en: Lunch at this place is cheap and generous too, so there is always a queue.
examples.ja: この店のランチは安い上に量も多いので、いつも行列ができている。

examples.en: On top of getting lost, it even started to rain.
examples.ja: 道に迷った上に、雨まで降り出した。

examples.en: The new office is far from the station, and there isn't even a convenience store nearby.
examples.ja: 新しいオフィスは駅から遠い上、周りにコンビニもない。

records.formation: V / Aい 普通形 + 上(に) / Aな な・である + 上(に) / N の・である + 上(に)
records.meaning: on top of …; besides …; not only … but also
records.nuance: Adds a second point pointing the same way as the first (both good or both bad), often with も or まで in the second clause. Common in speech and writing, but the second clause cannot be a command, request or invitation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでなく: neutral 'not only … but also'
〜ばかりか: stronger, the second item is surprising
〜上で: 'after doing / in doing', a different meaning

similar: 〜だけでなく: neutral 'not only … but also'
〜ばかりか: stronger, the second item is surprising
〜上で: 'after doing / in doing', a different meaning

examples.en: Knowing how quickly my younger brother loses interest, he'll probably give up on the guitar he just bought within three days.
examples.ja: 飽きっぽい弟のことだから、買ったばかりのギターもどうせ三日で放り出すだろう。

examples.en: Knowing how meticulous my mother is, she must have finished packing for the trip long ago.
examples.ja: 几帳面な母のことだから、旅行の準備はとっくに済ませているはずだ。

examples.en: Knowing how cautious our manager always is, I don't think we'll get an answer right away.
examples.ja: いつも慎重なうちの部長のことだから、すぐには返事をくれないと思うよ。

records.formation: Nの + ことだから
records.meaning: knowing …, surely …; since it's … we're talking about
records.nuance: The speaker makes a confident guess from what they know of a person's or group's character; the main clause is usually a conjecture (〜だろう, 〜に違いない, 〜はずだ). Conversational, and can be admiring or ironic.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ことから: objective evidence, written, not about character
〜だけあって: evaluates a result as befitting someone's status rather than predicting
〜のことなので: a slightly politer variant

similar: 〜ことから: objective evidence, written, not about character
〜だけあって: evaluates a result as befitting someone's status rather than predicting
〜のことなので: a slightly politer variant

examples.en: If the losses keep up like this, the shop will have to close sooner or later.
examples.ja: このまま赤字が続けば、遅かれ早かれ店を畳むことになるだろう。

examples.en: Everyone gets nervous, to a greater or lesser degree, when speaking in front of people.
examples.ja: 多かれ少なかれ、誰でも人前で話すときは緊張するものだ。

examples.en: For better or worse, social media has greatly changed the way we take in information.
examples.ja: 良かれ悪しかれ、SNSは私たちの情報の受け取り方を大きく変えた。

records.formation: Aい語幹 + かれ + 対義Aい語幹 + かれ (遅かれ早かれ・多かれ少なかれ・良かれ悪しかれ)
records.meaning: whether … or …; one way or the other (fixed pairs such as sooner or later, more or less)
records.nuance: A frozen classical construction that survives only in a few set pairs of opposite adjectives; it says the outcome holds regardless of which extreme applies. Common in essays, news commentary and serious conversation, often with a resigned or matter-of-fact tone.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にしろ〜にしろ: productive 'whether X or Y' with any words; かれ〜かれ is limited to fixed adjective pairs
〜であれ〜であれ: 'whether X or Y' with nouns, formal; not restricted to opposites
〜につけ〜につけ: 'whenever / whether X or Y' with emotional or situational pairs (良きにつけ悪しきにつけ)

similar: 〜にしろ〜にしろ: productive 'whether X or Y' with any words; かれ〜かれ is limited to fixed adjective pairs
〜であれ〜であれ: 'whether X or Y' with nouns, formal; not restricted to opposites
〜につけ〜につけ: 'whenever / whether X or Y' with emotional or situational pairs (良きにつけ悪しきにつけ)

records.formation: どんなに／どれほど／何度 など + 普通形（ナAな／である） + ことか
records.meaning: how …!; how many times …! (exclamation)
records.nuance: A strong, heartfelt exclamation, usually paired with a question word such as どんなに, どれほど or 何度. Slightly rhetorical and written in tone; in speech it sounds deeply emotional.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ものだ: exclamation of deep feeling or general truth, without the question word
〜だろう: どんなに〜だろう is similar but softer and more speculative
〜ことだ: can express advice ('you should …') or an exclamation (なんと美しいことだ); ことか typically pairs with a degree or quantity question word

similar: 〜ものだ: exclamation of deep feeling or general truth, without the question word
〜だろう: どんなに〜だろう is similar but softer and more speculative
〜ことだ: can express advice ('you should …') or an exclamation (なんと美しいことだ); ことか typically pairs with a degree or quantity question word

examples.en: Wanting to be of at least some help to the disaster area, many young people joined as volunteers.
examples.ja: 少しなりとも被災地の役に立ちたいと、多くの若者がボランティアに参加した。

examples.en: I would love to catch even a glimpse of my hometown's cherry blossoms once more.
examples.ja: 一目なりとも、故郷の桜をもう一度見たいものだ。

examples.en: If we can expect even a slight improvement in revenue, this measure is worth trying.
examples.ja: わずかなりとも収益の改善が見込めるなら、この施策を試す価値はある。

records.formation: N（少し・多少・わずか・一目 など最小量の語）+ なりとも
records.meaning: even a little; at least …
records.nuance: Formal and somewhat old-fashioned. Attaches to words for a minimal amount and expresses a modest wish or condition, often with 〜たい, 〜ば or 〜てほしい.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでも: 'at least', conversational
〜でも: casual 'even'
〜たりとも: used with a negative, 'not even one'; strict rather than modest

similar: 〜だけでも: 'at least', conversational
〜でも: casual 'even'
〜たりとも: used with a negative, 'not even one'; strict rather than modest

examples.en: On a muggy summer night, nothing beats an ice-cold beer.
examples.ja: 蒸し暑い夏の夜は、やっぱり冷えたビールに限る。

examples.en: When you're worn out, the best thing is to sleep soundly and not think about anything.
examples.ja: 疲れがたまっている時は、何も考えずにぐっすり寝るに限る。

examples.en: With difficult people at work, it's best to stay out of their way as much as possible.
examples.ja: 職場の面倒な人とは、なるべく関わらないに限る。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 / Vない形 + に限る
records.meaning: nothing beats …; the best thing is to …
records.nuance: The speaker's emphatic, personal judgment that X is the best choice in a given situation; conversational and subjective. In notices it can also mean 'limited to' (参加者は会員に限る).

relatedReferences.text: 〜に越したことはない: general common-sense 'best if possible', milder and less personal
〜が一番だ: plain 'is the best', less emphatic
〜に限り: formal 'limited to/only' in rules and notices

similar: 〜に越したことはない: general common-sense 'best if possible', milder and less personal
〜が一番だ: plain 'is the best', less emphatic
〜に限り: formal 'limited to/only' in rules and notices

records.formation: Vた形 + かと思うと / かと思ったら (普通形 + かと思ったら: 'I thought …, but')
records.meaning: no sooner … than …; just when I thought …
records.nuance: Describes a second event following the first almost immediately and unexpectedly, or a reality overturning what the speaker assumed. In the rapid-succession use, it describes observed events rather than the speaker's own deliberate actions and is not followed by commands or intentions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たとたん(に): 'the moment …', can describe one's own action; かと思うと is only for events the speaker observes
〜か〜ないかのうちに: even tighter timing, 'barely had … when'

examples.cloze: 美しさといったらなかった
examples.en: The beauty of the sunrise I saw from the summit for the first time was beyond words.

examples.cloze: 悔しいといったらない

examples.ja: 決勝であと一歩のところで逆転負けするなんて、悔しいといったらない。

examples.en: The new department head talks on and on beyond belief. The morning meeting lasts nearly an hour every day.

records.formation: N / イA辞書形 / ナA語幹 + といったらない（口語: ったらない）
records.meaning: indescribably …; so … beyond words
records.nuance: Emphasises that a feeling or quality is so intense it cannot be put into words, in either a good or bad sense. Emotional and conversational; the past form といったらなかった recalls an experience.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ことこの上ない: formal 'extremely', without the emotional outburst
〜てたまらない: about the speaker's own sensation; といったらない describes the degree of a quality
〜といったらありゃしない: colloquial variant, mostly for negative feelings

similar: 〜ことこの上ない: formal 'extremely', without the emotional outburst
〜てたまらない: about the speaker's own sensation; といったらない describes the degree of a quality
〜といったらありゃしない: colloquial variant, mostly for negative feelings

examples.cloze: 引き受けないものでもない

examples.cloze: 間に合わないものでもない

examples.en: I can sort of understand the other side's argument, but I still can't agree with their methods.

records.formation: Vない形 + ものでもない / Vない形 + でもない
records.meaning: it is not impossible that …; one might (reluctantly) …
records.nuance: Formal, hedging double negative. Expresses reluctant or partial possibility or willingness; the speaker stops short of a clear yes, often adding conditions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ないとも限らない: warns that a (usually bad) thing could happen

〜ないこともない: near-synonym; more conversational and far more common in speech

records.formation: N(組織・地域・集団) + きっての + N
records.meaning: the most … in all of (a group or place); the best in …
records.nuance: Praises someone or something as the top example within a defined organisation, region or field. Formal and somewhat literary, typical of journalism and introductions; nearly always positive.

relatedReferences.text: 〜随一の: 'the foremost in', a near-synonym; 随一 can also end a sentence (業界随一だ), while きっての only modifies a following noun

records.formation: N / V普通形 + にすぎない
records.meaning: nothing more than …; merely
records.nuance: Downplays something as small or insignificant; common in news commentary and argument, often with ほんの, 単なる or 一部.

examples.cloze: 備えておくに越したことはない

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vない形 / い形容詞 / な形容詞語幹・N(である) + に越したことはない
records.meaning: nothing is better than …; it is best (if possible) to …
records.nuance: States a common-sense ideal: doing or having X is the safest, best option, though not strictly required. Often followed by が/けど to add a practical reservation; neutral register, common in advice and commentary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に限る: emphatic personal 'nothing beats'; に越したことはない is a milder, common-sense 'best if possible'
〜ほうがいい: everyday advice for a specific case, without the 'ideally' tone
〜べきだ: states a duty; に越したことはない only says it would be better

〜はともかく: neutral 'setting aside', no complaint built in

examples.en: In the park, the children were cheerfully playing tag.
examples.ja: 公園では、子どもたちが楽しげに鬼ごっこをしていた。

examples.en: The clerk was staring at me with a look that suggested they wanted to say something.
examples.ja: その店員は、何か言いたげな顔でこちらをじっと見ていた。

examples.en: The player who scored proudly pointed to the badge on the chest of his jersey.
examples.ja: ゴールを決めた選手は、得意げにユニフォームの胸のエンブレムを指さした。

records.formation: イA語幹 / ナA語幹 / Vたい→Vたげ / 一部の動詞ます形（ありげ） + げ（だ／な／に）　※ない→なさげ、いい→よさげ
records.meaning: -looking; with an air of …; seeming …
records.nuance: Describes how someone or something appears from the outside, especially visible feelings (寂しげ, 得意げ). Somewhat literary and common in narration; casual speech uses forms like よさげ and なさげ.

relatedReferences.text: 〜そう: the everyday way to say 'looks …' (楽しそう); げ is more literary and leans toward visible emotion
〜っぽい: casual '-ish / kind of', also used for tendencies
〜らしい: 'typical of' or hearsay, not a visual impression

similar: 〜そう: the everyday way to say 'looks …' (楽しそう); げ is more literary and leans toward visible emotion
〜っぽい: casual '-ish / kind of', also used for tendencies
〜らしい: 'typical of' or hearsay, not a visual impression

examples.en: Some days go well and some don't. That's just what life is.
examples.ja: うまくいく日もあれば、そうでない日もある。それが人生というものだ。

examples.en: Hearing the other person out to the end is what courtesy is.
examples.ja: 相手の話を最後まで聞くのが、礼儀というものだ。

examples.en: Making them keep playing in this downpour is surely just unreasonable.
examples.ja: こんな大雨の中で試合を続けさせるのは、無理というものだろう。

records.formation: N / なA語幹 / V・いA普通形 + というものだ
records.meaning: that is what … truly is; that is simply …
records.nuance: Presents the speaker's judgement as a general truth or the essence of something. Firm and slightly didactic; common in essays, editorials and pointed remarks.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ものだ: general nature or tendency, less emphatic
〜わけだ: logical conclusion drawn from facts
〜というものではない: negative form, 'it does not necessarily follow'

similar: 〜ものだ: general nature or tendency, less emphatic
〜わけだ: logical conclusion drawn from facts
〜というものではない: negative form, 'it does not necessarily follow'

examples.en: Using a smartphone while driving is an extremely dangerous act.
examples.ja: 運転中にスマホを操作するのは、危険極まりない行為だ。

examples.en: Turning up an hour late for the reservation without a single word of apology is the height of rudeness.
examples.ja: 予約の時間に一時間も遅れておきながら謝罪の一言もないとは、失礼極まりない。

examples.en: At the post-match press conference, the manager sharply criticized the referees, calling it an utterly baffling decision.
examples.ja: 監督は試合後の会見で「不可解極まる判定だった」と審判団を厳しく批判した。

records.formation: ナ形容詞語幹 + 極まりない / 極まる；イ形容詞い・ナ形容詞な + こと + 極まりない（例: 危険極まりない、失礼極まる、腹立たしいこと極まりない）
records.meaning: utterly …; … in the extreme (the literary variant kiwamaru means the same)
records.nuance: A formal, emphatic way to condemn something, mostly with negative na-adjectives such as 失礼, 危険, 迷惑, 不愉快 and 退屈. Common in news, editorials and angry complaints; 〜極まる means the same but sounds more literary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜の極み: 'the height of', attaches to nouns (感激の極み, 贅沢の極み) and can be positive
〜この上ない: 'nothing could be more', also used for positive things (光栄この上ない)
〜限りだ: voices the speaker's own feeling (嬉しい限りだ) rather than a judgment of something

similar: 〜の極み: 'the height of', attaches to nouns (感激の極み, 贅沢の極み) and can be positive
〜この上ない: 'nothing could be more', also used for positive things (光栄この上ない)
〜限りだ: voices the speaker's own feeling (嬉しい限りだ) rather than a judgment of something

examples.cloze: なってからというもの
examples.en: Ever since I started working from home, the fatigue of commuting has gone and I can make good use of my mornings.
examples.ja: 在宅勤務になってからというもの、通勤の疲れがなくなり、朝の時間を有効に使えるようになった。

examples.cloze: できてからというもの
examples.en: Ever since a big shopping mall opened in front of the station, foot traffic in the shopping street has dropped sharply.
examples.ja: 駅前に大型ショッピングモールができてからというもの、商店街の人通りはめっきり減ってしまった。

examples.cloze: 生まれてからというもの
examples.en: Ever since our child was born, I haven't once sat back and watched a movie at night.
examples.ja: 子どもが生まれてからというもの、夜にゆっくり映画を見たことなど一度もない。

records.formation: Vて形 + からというもの
records.meaning: ever since … (a lasting change)
records.nuance: Marks a turning point after which the situation has changed and stayed changed; the speaker looks back with feeling at how different things have been since. Literary and emotional, so it rarely appears with routine events.

relatedReferences.text: 〜て以来: neutral 'since'; てからというもの stresses a striking, lasting change and carries more feeling
〜てから: plain 'after'; no sense of a continuing changed state
〜を境に: 'with … as a turning point', also used for one-off shifts and in reports

similar: 〜て以来: neutral 'since'; てからというもの stresses a striking, lasting change and carries more feeling
〜てから: plain 'after'; no sense of a continuing changed state
〜を境に: 'with … as a turning point', also used for one-off shifts and in reports

examples.en: After being spoken to like that, how could I possibly keep quiet?
examples.ja: あんなひどい言い方をされて、黙っていられるものか。

examples.en: As if those people could understand what we've been through.
examples.ja: こっちの苦労なんて、あの人たちにわかるものか。

examples.en: "Tired already?" "No way am I tired. I can keep running for ages."
examples.ja: 「もう疲れた？」「疲れてなんかいるもんか。まだまだ走れるよ。」

records.formation: V辞書形 / い形容詞 / な形容詞語幹な / Nな + ものか（口語: もんか、丁寧: ものですか）
records.meaning: as if …!; no way …!; I'll never …!
records.nuance: A rhetorical question used as a strong, emotional denial or refusal. Mostly spoken; もんか is casual and blunt, and ものですか is softer and sometimes heard in women's speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜わけがない: firm logical denial, less emotional than ものか
〜はずがない: denial based on reasoning or expectation, calm in tone
〜てたまるか: 'I won't let …', a defiant refusal to accept something happening

similar: 〜わけがない: firm logical denial, less emotional than ものか
〜はずがない: denial based on reasoning or expectation, calm in tone
〜てたまるか: 'I won't let …', a defiant refusal to accept something happening

examples.en: I decided to change jobs after talking it over thoroughly with my family.
examples.ja: 家族とよく話し合った上で、転職を決めた。

examples.cloze: ご確認いただいた上で
examples.en: Please apply after reading the terms of use.
examples.ja: 利用規約をご確認いただいた上で、お申し込みください。

examples.en: What matters in learning a foreign language is not being afraid of mistakes.
examples.ja: 外国語を学ぶ上で大切なのは、間違いを恐れないことだ。

records.formation: Vた形 + 上で (after) / V辞書形 + 上で (in doing) / Nの + 上で
records.meaning: after (doing, as a necessary step); in (doing) / for (the purpose of)
records.nuance: With Vた it marks a step that must be done before the next action (decide after consulting); with V辞書形 it means 'when it comes to doing'. Slightly formal; frequent in instructions and advice.

relatedReferences.text: 〜てから: plain sequence, without the sense of a required first step
〜にあたって: 'on the occasion of / when undertaking', more formal
〜上(に): 'besides / on top of', adding a point

similar: 〜てから: plain sequence, without the sense of a required first step
〜にあたって: 'on the occasion of / when undertaking', more formal
〜上(に): 'besides / on top of', adding a point

examples.en: Speaking from experience, the first three months at a new workplace are the hardest.
examples.ja: 経験から言うと、新しい職場では最初の三か月がいちばん大変だ。

examples.en: In terms of price, this plan is by far the better deal.
examples.ja: 価格の面から言えば、こちらのプランのほうがはるかにお得だ。

examples.en: From the standpoint of environmental protection, reducing single-use plastics is an issue that cannot be avoided.
examples.ja: 環境保護の観点から言うと、使い捨てプラスチックの削減は避けて通れない課題だ。

records.formation: N + から言うと / から言えば / から言って
records.meaning: from the standpoint of …; in terms of …; speaking from …
records.nuance: Introduces the criterion or standpoint behind a judgment (経験, 立場, 観点, 面). Neutral register; it normally follows abstract nouns rather than a person.

relatedReferences.text: 〜からすると: 'judging from / from someone's viewpoint', can follow people
〜にとって: how something is for a particular person
〜の点では: 'as far as … is concerned', names the aspect more explicitly

similar: 〜からすると: 'judging from / from someone's viewpoint', can follow people
〜にとって: how something is for a particular person
〜の点では: 'as far as … is concerned', names the aspect more explicitly

examples.en: Now that I've taken it on, I intend to take responsibility and see it through to the end.
examples.ja: 引き受けたからには、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げるつもりだ。

examples.en: Since I'm going to live in Japan, I want to be able to speak Japanese properly.
examples.ja: 日本に住むからには、日本語をきちんと話せるようになりたい。

examples.en: Now that we have been chosen as representatives, we must compete in a way worthy of the team's name.
examples.ja: 代表に選ばれたからには、チームの名に恥じない戦いをしなければならない。

records.formation: 普通形 (Nである / な形容詞である) + からには
records.meaning: now that …; since … (so one must / intends to …)
records.nuance: Given a situation, the speaker states resolve, obligation or a firm conclusion (〜べきだ, 〜つもりだ, 〜なければならない). Determined in tone; used in both speech and writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜以上(は): almost identical, slightly more logical and formal
〜上は: formal, literary equivalent (N1)
〜から: plain reason without the sense of resolve

similar: 〜以上(は): almost identical, slightly more logical and formal
〜上は: formal, literary equivalent (N1)
〜から: plain reason without the sense of resolve

examples.en: Ever since graduating from university, we've gone on a trip with the same group of friends every year.
examples.ja: 大学を卒業して以来、毎年同じ仲間で旅行に出かけている。

examples.en: Ever since a large shopping complex opened by the station, land prices in the area have kept rising.
examples.ja: 駅前に大型商業施設が開業して以来、周辺の地価は上昇を続けている。

examples.en: Ever since I moved to this town, my neighbours have always been there to help me.
examples.ja: この町に引っ越してきて以来、近所の人たちにはずっと助けられている。

records.formation: Vて形 + 以来; N + 以来
records.meaning: ever since …
records.nuance: Somewhat formal: marks a past starting point and a situation that has continued up to now. The main clause is an ongoing state or habit, not a single event, and the starting point is not very recent.

relatedReferences.text: 〜てから: simple 'after'; 以来 implies continuation to the present
〜てからというもの: emotional, a big change since that point
〜以降: 'from … onward', can also point to the future

similar: 〜てから: simple 'after'; 以来 implies continuation to the present
〜てからというもの: emotional, a big change since that point
〜以降: 'from … onward', can also point to the future

examples.en: This scholarship is open to all international students, regardless of nationality.
examples.ja: この奨学金は、国籍によらず、すべての留学生が応募できる。

examples.en: The owner of that shop may not look it, but he is fit enough to run full marathons on weekends.
examples.ja: あの店の主人は見かけによらず、週末にはフルマラソンを走るほどの体力の持ち主だ。

examples.en: Whatever it is, taking the first step is always the hardest part.
examples.ja: 何事によらず、最初の一歩を踏み出すのがいちばん難しい。

records.formation: N + によらず
records.meaning: regardless of …; irrespective of …
records.nuance: Formal, common in policies, recruitment and official notices (年齢によらず, 国籍によらず). Also appears in set phrases: 見かけによらず ('contrary to appearances') and 何事によらず ('whatever it may be').

relatedReferences.text: 〜にかかわらず: regardless of, often with paired opposites (晴雨にかかわらず) or degree words
〜を問わず: regardless of, usually with categories (男女を問わず)
〜もかまわず: heedless of, describing someone's behaviour ignoring something

similar: 〜にかかわらず: regardless of, often with paired opposites (晴雨にかかわらず) or degree words
〜を問わず: regardless of, usually with categories (男女を問わず)
〜もかまわず: heedless of, describing someone's behaviour ignoring something

examples.en: There's no way this much work is getting finished in one night.
examples.ja: こんな量の仕事、一晩で終わりっこないよ。

examples.en: I know there's no way I'll win the lottery, but I end up buying tickets anyway.
examples.ja: 宝くじなんて当たりっこないって分かってるけど、つい買っちゃうんだよね。

examples.en: Even if we run now, there's no way we'll make the last train.
examples.ja: 今から走ったって、終電に間に合いっこない。

records.formation: Vます形 + っこない
records.meaning: no way that …; there is no chance … (colloquial)
records.nuance: Casual spoken emphatic denial of possibility, often with potential or achievement verbs (できっこない, わかりっこない). Not used in formal writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜わけがない: same certainty, usable in more registers
〜はずがない: certainty based on logical reasoning
〜ようがない: there is no means or method of doing it

similar: 〜わけがない: same certainty, usable in more registers
〜はずがない: certainty based on logical reasoning
〜ようがない: there is no means or method of doing it

examples.en: The ceremony was solemnly conducted in accordance with long-standing tradition.
examples.ja: 式典は古くからの伝統にのっとって厳かに執り行われた。

examples.en: The personal information entrusted to us is properly managed in accordance with the law.
examples.ja: お預かりした個人情報は、法律にのっとって適切に管理しております。

examples.en: We pledge to compete fairly and squarely in the spirit of sportsmanship.
examples.ja: 我々はスポーツマンシップにのっとり、正々堂々と戦うことを誓います。

records.formation: N + にのっとって / にのっとり / にのっとった + N
records.meaning: in accordance with (rules, custom)
records.nuance: Formal. Means acting faithfully according to established laws, rules, traditions or procedures; typical of ceremonies, legal and official contexts.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に基づいて: 'based on' data or facts; broader
〜に沿って: 'in line with' a plan or wishes
〜に従って: 'following'; general and less formal

similar: 〜に基づいて: 'based on' data or facts; broader
〜に沿って: 'in line with' a plan or wishes
〜に従って: 'following'; general and less formal

examples.en: Whatever the reason, missing work without notice is not acceptable.
examples.ja: 理由が何であれ、無断で仕事を休むのは許されない。

examples.cloze: 大企業であれ中小企業であれ
examples.en: Whether at large companies or small ones, labor shortages have become a serious problem.
examples.ja: 大企業であれ中小企業であれ、人手不足は深刻な問題になっている。

examples.en: Even if it is a joke, you should refrain from remarks that mock someone's appearance.
examples.ja: たとえ冗談であれ、人の外見をからかうような発言は控えるべきだ。

records.formation: N + であれ / N1であれN2であれ / 疑問詞 + であれ（＝であろうと）
records.meaning: be it …; no matter what …; whether … or …
records.nuance: A literary way of saying that whatever the case, the conclusion stays the same; often paired with たとえ or a question word. The paired form lists two contrasting cases that are both covered.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にしろ〜にしろ／〜にせよ〜にせよ: same meaning, less stiff than であれ
〜を問わず: 'regardless of', attaches to category nouns such as 年齢 or 経験
〜であろうと: near-identical, slightly more emphatic

similar: 〜にしろ〜にしろ／〜にせよ〜にせよ: same meaning, less stiff than であれ
〜を問わず: 'regardless of', attaches to category nouns such as 年齢 or 経験
〜であろうと: near-identical, slightly more emphatic

audit.why: ようにも does not require repetition of the same verb: a clause explaining the obstacle is also possible, as in 連絡しようにも電話番号が分からない.

examples.en: I left my wallet at home, so even if I want to buy lunch, I can't.

audit.why: ようにも does not require repetition of the same verb: a clause explaining the obstacle is also possible, as in 連絡しようにも電話番号が分からない.

examples.ja: 財布を家に忘れてきたので、昼ご飯を買おうにも買えない。

examples.cloze: 起きようにも起きられなかった
examples.en: I had a fever of 39 degrees, and even when I tried to get up, I couldn't.

audit.why: ようにも does not require repetition of the same verb: a clause explaining the obstacle is also possible, as in 連絡しようにも電話番号が分からない.

examples.ja: 熱が三十九度もあって、起きようにも起きられなかった。

examples.en: Deep in the mountains with no signal, we couldn't call for help even if we tried.

audit.why: ようにも does not require repetition of the same verb: a clause explaining the obstacle is also possible, as in 連絡しようにも電話番号が分からない.

examples.ja: 山奥で電波が届かず、助けを呼ぼうにも呼べない状況だった。

records.formation: V意向形 + にも + 可能形の否定など、実行できない事情を表す節（例: 買おうにも買えない）
records.meaning: even if one wants to …, one cannot
records.nuance: The speaker wants or tries to do something but outside circumstances make it impossible, often with a note of frustration. The same verb is often repeated; common in conversation and narrative.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ようがない: there is no means at all, without stressing the wish to act
〜たくても〜ない: plain 'even though I want to, I can't', more neutral
〜に〜ない: repeated verb (泣くに泣けない), a fixed set of expressions with a similar feel

similar: 〜ようがない: there is no means at all, without stressing the wish to act
〜たくても〜ない: plain 'even though I want to, I can't', more neutral
〜に〜ない: repeated verb (泣くに泣けない), a fixed set of expressions with a similar feel

examples.en: There is something truly moving about the young players' wholehearted play.
examples.ja: 若い選手たちのひたむきなプレーには、胸を打つものがある。

examples.en: Honestly, a two-hour commute every day is pretty tough.
examples.ja: 毎日二時間の通勤は、正直かなりつらいものがある。

examples.cloze: 物足りないものがある
examples.en: The pace of economic recovery still leaves something to be desired.
examples.ja: 経済の回復ペースには、まだ物足りないものがある。

records.formation: V辞書形 / い形容詞 / な形容詞語幹な + ものがある
records.meaning: there is something … about it; it is truly …
records.nuance: Expresses a strong impression or evaluation that the speaker feels from a situation, without stating it as plain fact. Common in reviews, essays and commentary; it often pairs with feeling words such as 胸を打つ, つらい or 物足りない.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ものだ: states a general truth or a deep feeling, not an impression of a specific thing
〜ところがある: 'has a side that is …', points to one aspect of a person's character
〜感じがする: 'feels like …', lighter and more casual impression

similar: 〜ものだ: states a general truth or a deep feeling, not an impression of a specific thing
〜ところがある: 'has a side that is …', points to one aspect of a person's character
〜感じがする: 'feels like …', lighter and more casual impression

examples.en: I can't decide whether to buy it until I've seen the real thing.
examples.ja: 実物を見てからでないと、購入するかどうか決められない。

examples.en: This medicine cannot be prescribed until you have been examined by a doctor.
examples.ja: この薬は、医師の診察を受けてからでないと処方してもらえません。

examples.en: I'm afraid I can't give you an answer on that until I've consulted my manager.
examples.ja: 上司に相談してからでないと、その件についてはお答えできかねます。

records.formation: Vて形 + からでないと / からでなければ + negative or difficult result
records.meaning: not until … has been done; unless … first
records.nuance: States a necessary precondition; the main clause says something cannot or will not happen (〜できない, 〜わからない). Common in instructions, policies and polite refusals.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ないことには: 'unless', also with nouns and adjectives, same negative main clause
〜て初めて: positive realisation after an experience
〜なければ: general negative conditional, no sense of sequence

similar: 〜ないことには: 'unless', also with nouns and adjectives, same negative main clause
〜て初めて: positive realisation after an experience
〜なければ: general negative conditional, no sense of sequence

examples.en: Though small, the room gets plenty of sunlight, so it's good enough for working from home.
examples.ja: 狭いながらも日当たりのいい部屋で、在宅勤務には十分だ。

examples.en: Even though I know it's bad for me, I end up eating ramen in the middle of the night.
examples.ja: 体に悪いと知りながらも、つい夜中にラーメンを食べてしまう。

examples.en: Although it is a young company, the firm is breaking into overseas markets with its own technology.
examples.ja: 新興企業ながらも、同社は独自の技術で海外市場に食い込んでいる。

records.formation: Vます形 / Aい / Na / N + ながらも
records.meaning: while …, nevertheless …; although
records.nuance: Concessive and more emphatic or written than ながら alone. Set phrases such as 狭いながらも, 知りながらも and 少しずつながらも are very common.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ながら (simultaneous): doing two actions at once, no concession
〜のに: conversational concession that carries dissatisfaction
〜つつも: more formal concession, verbs only

similar: 〜ながら (simultaneous): doing two actions at once, no concession
〜のに: conversational concession that carries dissatisfaction
〜つつも: more formal concession, verbs only

examples.en: Residents are sharply divided over the construction of the new airport.
examples.ja: 新しい空港の建設をめぐって、住民の意見は大きく分かれている。

examples.en: The siblings' dispute over the inheritance finally ended up in court.
examples.ja: 遺産をめぐる兄弟の争いは、ついに裁判にまで発展した。

examples.en: Debate over generative AI and copyright is heating up in countries around the world.
examples.ja: 生成AIと著作権の問題をめぐり、各国で議論が活発になっている。

records.formation: N + をめぐって / をめぐり / をめぐる + N
records.meaning: over …; concerning …; surrounding … (a dispute or debate)
records.nuance: Marks the issue around which several parties argue, compete or discuss. Common in news and formal writing; をめぐり is the stiffer written form.

relatedReferences.text: 〜について: neutral 'about', with no sense of conflict between parties
〜に関して: formal 'regarding', also neutral
〜を中心に: 'centred on', a focus rather than a contested issue

similar: 〜について: neutral 'about', with no sense of conflict between parties
〜に関して: formal 'regarding', also neutral
〜を中心に: 'centred on', a focus rather than a contested issue

examples.en: This event will be held as scheduled regardless of the weather.
examples.ja: このイベントは天候にかかわらず予定通り開催します。

examples.en: We welcome motivated applicants, whether or not they have experience.
examples.ja: 経験の有無にかかわらず、やる気のある方を歓迎します。

examples.cloze: するしないにかかわらず
examples.en: Whether or not you will attend, please reply by next week.
examples.ja: 参加するしないにかかわらず、来週までに返事をください。

records.formation: N + にかかわらず / V辞書形 + Vない形 + にかかわらず / Aい + Aくない + にかかわらず
records.meaning: irrespective of …; regardless of whether …
records.nuance: Formal and frequent in notices and policies. Attaches to words that contain variation (天候, 年齢, 有無, 好き嫌い) or to contrasting pairs, saying none of it changes the outcome.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にもかかわらず: 'despite'; concedes a fact rather than dismissing variation
〜を問わず: near-synonym, used with nouns only
〜に関係なく: conversational equivalent

similar: 〜にもかかわらず: 'despite'; concedes a fact rather than dismissing variation
〜を問わず: near-synonym, used with nouns only
〜に関係なく: conversational equivalent

examples.en: Soaking in an open-air bath from the morning and savoring the local sake is the height of luxury.
examples.ja: 朝から露天風呂に入って地酒を味わうなんて、贅沢の極みだ。

examples.en: Management's attitude of pinning the blame for the accident on frontline staff can only be called the height of irresponsibility.
examples.ja: 事故の責任を現場に押しつける経営陣の姿勢は、無責任の極みと言わざるを得ない。

examples.en: After three all-nighters in a row, the whole team had reached the point of utter exhaustion.
examples.ja: 三日連続の徹夜で、チーム全員が疲労の極みに達していた。

records.formation: N + の極み
records.meaning: the height of …; the ultimate in …
records.nuance: Formal and emphatic; says a state has reached its extreme. Works for praise (贅沢の極み, 感激の極み) and for criticism (無責任の極み), and also for physical states (疲労の極み).

relatedReferences.text: 〜の至り: mostly fixed, ceremonial expressions of the speaker's own feeling (光栄の至り)
〜極まりない / 〜極まる: attaches to Na-adjectives and is mostly critical (失礼極まりない)
〜の限り: 'to the limit of' (力の限り); effort or extent rather than a peak state

similar: 〜の至り: mostly fixed, ceremonial expressions of the speaker's own feeling (光栄の至り)
〜極まりない / 〜極まる: attaches to Na-adjectives and is mostly critical (失礼極まりない)
〜の限り: 'to the limit of' (力の限り); effort or extent rather than a peak state

examples.en: It is said that language is precisely what makes human beings human.
examples.ja: 言葉こそが、人間を人間たらしめているものだと言われる。

examples.en: What makes this shop a truly renowned one is its commitment to handwork, unchanged since its founding.
examples.ja: この店を名店たらしめているのは、創業以来変わらない手仕事へのこだわりだ。

examples.en: It was the many trials she faced that made her a true leader.
examples.ja: 数々の試練こそが、彼女を真のリーダーたらしめたのである。

records.formation: N1 を N2 + たらしめる (e.g. 人間を人間たらしめる)
records.meaning: to make (something) truly what it is; to make … into a true …
records.nuance: A highly literary, classical causative used in essays, criticism and philosophy to name the essential quality that makes something what it is. It is almost never heard in casual conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にする: plain 'make into', with no sense of essence
〜させる: the ordinary causative; たらしめる concerns identity and essential nature
〜たる: 'one who is …' (the state itself), whereas たらしめる means making something so

similar: 〜にする: plain 'make into', with no sense of essence
〜させる: the ordinary causative; たらしめる concerns identity and essential nature
〜たる: 'one who is …' (the state itself), whereas たらしめる means making something so

examples.en: I took medicine, but far from going down, my fever has gone up.
examples.ja: 薬を飲んだのに、熱は下がるどころか上がってきた。

examples.en: As a child, far from being able to swim, I couldn't even put my face in the water.
examples.ja: 子どもの頃は、泳ぐどころか水に顔をつけることさえできなかった。

examples.en: Far from falling, tourist numbers in that town have doubled over the past few years.
examples.ja: その町では観光客が減るどころか、ここ数年で倍に増えている。

records.formation: N / なA語幹 / V・いA普通形 + どころか
records.meaning: far from …; not only not A, but (the opposite) B
records.nuance: Flatly denies an expectation and states that reality is the opposite or goes far beyond it. Emphatic and emotional; common in conversation and essays.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ばかりか: 'not only A but also B', same direction
〜というより: softer correction of a description
〜どころではない: 'in no position to', circumstances rule something out

similar: 〜ばかりか: 'not only A but also B', same direction
〜というより: softer correction of a description
〜どころではない: 'in no position to', circumstances rule something out

examples.en: Is it really necessary to go so far as to borrow money to buy a luxury car?
examples.ja: 借金までして高級車を買う必要が、本当にあるのだろうか。

examples.en: The proposal I'd stayed up all night to finish was flatly rejected at the meeting.
examples.ja: 徹夜までして仕上げた企画書が、会議であっさり却下された。

examples.en: Camping out for three days for limited-edition sneakers — are they really worth going that far for?
examples.ja: 限定スニーカーのために三日も野宿するなんて、そこまでして欲しいものなのだろうか。

records.formation: N（借金・徹夜 などの動作名詞） / そこ + までして（Vて形 + まで も同義）
records.meaning: going so far as to …; even to the point of …
records.nuance: Highlights an extreme measure or sacrifice taken to achieve something. Often followed by doubt about whether it is worth it (〜必要があるのか, 〜たくない), or by disappointment that the effort went unrewarded.

relatedReferences.text: 〜てまで: same idea attached to a verb te-form (嘘をついてまで)
〜さえ: 'even'; stresses an extreme item without the sense of sacrifice
〜までもない: 'there is no need to go as far as' (言うまでもない); the effort is judged unnecessary, not made

similar: 〜てまで: same idea attached to a verb te-form (嘘をついてまで)
〜さえ: 'even'; stresses an extreme item without the sense of sacrifice
〜までもない: 'there is no need to go as far as' (言うまでもない); the effort is judged unnecessary, not made

examples.en: For forty years, the craftsman has worked in his studio without taking a single day off.
examples.ja: その職人は四十年間、一日も休むことなく工房に立ち続けてきた。

examples.en: The bill was passed by the Diet without being properly debated.
examples.ja: その法案は、十分に議論されることなく国会で可決された。

examples.en: I want you to keep taking on new challenges without being afraid of failure.
examples.ja: 失敗を恐れることなく、どんどん新しいことに挑戦してほしい。

records.formation: V辞書形 + ことなく
records.meaning: without doing …; without ever …
records.nuance: A formal, written equivalent of 〜ずに / 〜ないで, common in news and speeches. It often stresses that something one might expect did not happen (休むことなく, 迷うことなく).

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずに: everyday 'without doing', less emphatic
〜ないで: conversational 'without doing'
〜ことなしに: even more formal; often 'without X, Y is impossible'

similar: 〜ずに: everyday 'without doing', less emphatic
〜ないで: conversational 'without doing'
〜ことなしに: even more formal; often 'without X, Y is impossible'

examples.en: Some are saying the penalty is too harsh in light of past cases.
examples.ja: 今回の処分は、過去の事例に照らして重すぎるとの声が上がっている。

examples.en: Judged against the law, this contract is very likely to be void.
examples.ja: 法律に照らして判断すれば、この契約は無効になる可能性が高い。

examples.en: Even measured against my own experience, I just can't accept that explanation.
examples.ja: 自分の経験に照らしてみても、その説明にはどうも納得がいかない。

records.formation: N + に照らして / N + に照らすと / N + に照らし合わせて
records.meaning: in light of …; measured against …
records.nuance: Formal: judging something by holding it up against a standard such as laws, rules, precedents, experience or common sense. Frequent in legal, administrative and editorial writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に基づいて: using as a basis; に照らして compares against a standard in order to judge
〜に即して: conforming to facts or reality
〜から見て: plain 'from the viewpoint of', less formal

similar: 〜に基づいて: using as a basis; に照らして compares against a standard in order to judge
〜に即して: conforming to facts or reality
〜から見て: plain 'from the viewpoint of', less formal

examples.en: 'Food loss' refers to food that is thrown away even though it is still edible.
examples.ja: 「フードロス」とは、まだ食べられるのに捨てられてしまう食品のことだ。

examples.en: No one ever imagined that long-established shop would close.
examples.ja: あの老舗が閉店するとは、誰も想像していなかった。

examples.en: Who would have thought the tickets would sell out in a single night!
examples.ja: まさか一晩でチケットが完売するとは。

records.formation: N + とは（定義） / 普通形 + とは（驚き）
records.meaning: … means …; to think that …! (surprise)
records.nuance: Either introduces a definition in formal, explanatory style, or voices surprise or dismay at something unexpected, often leaving the rest of the sentence unsaid.

relatedReferences.text: 〜というのは: plainer, more conversational definition
〜なんて: casual surprise or disdain
〜って: colloquial topic marker for asking what something means

similar: 〜というのは: plainer, more conversational definition
〜なんて: casual surprise or disdain
〜って: colloquial topic marker for asking what something means

audit.why: The rate/distribution use of につき is also normal in spoken explanations; only the causal use is characteristically restricted to formal notices and similar contexts.

examples.en: We are closed today due to renovation work.

audit.why: The rate/distribution use of につき is also normal in spoken explanations; only the causal use is characteristically restricted to formal notices and similar contexts.

examples.ja: 本日は改装工事中につき、休業とさせていただきます。

examples.en: The participation fee is 3,000 yen per person, payable at the venue on the day.

audit.why: The rate/distribution use of につき is also normal in spoken explanations; only the causal use is characteristically restricted to formal notices and similar contexts.

examples.ja: 参加費は一人につき三千円で、当日会場でお支払いください。

examples.en: As the car park is full, please use a nearby paid car park.

audit.why: The rate/distribution use of につき is also normal in spoken explanations; only the causal use is characteristically restricted to formal notices and similar contexts.

examples.ja: 駐車場は満車につき、近隣の有料駐車場をご利用ください。

records.formation: N + につき
records.meaning: due to … (in notices); per …
records.nuance: The reason use is stiff and written, especially on signs and notices (工事中につき); the rate use (一人につき) also occurs in spoken explanations. The reason use is not normally used for personal explanations in conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜のため: general reason, neutral register
〜について: everyday 'about, concerning'; につき has this sense only in stiff formal writing (本件につき)
〜ごとに: 'every, each'; stresses repetition rather than a rate

similar: 〜のため: general reason, neutral register
〜について: everyday 'about, concerning'; につき has this sense only in stiff formal writing (本件につき)
〜ごとに: 'every, each'; stresses repetition rather than a rate

examples.cloze: 聞くなり自分で調べるなり
examples.en: If there is something you don't understand, either ask a senior colleague or look it up yourself.
examples.ja: わからないことがあれば、先輩に聞くなり自分で調べるなりしてください。

examples.cloze: 見るなり買い物に行くなり
examples.en: At least on weekends, why not refresh yourself by seeing a movie or going shopping?
examples.ja: 週末くらい、映画を見るなり買い物に行くなりして気分転換したらどう？

examples.en: Please be sure to notify us in advance of any absence, by email or by phone.
examples.ja: 欠席の連絡は、メールなり電話なりで必ず事前にお願いします。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + なり + N / V辞書形 + なり（＋する）
records.meaning: either … or …; … or … (suggesting options)
records.nuance: Offers example options and leaves the choice to the listener, typically in advice or instructions. Not used for past facts, and can sound blunt toward superiors.

relatedReferences.text: 〜か〜か: neutral choice between alternatives
〜やら〜やら: lists many things that happened, not options to choose from
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether … or …'; the outcome is the same either way

similar: 〜か〜か: neutral choice between alternatives
〜やら〜やら: lists many things that happened, not options to choose from
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether … or …'; the outcome is the same either way

examples.en: Ancient capitals such as Kyoto and Nara draw many tourists all year round.
examples.ja: 京都や奈良といった古都には、一年を通して多くの観光客が訪れる。

examples.en: It's wise to keep emergency food on hand in preparation for natural disasters such as earthquakes and typhoons.
examples.ja: 地震や台風といった自然災害に備えて、日頃から非常食を用意しておきたい。

examples.en: More and more young people now spend money on digital services such as video streaming and e-books.
examples.ja: 最近は、動画配信や電子書籍といったデジタルサービスにお金を使う若者が増えている。

records.formation: N1（や/、）N2 + といった + N3
records.meaning: such as … (listing)
records.nuance: Gives representative examples and then names the category they belong to. Neutral to formal; common in news, explanations and business writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜など: 'etc.', less formal and can end a list on its own
〜のような: 'like', examples by resemblance
〜をはじめ: 'starting with', puts a leading example first

similar: 〜など: 'etc.', less formal and can end a list on its own
〜のような: 'like', examples by resemblance
〜をはじめ: 'starting with', puts a leading example first

examples.cloze: 苦いだの魚は骨があるだの
examples.en: Our child keeps complaining that vegetables are bitter, that fish has bones and so on, and hardly eats anything.
examples.ja: うちの子は、野菜は苦いだの魚は骨があるだのと文句ばかり言って、なかなか食べない。

examples.cloze: 報告が遅いだの資料が見にくいだの
examples.en: The department head is fussy about details, complaining that reports are late, that documents are hard to read and so on.
examples.ja: 部長は、報告が遅いだの資料が見にくいだの、細かいことにうるさい。

examples.cloze: 手続きだの荷造りだの
examples.en: Before the move, what with paperwork, packing and so on, I had no time to rest.
examples.ja: 引っ越しの前は、手続きだの荷造りだので、ゆっくり休む暇もなかった。

records.formation: N / Na語幹 / V・Aい普通形 + だの + … + だの (〜だの〜だのと言う / 〜だの何だの)
records.meaning: … and … and so on (listing, often as complaints)
records.nuance: Conversational; lists examples, typically of what someone says, demands or complains about, with a critical or annoyed tone. Often followed by と言う, と文句を言う or うるさい.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とか〜とか: neutral casual listing without the annoyed tone
〜やら〜やら: lists many things, often stressing confusion or being overwhelmed
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether … or …', covering both cases rather than listing

similar: 〜とか〜とか: neutral casual listing without the annoyed tone
〜やら〜やら: lists many things, often stressing confusion or being overwhelmed
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether … or …', covering both cases rather than listing

examples.en: Surprisingly, Edo-period gold coins were found under the floor of the old house.
examples.ja: 驚いたことに、その古い民家の床下から江戸時代の小判が見つかった。

examples.en: Unfortunately, this year's fireworks festival was canceled because of the rain.
examples.ja: 残念なことに、雨のため今年の花火大会は中止になってしまった。

examples.en: To our delight, a small local diner was featured in a national magazine.
examples.ja: うれしいことに、地元の小さな食堂が全国誌で紹介された。

records.formation: Vた形 / イAい / ナAな + ことに
records.meaning: to (my / our) …; much to one's … (emotion stated first)
records.nuance: Puts the speaker's emotional reaction up front (驚いたことに, 残念なことに, うれしいことに) before stating the fact. Somewhat formal; frequent in news, essays and speeches.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ないことには: 'unless …', a condition, not an emotional lead-in
〜ことか: an exclamation at the end of the sentence, not a leading evaluation
〜ことにする: a decision ('decide to'), unrelated in meaning

similar: 〜ないことには: 'unless …', a condition, not an emotional lead-in
〜ことか: an exclamation at the end of the sentence, not a leading evaluation
〜ことにする: a decision ('decide to'), unrelated in meaning

examples.en: Drink-driving is conduct utterly unbecoming of a police officer.
examples.ja: 飲酒運転は、警察官としてあるまじき行為だ。

examples.en: Leaking patients' personal information to outsiders is utterly unacceptable for a healthcare worker.
examples.ja: 患者の個人情報を外部に漏らすなど、医療従事者にあるまじきことだ。

examples.en: However angry the boss was, that was something no boss should ever say to a subordinate.
examples.ja: いくら腹が立ったとはいえ、あれは上司が部下に言うまじき一言だった。

records.formation: Nに / Nとして + あるまじき + N ／ V辞書形 + まじき + N（する → すまじき）
records.meaning: unbecoming of …; that must not be done (by someone in that position)
records.nuance: Very formal and strongly critical; condemns conduct as unacceptable for someone in a given role. Most often appears as 〜にあるまじき + N (行為, 発言); with other verbs it is rarer and literary (言うまじき一言).

relatedReferences.text: 〜べからざる: general 'must not / cannot', not tied to a person's role
〜にふさわしくない: neutral 'unsuitable for', much milder
〜てはならない: modern formal prohibition

similar: 〜べからざる: general 'must not / cannot', not tied to a person's role
〜にふさわしくない: neutral 'unsuitable for', much milder
〜てはならない: modern formal prohibition

examples.en: I got my licence, but since I don't have a car I've never actually driven.
examples.ja: 免許は取ったものの、車がないので一度も運転していない。

examples.en: Although the economy is on a recovery trend, consumer spending is still sluggish.
examples.ja: 景気は回復傾向にあるものの、個人消費はまだ伸び悩んでいる。

examples.en: It may be spring, but mornings and evenings are still chilly.
examples.ja: 春とはいうものの、朝晩はまだ冷え込む日が続いている。

records.formation: 普通形（な形容詞語幹な・である / Nである）+ ものの；普通形 / N + とはいうものの
records.meaning: although …; even though … (and yet the expected result does not follow)
records.nuance: Admits a fact, then states a contrary or disappointing outcome. Written and formal in tone; とはいうものの means 'that said' and can also start a sentence.

relatedReferences.text: 〜けれども / 〜が: everyday 'but', neutral and more conversational
〜にもかかわらず: 'despite …', stronger surprise that the result runs against expectation
〜とはいえ: 'even so', close to とはいうものの and also written

similar: 〜けれども / 〜が: everyday 'but', neutral and more conversational
〜にもかかわらず: 'despite …', stronger surprise that the result runs against expectation
〜とはいえ: 'even so', close to とはいうものの and also written

examples.en: As we were entirely unaccustomed to this, we deeply apologise for the inconvenience caused.
examples.ja: 何分にも慣れないこととて、ご迷惑をおかけしましたことを深くお詫び申し上げます。

examples.en: As it was so sudden, please forgive us for not being able to welcome you properly.
examples.ja: 急なこととて、十分なおもてなしもできず失礼いたしました。

examples.en: Since it was a child who did it, could you possibly overlook it this once?
examples.ja: 子どものしたこととて、どうか大目に見ていただけないでしょうか。

records.formation: V普通形 / Vない形 + こととて ; Aな語幹 + な + こととて ; Nの + こととて
records.meaning: because …; since it is (the case that) … (formal excuse or apology)
records.nuance: An old-fashioned, formal causal used to offer a reason when apologising or asking for forgiveness. Found in letters, business apologies and polite speech; the main clause is often an apology or request for leniency.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ゆえ(に): formal 'because' with no apologetic nuance
〜ので: plain, everyday 'because'
〜ことだから: reason based on knowing someone's character (あの人のことだから)

similar: 〜ゆえ(に): formal 'because' with no apologetic nuance
〜ので: plain, everyday 'because'
〜ことだから: reason based on knowing someone's character (あの人のことだから)

examples.en: As you'd expect of a long-established inn, the care extends to the smallest details.
examples.ja: さすが老舗の旅館だけあって、細かいところまで心配りが行き届いている。

examples.en: As you'd expect from something ten years in development, this new engine has remarkably good fuel economy.
examples.ja: 十年かけて開発されただけあって、この新型エンジンは燃費が驚くほどいい。

examples.en: As you'd expect from a team that does running drills every morning, they keep going strong even late in the second half.
examples.ja: 毎朝走り込んでいるだけあって、あのチームは後半になっても足が止まらない。

records.formation: N / Naな / Aい / V普通形 + だけあって
records.meaning: as one would expect of …; befitting …
records.nuance: Positive evaluation: the result fits the status, effort or reputation just named, and the speaker is impressed. Often paired with さすが; rarely used for bad outcomes.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけに: 'all the more because' or 'as you would expect'; the result can be good or bad
〜だけのことはある: same praise, but placed at the end of the sentence
〜からこそ: stresses the reason itself without judging whether the result fits

similar: 〜だけに: 'all the more because' or 'as you would expect'; the result can be good or bad
〜だけのことはある: same praise, but placed at the end of the sentence
〜からこそ: stresses the reason itself without judging whether the result fits

examples.cloze: 迷惑なことこの上ない
examples.en: Construction noise that goes on late into the night is an enormous nuisance for local residents.
examples.ja: 深夜まで続く工事の騒音は、近隣住民にとって迷惑なことこの上ない。

examples.cloze: 不快なことこの上なかった
examples.en: Being made to wait in line for three hours in the rain was as unpleasant as it gets.
examples.ja: 雨の中、三時間も行列に並ばされたのは不快なことこの上なかった。

examples.cloze: 贅沢なことこの上ない
examples.en: Soaking in an open-air bath while gazing at Mount Fuji is the height of luxury.
examples.ja: 富士山を眺めながら露天風呂に浸かるのは、贅沢なことこの上ない。

records.formation: Aい + ことこの上ない ; Aな語幹 + なことこの上ない
records.meaning: extremely …; nothing could be more …
records.nuance: An emphatic, formal way to say a quality is at its absolute peak, used for both good and bad things. Typical of writing and stiff speech; it often voices strong feeling with a touch of exaggeration.

relatedReferences.text: 〜極まりない / 〜極まる: similar 'utterly', mostly for negative Aな words (失礼極まりない)
〜限りだ: expresses the speaker's own emotion (うれしい限りだ), not an objective quality
〜の極み: 'the height of' with nouns (贅沢の極み)

similar: 〜極まりない / 〜極まる: similar 'utterly', mostly for negative Aな words (失礼極まりない)
〜限りだ: expresses the speaker's own emotion (うれしい限りだ), not an objective quality
〜の極み: 'the height of' with nouns (贅沢の極み)

examples.en: I thought it would be sunny all day, but in the afternoon we were hit by a violent thunderstorm.
examples.ja: 今日は一日晴れると思いきや、午後から激しい雷雨に見舞われた。

examples.en: I thought it would be an easy exam, but the last question turned out to be fiendishly hard.
examples.ja: 簡単な試験だと思いきや、最後の問題がとんでもない難問だった。

examples.en: Just when I thought work was finally over, my boss asked me to prepare some additional documents.
examples.ja: やっと仕事が終わったと思いきや、上司から追加の資料作りを頼まれた。

records.formation: 普通形 + と思いきや
records.meaning: I thought …, but (unexpectedly) …
records.nuance: Slightly literary but common in magazines, blogs and TV narration. Sets up an expectation and then reveals a surprising outcome; the result is often comic or ironic.

relatedReferences.text: 〜と思ったら: conversational; also used for 'as soon as'
〜かと思うと: 'no sooner … than'; focuses on quick succession
〜にもかかわらず: 'despite'; objective contrast without the speaker's mistaken expectation

similar: 〜と思ったら: conversational; also used for 'as soon as'
〜かと思うと: 'no sooner … than'; focuses on quick succession
〜にもかかわらず: 'despite'; objective contrast without the speaker's mistaken expectation

examples.en: Reports should avoid speculation and be written in line with the facts.
examples.ja: 報告書は推測を避け、事実に即して書くべきだ。

examples.en: It was decided to review the number of bus services in line with the actual situation in the area.
examples.ja: 地域の実情に即して、バスの運行本数を見直すことになった。

examples.en: You learn more by practicing conversation geared to real situations than by memorizing textbook example sentences.
examples.ja: 教科書の例文を丸暗記するより、実際の場面に即して会話を練習したほうが身につく。

records.formation: N + に即して / N + に即した + N
records.meaning: in line with …; in keeping with (the facts, reality, actual conditions)
records.nuance: Formal: acting or judging in close conformity with facts, reality or actual circumstances (事実, 実情, 現状, 実態). When the standard is a rule or law, the same reading is often written 則して.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に沿って: following a plan, policy or wishes
〜に基づいて: using something (data, evidence) as the foundation
〜に応じて: adjusting according to changing conditions

similar: 〜に沿って: following a plan, policy or wishes
〜に基づいて: using something (data, evidence) as the foundation
〜に応じて: adjusting according to changing conditions

examples.en: Cashless payments are rapidly spreading, even in rural areas.
examples.ja: 地方でも、キャッシュレス決済が急速に広がりつつある。

examples.en: Thanks to the development of new drugs, even diseases once thought incurable are being overcome.
examples.ja: 新薬の開発によって、かつては不治とされた病気も克服されつつある。

examples.en: Although the town's population is recovering, young people are still moving away.
examples.ja: 町の人口は回復しつつあるものの、若い世代の流出は依然として続いている。

records.formation: Vます形 + つつある
records.meaning: is in the process of …ing; is gradually …
records.nuance: Formal and typical of news and reports: a gradual change is under way toward a result, usually with change verbs (増える, 変わる). Not used for simple ongoing actions like eating.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ている: general progressive or resulting state; つつある stresses gradual change in progress
〜てきている: change up to now, more conversational
〜一方だ: change keeps moving in one direction, often a bad one

similar: 〜ている: general progressive or resulting state; つつある stresses gradual change in progress
〜てきている: change up to now, more conversational
〜一方だ: change keeps moving in one direction, often a bad one

examples.en: No matter what anyone says, I intend to follow the path I've chosen.
examples.ja: 誰に何を言われようと、自分の決めた道を進むつもりだ。

examples.en: However expensive it is, if you really want it, it's worth buying.
examples.ja: どんなに高かろうが、本当に欲しいものなら買う価値はある。

examples.en: Even the company president has to follow the rules.
examples.ja: たとえ社長であろうと、ルールは守ってもらわなければ困る。

records.formation: V意向形 + が / と; イA → 〜かろうが / かろうと; ナA・N → 〜だろうが / であろうと; often with どんなに・何を・誰が
records.meaning: no matter how / what / whether …; even if …
records.nuance: Says the outcome or the speaker's stance will not change whatever happens. Strong and somewhat defiant, used in both speech and writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ても: 'even if', plain and neutral
〜にしても / 〜にせよ: 'even if', more measured and less defiant
〜ようが〜まいが: covers both alternatives, 'whether or not'

similar: 〜ても: 'even if', plain and neutral
〜にしても / 〜にせよ: 'even if', more measured and less defiant
〜ようが〜まいが: covers both alternatives, 'whether or not'

examples.en: It is hard to believe that a cabinet minister, of all people, would make such a gaffe at a press conference.
examples.ja: 大臣ともあろう人が、記者会見でこんな失言をするとは信じられない。

examples.en: For a top-class hotel, of all places, to keep a guest waiting a whole hour over a booking mix-up is unthinkable.
examples.ja: 一流ホテルともあろうものが、予約の手違いで客を一時間も待たせるなんて。

examples.en: For a teacher, of all people, to lie brazenly in front of students is something that must never happen.
examples.ja: 教師ともあろう者が、生徒の前で平気でうそをつくなど、あってはならないことだ。

records.formation: N（地位・立場）+ ともあろう + 人／者／もの + が
records.meaning: someone of (high) standing like …; for a … of all people
records.nuance: Formal and critical. Stresses a person's or organisation's high status or responsibility to condemn behaviour unworthy of it; usually followed by an expression of disbelief or reproach.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ともなると: 'once one reaches the level of'; states a natural consequence, not criticism
〜にあるまじき: 'unbecoming of'; describes the act itself as inappropriate
〜くせに: casual, contemptuous 'even though'; no emphasis on rank

similar: 〜ともなると: 'once one reaches the level of'; states a natural consequence, not criticism
〜にあるまじき: 'unbecoming of'; describes the act itself as inappropriate
〜くせに: casual, contemptuous 'even though'; no emphasis on rank

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ずにはいられない (笑わない → 笑わずにはいられない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.cloze: 願わずにはいられない
examples.en: Every time I see footage of the disaster area, I can't help hoping for a swift recovery.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ずにはいられない (笑わない → 笑わずにはいられない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: 被災地の映像を見るたびに、一日も早い復興を願わずにはいられない。

examples.cloze: 笑わずにはいられなかった
examples.en: The excuse was so ridiculous that I couldn't help laughing.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ずにはいられない (笑わない → 笑わずにはいられない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: あまりにもばかばかしい言い訳に、笑わずにはいられなかった。

examples.cloze: 買わずにはいられない
examples.en: I have a real weakness for sweets, so whenever I spot a new dessert I just can't resist buying it.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ずにはいられない (笑わない → 笑わずにはいられない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: 甘いものに目がないので、新作のスイーツを見かけると買わずにはいられない。

records.formation: Vない形から「ない」を除く + ずにはいられない（する→せずにはいられない）
records.meaning: cannot help but …; cannot stop oneself from …
records.nuance: Expresses an irresistible emotional or physical urge felt by the speaker. Slightly formal; in speech 〜ないではいられない or 〜ずにいられない are also heard.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ざるを得ない: forced by circumstances, not an inner impulse
〜てならない: a feeling that wells up (心配でならない); describes a state rather than an action
〜ないではいられない: same meaning, slightly more colloquial

similar: 〜ざるを得ない: forced by circumstances, not an inner impulse
〜てならない: a feeling that wells up (心配でならない); describes a state rather than an action
〜ないではいられない: same meaning, slightly more colloquial

examples.en: The line, suspended because of heavy snow, resumed service for the first time in five days.
examples.ja: 大雪の影響で運休していた路線が、五日ぶりに運転を再開した。

examples.en: This winter has been so severe that, reportedly, it is the first time in thirty years the lake has frozen over completely.
examples.ja: 今年の冬は寒さが厳しく、湖が全面結氷したのは三十年ぶりのことだという。

examples.en: Even the managers are impressed by the newcomer's assured way of working; you would never guess they were new.
examples.ja: 新人とは思えない堂々とした仕事ぶりに、上司たちも感心している。

records.formation: 期間 + ぶり(に/の) / N・Vます形 + ぶり
records.meaning: for the first time in (a period); manner or way of …
records.nuance: After a time span it marks a long gap before something happens again (三年ぶりに, 久しぶり). After a noun or verb stem it describes how someone does something (仕事ぶり, 話しぶり), usually with an evaluation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜後: plain 'after', without the sense of a long interval
〜方: neutral 'way of doing' (method); ぶり describes an observed style
〜ようす: general appearance or state, not a manner of acting

similar: 〜後: plain 'after', without the sense of a long interval
〜方: neutral 'way of doing' (method); ぶり describes an observed style
〜ようす: general appearance or state, not a manner of acting

examples.en: Speaking of Kyoto, the autumn leaves are surely the top attraction.
examples.ja: 京都といえば、やはり秋の紅葉が一番の見どころだろう。

examples.en: When it comes to the classic sights of a Japanese summer, many people think of fireworks festivals.
examples.ja: 日本の夏の風物詩というと、花火大会を思い浮かべる人が多い。

examples.en: When it comes to weekend mornings, it's got to be freshly baked bread and coffee.
examples.ja: 週末の朝といったら、やっぱり焼きたてのパンとコーヒーでしょう。

records.formation: N / 普通形 + というと／といえば／といったら
records.meaning: speaking of …; when it comes to …
records.nuance: Raises a topic and brings up the first thing it calls to mind; というと can also check what the other person means ('X — you mean …?'). といえば is the most common; といったら is more conversational and often emotional.
records.pattern: 〜というと／〜といえば／〜といったら

relatedReferences.text: 〜について: neutral 'about', no associative leap
〜といったらない: 'indescribably …', emphasises degree rather than raising a topic
〜にかけては: 'when it comes to' a skill, used to praise ability

similar: 〜について: neutral 'about', no associative leap
〜といったらない: 'indescribably …', emphasises degree rather than raising a topic
〜にかけては: 'when it comes to' a skill, used to praise ability

examples.cloze: 留守なのをいいことに
examples.en: Taking advantage of their parents being away, the children played games until late at night.
examples.ja: 親が留守なのをいいことに、子どもたちは夜遅くまでゲームをしていた。

examples.cloze: 言わないのをいいことに
examples.en: Since the boss never says anything, he takes advantage and comes in late almost every day.
examples.ja: 上司が何も言わないのをいいことに、彼は毎日のように遅刻している。

examples.en: Unscrupulous sales tactics that exploit people's ignorance to push expensive contracts have become a problem.
examples.ja: 相手の無知をいいことに、高額な契約を結ばせる悪質な商法が問題になっている。

records.formation: N + をいいことに; V・イA普通形 / ナA・N + な + の + をいいことに
records.meaning: taking (unfair) advantage of …
records.nuance: Criticises someone for exploiting a circumstance to do something they should not. Always carries the speaker's disapproval; used in speech and news.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に乗じて: 'seizing the chance of', more formal and focused on opportunity, not necessarily blamed
〜を利用して: 'using', neutral and without built-in criticism
〜をよそに: 'ignoring', disregard of others' concern rather than exploitation

similar: 〜に乗じて: 'seizing the chance of', more formal and focused on opportunity, not necessarily blamed
〜を利用して: 'using', neutral and without built-in criticism
〜をよそに: 'ignoring', disregard of others' concern rather than exploitation

examples.en: Compared with last year's brutal heat, this summer has been much more comfortable.
examples.ja: 去年の猛暑にひきかえ、今年の夏はずいぶん過ごしやすい。

examples.cloze: 几帳面なのにひきかえ
examples.en: Whereas the older brother is meticulous, the younger one barely even tidies his room.
examples.ja: 兄が几帳面なのにひきかえ、弟は部屋の片付けもろくにしない。

examples.cloze: にぎわっているのにひきかえ
examples.en: Whereas shopping centers in central Tokyo are packed day after day, regional shopping streets are mostly rows of shuttered stores.
examples.ja: 都心の商業施設が連日にぎわっているのにひきかえ、地方の商店街はシャッターを下ろした店ばかりだ。

records.formation: N + にひきかえ / 普通形(なA・N + な) + の + にひきかえ
records.meaning: in contrast to …; whereas …
records.nuance: Sets two things side by side and contrasts them with a clear value judgment, one seen as better and one as worse. It often carries the speaker's dissatisfaction or surprise; slightly literary but common in conversation and columns.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に対して: neutral, objective contrast with no evaluation
〜とは裏腹に: contrary to appearances, words or expectations
〜反面: two opposite sides of the same thing, not two different things

similar: 〜に対して: neutral, objective contrast with no evaluation
〜とは裏腹に: contrary to appearances, words or expectations
〜反面: two opposite sides of the same thing, not two different things

examples.en: To mark the opening of our new store, we have prepared a limited menu using local ingredients.
examples.ja: 新店舗のオープンにあたって、地元の食材を使った限定メニューを用意しました。

examples.en: When starting to work abroad, it is important first to learn the local way of life.
examples.ja: 海外で働くにあたって、まず現地の生活習慣を学ぶことが大切だ。

examples.en: In preparing to submit the bill, the government widely sought the views of experts.
examples.ja: 法案の提出にあたり、政府は専門家の意見を広く募った。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + にあたって（にあたり）
records.meaning: on the occasion of …; when embarking on …
records.nuance: Formal; used for significant, one-off undertakings such as an opening, a launch or a move abroad, in speeches, notices and business writing. Not used for routine actions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に際して: near-synonym, slightly stiffer and more neutral
〜に先立って: 'prior to'; stresses a step taken beforehand, not the occasion itself
〜ときに: plain 'when', for any situation

similar: 〜に際して: near-synonym, slightly stiffer and more neutral
〜に先立って: 'prior to'; stresses a step taken beforehand, not the occasion itself
〜ときに: plain 'when', for any situation

examples.en: As far as I know, this shop has been in business in the same spot since the early Showa era.
examples.ja: 私の知る限りでは、この店は昭和の初めからずっと同じ場所で営業している。

examples.en: As far as we have been able to find, no similar accident has been reported before.
examples.ja: 調べた限りでは、同じような事故は過去に報告されていない。

examples.en: Judging from this poll's results, the new policy seems to be broadly supported.
examples.ja: 今回の世論調査の結果を見る限りでは、新しい政策はおおむね支持されているようだ。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 / Vている + 限りでは / Nの + 限りでは
records.meaning: as far as … goes; to the extent that …
records.nuance: Limits a statement to what the speaker knows, has seen or has checked, hedging the claim. Typically with 知る, 見る, 聞く, 調べる; common in reports and careful conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜限り: 'as long as', a lasting condition rather than a limit on knowledge
〜によると: 'according to', citing a source without hedging one's own knowledge
〜範囲では: 'within the range of', a more literal statement of scope

similar: 〜限り: 'as long as', a lasting condition rather than a limit on knowledge
〜によると: 'according to', citing a source without hedging one's own knowledge
〜範囲では: 'within the range of', a more literal statement of scope

examples.en: Without the cooperation of local residents, this festival could never have succeeded.
examples.ja: 地域住民の協力なくして、この祭りの成功はありえなかった。

examples.en: Without steady daily effort, no talent will ever blossom.
examples.ja: 日々の地道な努力なくしては、どんな才能も花開くことはない。

examples.en: Without trust among its members, a team cannot hope to achieve results.
examples.ja: メンバー同士の信頼関係なくして、チームとしての成果は望めない。

records.formation: N + なくして（は）+ 否定・不可能の表現
records.meaning: without … (something cannot happen)
records.nuance: Formal, common in speeches and editorials. Names something essential and states that the result would be impossible without it, often to express gratitude or stress necessity.

relatedReferences.text: 〜なしには: near-synonym, slightly less formal
〜抜きで（は）: 'leaving out'; can be neutral and does not always imply impossibility
〜がなければ: plain conditional 'if there were no'

similar: 〜なしには: near-synonym, slightly less formal
〜抜きで（は）: 'leaving out'; can be neutral and does not always imply impossibility
〜がなければ: plain conditional 'if there were no'

examples.en: Let's skip the formal speeches and get straight to the toast.
examples.ja: 堅い挨拶は抜きにして、さっそく乾杯しましょう。

examples.cloze: 観光業を抜きにしては
examples.en: You can't talk about this island's economy without tourism.
examples.ja: 観光業を抜きにしては、この島の経済は語れない。

examples.en: Setting profit and loss aside, I want to think about what I can do for the community.
examples.ja: 損得を抜きにして、地域のために何ができるかを考えたい。

records.formation: Nを / Nは + 抜きにして / N + 抜きで / Nを抜きにしては〜ない
records.meaning: leaving … out; without …; setting … aside
records.nuance: Removes something that would normally be included (formalities, jokes, self-interest). The form 〜を抜きにしては…ない stresses that something is indispensable; neutral register, common in conversation and commentary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜を除いて: 'except for', removing an exception from a set; 抜きにして drops an element from an activity
〜はさておき: 'leaving … aside for now', postponing a topic rather than omitting it
〜なしには: 'without … (something cannot happen)', close to 抜きにしては but more formal

similar: 〜を除いて: 'except for', removing an exception from a set; 抜きにして drops an element from an activity
〜はさておき: 'leaving … aside for now', postponing a topic rather than omitting it
〜なしには: 'without … (something cannot happen)', close to 抜きにしては but more formal

examples.en: A row of cherry trees runs along the river, and in spring it is busy with crowds of blossom viewers.
examples.ja: 川に沿って桜並木が続き、春には多くの花見客でにぎわう。

examples.en: In line with company policy, it has been decided to increase the number of work-from-home days from next fiscal year.
examples.ja: 会社の方針に沿って、来年度から在宅勤務の日数を増やすことになった。

examples.en: A member of our staff will propose a plan that matches your wishes.
examples.ja: お客様のご要望に沿ったプランを、担当者がご提案いたします。

records.formation: N + に沿って / に沿い / に沿うN / に沿ったN
records.meaning: along …; in line with …
records.nuance: Physically, follows the line of a road, river or coast; abstractly, acts in accordance with a plan, policy, manual or someone's wishes. Neutral to formal; に沿ったN is common in business and service language.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に基づいて: grounded in data or rules as a basis, not following a line or direction
〜に従って: obeying instructions or rules; also proportional 'as …'
〜を通って: passing through a place, not running alongside it

similar: 〜に基づいて: grounded in data or rules as a basis, not following a line or direction
〜に従って: obeying instructions or rules; also proportional 'as …'
〜を通って: passing through a place, not running alongside it

examples.cloze: 公言してはばからない
examples.en: The director openly declares that his new film is the best movie of the year.
examples.ja: その監督は、自分の新作こそ今年最高の映画だと公言してはばからない。

examples.en: The new president does not hesitate to say that he puts employees' happiness ahead of profit.
examples.ja: 新社長は、利益よりも社員の幸せを優先すると言ってはばからない。

examples.cloze: 口にしてはばからない
examples.en: Some politicians think nothing of quoting baseless figures as if they were facts.
examples.ja: 一部の政治家は、根拠のない数字をまるで事実であるかのように口にしてはばからない。

records.formation: Vて形 + はばからない（言う・公言する・主張する 等）
records.meaning: not hesitate to …; unabashedly …
records.nuance: Describes someone who says or does something openly, without the restraint others would show. Mostly used in writing about a third person, often with a hint of disapproval or surprise at their boldness.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をためらわない: 'not hesitate to', neutral and can be positive
〜てやまない: a sincere, continuing feeling such as hope; はばからない is about saying things boldly
〜を恐れず: 'without fear of', praises courage

similar: 〜をためらわない: 'not hesitate to', neutral and can be positive
〜てやまない: a sincere, continuing feeling such as hope; はばからない is about saying things boldly
〜を恐れず: 'without fear of', praises courage

audit.why: ながら also links activities over a long period, as in 働きながら大学に通う; restricting it to actions at the same moment creates a false contrast with かたわら.

examples.en: Alongside a day job at a company, the writer kept writing fiction every morning without fail.

audit.why: ながら also links activities over a long period, as in 働きながら大学に通う; restricting it to actions at the same moment creates a false contrast with かたわら.

examples.ja: その作家は、会社勤めのかたわら、毎朝欠かさず小説を書き続けた。

examples.en: Alongside her research at a university, she tutors local children for free.

audit.why: ながら also links activities over a long period, as in 働きながら大学に通う; restricting it to actions at the same moment creates a false contrast with かたわら.

examples.ja: 彼女は大学で研究を続けるかたわら、地域の子どもたちに無料で勉強を教えている。

examples.en: More and more people are running cafés in renovated old houses while also working as farmers.

audit.why: ながら also links activities over a long period, as in 働きながら大学に通う; restricting it to actions at the same moment creates a false contrast with かたわら.

examples.ja: 農業を営むかたわら、古民家を改装したカフェを経営する人が増えている。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Nの + かたわら
records.meaning: while also …; alongside (one's main work) …
records.nuance: Someone pursues a second activity alongside their main occupation over a long period. Written and slightly literary, common in profiles and biographies; it also has the literal sense 'beside'.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ながら: two activities in parallel, either at a particular moment or over a longer period (働きながら大学に通う); everyday register
〜一方(で): contrasting two aspects or activities, not necessarily main versus side
〜かたがた: one action serving two purposes on a single occasion

similar: 〜ながら: two activities in parallel, either at a particular moment or over a longer period (働きながら大学に通う); everyday register
〜一方(で): contrasting two aspects or activities, not necessarily main versus side
〜かたがた: one action serving two purposes on a single occasion

examples.en: Heavy snow is possible in the Kanto region from tonight through tomorrow morning.
examples.ja: 今夜から明日の朝にかけて、関東地方では大雪のおそれがあります。

examples.en: This flower blooms across the whole mountainside from spring through early summer.
examples.ja: この花は春から初夏にかけて、山の斜面一面に咲く。

examples.en: Pain running from the neck to the shoulders may be caused by long hours of desk work.
examples.ja: 首から肩にかけての痛みは、長時間のデスクワークが原因かもしれない。

records.formation: （N1 + から）+ N2 + にかけて
records.meaning: (from …) through …; over a span of time or area
records.nuance: Marks a range with fuzzy edges and is a staple of weather forecasts, news and seasonal writing. Unlike まで, it does not pin down an exact end point.

relatedReferences.text: 〜から〜まで: exact start and end points
〜にわたって: stresses that the whole span is covered, often a long one
〜にかけては: 'when it comes to' a skill, a different pattern

similar: 〜から〜まで: exact start and end points
〜にわたって: stresses that the whole span is covered, often a long one
〜にかけては: 'when it comes to' a skill, a different pattern

examples.en: We are open every day except over the New Year holidays.
examples.ja: 当店は年末年始を除いて、毎日営業しております。

examples.en: Apart from some areas, it will be sunny across the country.
examples.ja: 一部の地域を除いて、全国的に晴れるでしょう。

examples.en: Apart from this problem, the plan is progressing largely on schedule.
examples.ja: この問題を除けば、計画はおおむね順調に進んでいる。

records.formation: N + を除いて / N + を除けば / N + を除く + N
records.meaning: except for …; excluding …
records.nuance: Takes one item out of a set and says the statement holds for the rest. Somewhat formal; typical of notices, forecasts and reports.

relatedReferences.text: 〜以外: neutral 'other than', usable in any register
〜はさておき: setting a topic aside for now, not excluding it from a group
〜を別にして: 'leaving … aside', often a matter to be dealt with separately

similar: 〜以外: neutral 'other than', usable in any register
