examples.en: Because of the typhoon, power outages occurred over a wide area of the Kanto region.
examples.ja: 台風の影響で、関東地方の広い範囲にわたって停電が発生した。

examples.en: The team of experts has spent three years carrying out interviews on site.
examples.ja: 専門家チームは、三年にわたって現地で聞き取り調査を続けてきた。

examples.en: After an operation lasting ten hours, the patient safely regained consciousness.
examples.ja: 十時間にわたる手術の末、患者は無事に意識を取り戻した。

records.formation: N（期間・範囲・回数）+ にわたって / にわたり / にわたるN
records.meaning: spanning …; over (a whole period, area or number of times)
records.nuance: Emphasizes that something extends across the entire stretch of a period, area or series; formal and very common in news reports. The noun usually signals scale (三年, 広い範囲, 数回).

relatedReferences.text: 〜を通じて／通して: 'throughout' a period, with no sense of covering a large extent; also means 'via'
〜にかけて: a loose range, usually 〜から〜にかけて (夜から朝にかけて)
〜中（じゅう）: casual 'all through' (一年中), without the formal sense of scale

similar: 〜を通じて／通して: 'throughout' a period, with no sense of covering a large extent; also means 'via'
〜にかけて: a loose range, usually 〜から〜にかけて (夜から朝にかけて)
〜中（じゅう）: casual 'all through' (一年中), without the formal sense of scale

examples.en: The man finished a full marathon for the first time at the age of sixty.
examples.ja: その男性は六十歳にして初めてフルマラソンを完走した。

examples.en: AI detected signs of disease that even a veteran specialist had failed to spot.
examples.ja: ベテランの専門医にして見抜けなかった病気の兆候を、AIが見つけ出した。

examples.en: The author of this book is both a novelist and a painter, and painted the cover art personally.
examples.ja: この本の著者は小説家にして画家でもあり、表紙の絵も自ら手がけている。

records.formation: N + にして
records.meaning: only at …; even …; both … and …
records.nuance: Formal and written. After an age or stage: 'only at that point' (often with 初めて / ようやく); after a highly capable person: 'even X'; between two roles: 'X and also Y'.

relatedReferences.text: 〜で初めて: plain 'not until'
〜でさえ: 'even'; neutral emphasis without the formal tone
〜であると同時に: plain 'at the same time as being'

similar: 〜で初めて: plain 'not until'
〜でさえ: 'even'; neutral emphasis without the formal tone
〜であると同時に: plain 'at the same time as being'

examples.en: With the typhoon approaching, there is a risk of heavy rain in the Kanto region tomorrow as well.
examples.ja: 台風の接近に伴い、明日は関東地方でも大雨になる恐れがあります。

examples.en: If prices keep rising like this, spending by younger people may cool even further.
examples.ja: このまま値上げが続けば、若い世代の消費がさらに冷え込む恐れがある。

examples.en: Experts are urging caution, saying this app poses a risk of personal data leaks.
examples.ja: このアプリには個人情報流出の恐れがあるとして、専門家が注意を呼びかけている。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vない形 / Nの + 恐れがある
records.meaning: there is a risk of …; … may (unfortunately) happen
records.nuance: Points to the possibility of something bad happening, in a sober, objective tone. Typical of news, weather forecasts, official warnings and product notices; never used for good outcomes.

relatedReferences.text: 〜かねない: 'could well lead to', a speaker's judgment that something bad might result; 恐れがある sounds more official and objective
〜可能性がある: neutral 'there is a possibility', usable for good or bad outcomes
〜危険がある: 'there is a danger of', usually physical harm

similar: 〜かねない: 'could well lead to', a speaker's judgment that something bad might result; 恐れがある sounds more official and objective
〜可能性がある: neutral 'there is a possibility', usable for good or bad outcomes
〜危険がある: 'there is a danger of', usually physical harm

examples.en: Record-breaking heat hit major cities across the country, Tokyo first among them.
examples.ja: 東京をはじめ、全国の主要都市で記録的な猛暑となった。

examples.en: Our president and all of our staff look forward to welcoming you.

examples.en: Japanese food, including sushi and ramen, is very popular overseas too.
examples.ja: 寿司やラーメンをはじめとする日本食は、海外でも人気が高い。

records.formation: N + をはじめ(として) / をはじめとする + N
records.meaning: starting with …; … and others; including …
records.nuance: Names the most prominent or representative member of a group, then implies the rest. Formal and common in news, speeches and business greetings.

relatedReferences.text: 〜など: plain 'and so on', with no stress on a leading example
〜を中心に: 'centred on', describes a focus or core, not a representative
〜から〜まで: gives the full range from one end to the other

similar: 〜など: plain 'and so on', with no stress on a leading example
〜を中心に: 'centred on', describes a focus or core, not a representative
〜から〜まで: gives the full range from one end to the other

examples.en: The window has been smashed, so the culprit must have broken in here.
examples.ja: 窓ガラスが割られているから、犯人はここから侵入したに違いない。

examples.en: If people are lining up like this in the middle of a weekday, the ramen here must be exceptionally good.
examples.ja: 平日の昼間からこんなに行列ができているのだから、この店のラーメンはよほどおいしいに違いない。

examples.en: For the athletes who won the national championship, today will no doubt be a day they never forget.
examples.ja: 全国大会で優勝した選手たちにとって、今日は一生忘れられない一日になるに違いない。

records.formation: V普通形 / い形容詞普通形 / な形容詞語幹・N(である) + に違いない
records.meaning: must be …; there is no doubt that …
records.nuance: Expresses the speaker's strong conviction, based on evidence or intuition. Firmer and more written than だろう; な-adjectives and nouns attach directly without だ.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はずだ: logical expectation from facts or reasoning; に違いない is a more subjective, gut-level certainty
〜に相違ない: same meaning, stiffer and more formal written style
〜かもしれない: only a possibility, far weaker

similar: 〜はずだ: logical expectation from facts or reasoning; に違いない is a more subjective, gut-level certainty
〜に相違ない: same meaning, stiffer and more formal written style

records.formation: N / V普通形の + をきっかけに(して) / をきっかけとして（硬い: を契機に）
records.meaning: taking … as the occasion; triggered by …; since …
records.nuance: Marks the event that prompted a change or new start, often a personal turning point. Neutral in register; を契機に is the formal written equivalent seen in news and reports.

relatedReferences.text: 〜を機に: 'on the occasion of', often a planned milestone such as a birthday or retirement
〜がもとで: marks the cause of something, usually a bad result
〜以来: 'ever since', focuses on time passed, not the trigger

examples.en: The moment the new game went on sale, orders flooded the online store.

examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.
examples.ja: ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。

examples.en: As soon as they heard about the accident, the reporters all headed to the scene.
examples.ja: 事故の知らせを聞くや、記者たちは一斉に現場へ向かった。

records.formation: V辞書形 + や否や / や
records.meaning: the instant …; no sooner had … than …
records.nuance: Shows that a second event follows the first almost instantly. Written and formal, typical of news and narrative; the second clause describes what actually happened, never a request or intention, and the short form 〜や is even more literary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たとたん(に): 'just as', more conversational, often with an unexpected result

records.nuance: Formal, usually attributive: something is adequate or worthy enough to justify an action or judgment (信頼に足る, 尊敬に足る, 証明するに足る). The negative idiom 取るに足らない means 'trivial'.

examples.en: The child kept playing in the puddle without caring that their clothes were getting dirty.

examples.en: Someone was crying loudly on the station platform, heedless of who was watching.
examples.ja: 人目もかまわず、駅のホームで大声で泣いている人がいた。

examples.en: The neighbour plays music at full volume, without caring that it's the middle of the night.
examples.ja: 隣の住人は深夜なのもかまわず、大音量で音楽を流している。

records.formation: N + もかまわず; V・イA普通形 / ナA・N + な + の + もかまわず
records.meaning: heedless of …; without caring about …
records.nuance: Describes someone acting without regard for something they would normally worry about, such as other people's eyes, the weather or the hour. Often carries mild criticism or surprise from the speaker.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をよそに: 'paying no heed to', usually others' worries or opposition; more written

similar: 〜をよそに: 'paying no heed to', usually others' worries or opposition; more written

records.formation: N / Vます形 + がましい (恩着せがましい・言い訳がましい・押し付けがましい・差し出がましい)
records.meaning: smacking of …; coming across unpleasantly as … (disapproved)
records.nuance: Attaches to a limited set of words to say that someone's words or manner come across unpleasantly as that thing: excuse-making, favour-flaunting, pushy or clinging (言い訳がましい, 恩着せがましい, 押し付けがましい, 未練がましい). Almost always critical; 差し出がましいようですが is a set humble opener before giving advice.

relatedReferences.text: 〜じみる: looks or feels like something it should not be (子供じみた, 所帯じみた); about resemblance, not off-putting behaviour aimed at others

records.formation: N + からすると / からすれば / から見ると / から見れば

records.formation: N + を経て

examples.en: The defending champions showed the poise of true champions as they advanced to the final.

records.formation: N + たる + N (者 / もの / other nouns); typically 〜たる者、〜べきだ
records.meaning: as one who is …; one worthy of the name …
records.nuance: Formal and literary, used to state the duties or standards expected of someone in a given role. It sounds lofty and somewhat preachy, as in a code of conduct or an editorial.

relatedReferences.text: 〜として: neutral 'as …', with no lofty tone
〜である以上: 'since one is …', a logical premise for an obligation
〜にふさわしい: 'befitting …', describing suitability rather than duty

similar: 〜として: neutral 'as …', with no lofty tone
〜である以上: 'since one is …', a logical premise for an obligation
〜にふさわしい: 'befitting …', describing suitability rather than duty

examples.en: At the park entrance there is a sign that reads 'Keep off the grass.'
examples.ja: 公園の入り口には「芝生に立ち入るべからず」と書かれた看板が立っている。

examples.en: Water is indispensable to human life.
examples.ja: 水は人間の生活にとって欠くべからざるものだ。

examples.en: My grandfather often used to say, 'He who does not work shall not eat.'
examples.ja: 「働かざる者食うべからず」という言葉を、祖父はよく口にしていた。

records.formation: V辞書形 + べからず（文末） / V辞書形 + べからざる + N（する → すべからず・すべからざる）
records.meaning: must not …; should not … (attributive form before a noun: that must not / cannot be …)
records.nuance: Classical prohibition, seen today on signs, notices and in proverbs (立ち入るべからず). べからざる modifies a noun in set phrases such as 欠くべからざる ('indispensable') and 許すべからざる ('unforgivable').

relatedReferences.text: 〜べきではない: modern 'should not', advice rather than a prohibition
〜てはならない: modern formal prohibition
〜まじき: 'unbecoming of', tied to one's role (教師にあるまじき)

similar: 〜べきではない: modern 'should not', advice rather than a prohibition
〜てはならない: modern formal prohibition
〜まじき: 'unbecoming of', tied to one's role (教師にあるまじき)

examples.en: My son is absorbed in games every night, and now it has come to the point where he skips school.
examples.ja: 息子は毎晩ゲームに夢中で、ついには学校を休む始末だ。

examples.en: No matter how many times we warn our new hire, the lateness continues, and lately they don't even bother to let us know.
examples.ja: うちの新人は何度注意しても遅刻が直らず、最近では連絡すらよこさない始末だ。

examples.en: It started as a small mistake, but they told lie after lie to cover it up and in the end wound up leaving the company.
examples.ja: 最初は小さなミスだったのに、それを隠そうと嘘を重ね、最後には会社を辞める始末だった。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vない形 + 始末だ（この始末だ も可）
records.meaning: end up (in a deplorable state); it has come to the point of …
records.nuance: After a chain of bad developments, names the final unfortunate outcome with the speaker's exasperation or disapproval. Used in conversation and essays when complaining about someone's behaviour or a situation going downhill.

relatedReferences.text: 〜羽目になる: end up in a troublesome situation, often oneself, with regret rather than criticism
〜末（に）: after a long process, neutral about whether the result is good or bad
〜結果になる: neutral 'result in', with no emotional colouring

similar: 〜羽目になる: end up in a troublesome situation, often oneself, with regret rather than criticism
〜末（に）: after a long process, neutral about whether the result is good or bad
〜結果になる: neutral 'result in', with no emotional colouring

examples.en: In this film, the actors' powerful performances, combined with the beautiful visuals, deeply moved the audience.
examples.ja: この映画では、俳優たちの迫真の演技が美しい映像と相まって、観客を深く感動させた。

examples.en: The weak yen, coupled with more flights, pushed the number of foreign visitors this summer to a record high.
examples.ja: 円安が航空便の増便と相まって、今年の夏の訪日客数を過去最多に押し上げた。

examples.en: The relentless heat, combined with higher electricity rates, is weighing ever more heavily on household budgets.
examples.ja: 連日の猛暑が電気料金の値上げと相まって、家計の負担を一段と重くしている。

records.formation: N1がN2と相まって（とあいまって） / N1とN2が相まって
records.meaning: combined with …; coupled with …
records.nuance: Says that two factors combine and reinforce each other to produce a stronger effect. Typical of news, reviews and analytical writing; usually written 相まって.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とともに: 'together with', neutral, no sense of mutual reinforcement
〜に加えて: 'in addition to', simply adds one factor to another
〜も手伝って: 'partly helped by', presents one contributing factor

similar: 〜とともに: 'together with', neutral, no sense of mutual reinforcement
〜に加えて: 'in addition to', simply adds one factor to another
〜も手伝って: 'partly helped by', presents one contributing factor

examples.en: We've practised this hard, so there's no way we'll lose.
examples.ja: こんなに練習したんだから、負けるわけがない。

examples.en: Losing ten kilos in a month? A deal that good can't possibly be real.
examples.ja: 一か月で十キロもやせられるなんて、そんなうまい話があるわけがない。

examples.en: Working that much overtime every day can't possibly be good for your health.
examples.ja: 毎日あれだけ残業していて、体に悪くないわけがない。

records.formation: 普通形（な形容詞語幹な・である / Nの・である）+ わけがない / わけはない
records.meaning: there is no way that …; it cannot possibly be that …
records.nuance: A confident, subjective denial that something could be true or happen. Common in conversation; it sounds certain and can be emphatic or dismissive.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はずがない: denial based on reasoning or evidence, slightly more objective
〜わけではない: 'it is not that …', a partial denial, not an impossibility
〜ものか: emotional rhetorical denial, more forceful and spoken

similar: 〜はずがない: denial based on reasoning or evidence, slightly more objective
〜わけではない: 'it is not that …', a partial denial, not an impossibility
〜ものか: emotional rhetorical denial, more forceful and spoken

audit.why: よりむしろ can also reclassify or refine a description, so excluding that function creates a false contrast with というより.

examples.en: It's not so much cool today as downright cold.

audit.why: よりむしろ can also reclassify or refine a description, so excluding that function creates a false contrast with というより.

examples.ja: 今日は涼しいというより、むしろ寒いくらいだ。

examples.en: That shop has become less a restaurant than a place where locals gather.

audit.why: よりむしろ can also reclassify or refine a description, so excluding that function creates a false contrast with というより.

examples.ja: あの店は飲食店というより、地域の人が集まる居場所になっている。

examples.en: To me this film felt less like a horror movie than a poignant family story.

audit.why: よりむしろ can also reclassify or refine a description, so excluding that function creates a false contrast with というより.

examples.ja: この映画は、ホラーというより切ない家族の物語だと感じた。

records.formation: N / 普通形（なAだ・Nだ は「だ」を省略可） + というより（むしろ）
records.meaning: rather than …; more … than …
records.nuance: Corrects or refines a description: the second wording fits better than the first. Often paired with むしろ; common in both speech and writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜よりむしろ: also favours the second description or option; というより explicitly revises the first wording
〜どころか: 'far from A', reality is the opposite or much more
〜かわりに: 'instead of', substitution of one thing for another

similar: 〜よりむしろ: also favours the second description or option; というより explicitly revises the first wording
〜どころか: 'far from A', reality is the opposite or much more
〜かわりに: 'instead of', substitution of one thing for another

examples.en: Whenever I hear news about empty houses in the countryside, I worry about what will become of my hometown.
examples.ja: 地方の空き家問題のニュースを聞くにつけ、故郷の町の行く末が気にかかる。

examples.en: My boss says "things were better in the old days" at every turn, and honestly I'm sick of it.
examples.ja: うちの上司は何かにつけて「昔はよかった」と言うので、正直うんざりしている。

examples.cloze: 良きにつけ悪しきにつけ
examples.en: For better or for worse, social media has changed our lives enormously.
examples.ja: 良きにつけ悪しきにつけ、SNSは私たちの暮らしを大きく変えた。

records.formation: V辞書形 + につけ(て) / N + につけ(て)；AにつけBにつけ
records.meaning: whenever …; every time … (a feeling or memory arises); whether … or …
records.nuance: Attaches to verbs of perceiving or thinking (見る, 聞く, 思う) and is followed by a feeling or recollection that arises naturally; somewhat literary. Also survives in set phrases such as 何かにつけて (at every turn) and 良きにつけ悪しきにつけ (for better or worse).

relatedReferences.text: 〜たびに: neutral 'every time', any verb and any result; につけ is limited to perception/thought verbs plus a spontaneous emotion
〜ごとに: at each interval or unit (三日ごとに), mechanical repetition rather than a triggered feeling
AにしろBにしろ: 'whether A or B' for any pair; AにつけBにつけ is mostly fixed pairs like 良き/悪しき, 嬉しい/悲しい

similar: 〜たびに: neutral 'every time', any verb and any result; につけ is limited to perception/thought verbs plus a spontaneous emotion

examples.en: Judging from the footprints left at the scene, the culprit must have come in through the back door.
examples.ja: 現場に残された足跡から見て、犯人は裏口から侵入したに相違ない。

examples.en: This discovery will undoubtedly be a major clue to unraveling how the universe came to be.
examples.ja: この発見は、宇宙の成り立ちを解き明かす大きな手がかりになるに相違ない。

examples.en: Seeing that the lights are on late every night, that office must be extremely busy.
examples.ja: 毎晩遅くまで明かりがついているところを見ると、あの事務所はよほど忙しいに相違ない。

records.formation: 普通形（なA語幹・N は だ を付けない／である）+ に相違ない
records.meaning: without doubt …; must be … (formal)
records.nuance: Formal, written equivalent of に違いない, expressing the speaker's firm conviction; found in essays, reports and detective fiction. Also fixed in documents as 相違ありません ('this is correct').

relatedReferences.text: 〜に違いない: same meaning, neutral and usable in speech
〜に決まっている: casual and subjective, can sound pushy
〜にほかならない: identifies something as 'nothing but X', not a conjecture

similar: 〜に違いない: same meaning, neutral and usable in speech
〜に決まっている: casual and subjective, can sound pushy
〜にほかならない: identifies something as 'nothing but X', not a conjecture

examples.en: Although it is a student's independent production, it has turned out to be a work well worth watching.
examples.ja: 学生の自主制作とはいえ、十分に鑑賞に堪える作品に仕上がっている。

examples.en: This suitcase's selling point is that it is sturdy enough to stand up to more than ten years of use.
examples.ja: このスーツケースは、十年以上の使用に堪える頑丈さが売りだ。

examples.en: This translation is not stiffly literal; it is in natural Japanese that holds up well for general readers.
examples.ja: この翻訳は直訳調ではなく、一般の読者が読むに堪える自然な日本語になっている。

records.formation: V辞書形 + に堪える / N(鑑賞・使用・批判) + に堪える
records.meaning: worth …ing; able to stand up to …
records.nuance: Formal and evaluative: something is good or strong enough to withstand viewing, reading, use or scrutiny (鑑賞に堪える, 実用に堪える). Common in reviews and product descriptions; the negative に堪えない is even more frequent.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に足る: worthy or sufficient (信頼に足る); に堪える stresses holding up under use or scrutiny
〜に値する: deserving, stressing value (賞賛に値する)
〜に堪えない: the negative, 'too awful to'

similar: 〜に足る: worthy or sufficient (信頼に足る); に堪える stresses holding up under use or scrutiny
〜に値する: deserving, stressing value (賞賛に値する)
〜に堪えない: the negative, 'too awful to'

examples.en: If the trains aren't running, I'll simply walk home.
examples.ja: 電車が動かないなら、歩いて帰るまでだ。

examples.en: There's no deeper meaning. I merely said what I thought.
examples.ja: 別に深い意味はありません。思ったことを言ったまでです。

examples.cloze: 挑戦するまでのことだ
examples.en: If I don't pass this screening, I'll just try again next year.
examples.ja: 今回の審査に通らなければ、来年また挑戦するまでのことだ。

records.formation: V辞書形 + までだ / までのことだ（決意）; Vた形 + までだ / までのことだ（理由の限定）
records.meaning: will simply …; (I) merely did …, nothing more
records.nuance: With the dictionary form it shows calm resolve: if plan A fails, the speaker will just take the next step without fuss. With the past form it plays down an action as having no deeper motive. Somewhat formal and firm in tone.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ばそれまでだ: 'if X happens, that's the end of it', expresses futility rather than resolve
〜だけだ: 'only/just', neutral and everyday, lacks the firm, unbothered tone
〜しかない: 'no choice but to', sounds resigned rather than resolute

similar: 〜ばそれまでだ: 'if X happens, that's the end of it', expresses futility rather than resolve

audit.why: は別として can also set a topic aside, as in 費用の問題は別として; restricting it to exceptions creates a false contrast.

examples.en: Joking aside, let's discuss the main issue: the budget for next month's event.

audit.why: は別として can also set a topic aside, as in 費用の問題は別として; restricting it to exceptions creates a false contrast.

examples.ja: 冗談はさておき、本題である来月のイベントの予算について話し合いましょう。

examples.en: Leaving the question of cost aside, how many people would support this plan in the first place?

audit.why: は別として can also set a topic aside, as in 費用の問題は別として; restricting it to exceptions creates a false contrast.

examples.ja: 費用の問題はさておき、そもそもこの計画に賛同する人がどれだけいるだろうか。

examples.en: Setting aside whether it's feasible, let's start by freely throwing out ideas.

audit.why: は別として can also set a topic aside, as in 費用の問題は別として; restricting it to exceptions creates a false contrast.

examples.ja: 実現できるかどうかはさておき、まずはアイデアを自由に出し合ってみよう。

records.formation: N / 〜かどうか + はさておき
records.meaning: leaving … aside for now; setting … aside
records.nuance: Sets one topic aside to move to what matters more; used in conversation and writing alike. Set phrases: 冗談はさておき, それはさておき, 〜かどうかはさておき.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はともかく(として): very close and often interchangeable, but leans toward evaluating ('X aside, Y is fine') rather than postponing a topic
〜は別として: 'apart from / setting aside'; can mark an exception or leave an issue out of consideration
〜をさしおいて: 'passing over' someone or something that should come first, often critical

similar: 〜はともかく(として): very close and often interchangeable, but leans toward evaluating ('X aside, Y is fine') rather than postponing a topic

audit.why: がてら is conventionally classified as N1 grammar rather than N2.

examples.en: While out for a walk, I stopped to take a look at the new bakery in front of the station.

audit.why: がてら is conventionally classified as N1 grammar rather than N2.

examples.ja: 散歩がてら、駅前に新しくできたパン屋をのぞいてみた。

examples.en: This weekend I plan to take a drive along the coast and, while I'm at it, go buy vegetables at the roadside station in the next town.

audit.why: がてら is conventionally classified as N1 grammar rather than N2.

examples.ja: 週末は海沿いをドライブがてら、隣町の道の駅まで野菜を買いに行くつもりだ。

examples.en: While paying a courtesy call on a client, I also checked on how the newly opened branch was doing.

audit.why: がてら is conventionally classified as N1 grammar rather than N2.

examples.ja: 取引先へのあいさつがてら、新しくできた支店の様子も見てきた。

records.formation: Vます形 / N(動作性名詞) + がてら
records.meaning: while at it; taking the chance to …; combining … with …
records.nuance: Doing one thing, the speaker also takes care of another on the same outing; the main clause usually has a movement verb such as 行く or 歩く. Relaxed in tone and used in both conversation and casual writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ついでに: broader 'while I'm at it'; the first action is clearly the main purpose
〜かたがた: formal, letter and business register (お礼かたがた)
〜ながら: two actions happening at the same moment, not combining errands

similar: 〜ついでに: broader 'while I'm at it'; the first action is clearly the main purpose

examples.cloze: 鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに
examples.en: The bell marking the end of class had barely rung when the students rushed out of the classroom.
examples.ja: 授業終了のチャイムが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、学生たちは教室を飛び出した。

examples.cloze: 始まるか始まらないかのうちに

examples.ja: 新作のチケットは、販売が始まるか始まらないかのうちに完売した。

examples.cloze: 入ったか入らないかのうちに
examples.en: My father had scarcely got into bed when he started snoring.
examples.ja: 父は布団に入ったか入らないかのうちに、いびきをかき始めた。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 + か + Vない + かのうちに (same verb both times)
records.meaning: scarcely had … when …; almost before … had finished
records.nuance: Stresses that the second event started almost at the same instant as the first, before it was even complete. Written and narrative in tone; describes facts, not the speaker's intentions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たとたん(に): right after, with surprise; less focus on the first action being incomplete
〜かと思うと: rapid, surprising succession with looser timing
〜や否や: literary 'the instant that' (N1)

similar: 〜たとたん(に): right after, with surprise; less focus on the first action being incomplete

audit.why: ついでに does not require a spontaneous decision; a secondary errand can be planned in advance.

examples.en: While I was out at the post office, I also stopped by the dry cleaner's near the station.

audit.why: ついでに does not require a spontaneous decision; a secondary errand can be planned in advance.

examples.ja: 郵便局に行ったついでに、駅前のクリーニング店にも寄ってきた。

examples.en: While on a business trip, I took the chance to walk around the town where I spent my student days, for the first time in years.

audit.why: ついでに does not require a spontaneous decision; a secondary errand can be planned in advance.

examples.ja: 出張のついでに、学生時代を過ごした街を久しぶりに歩いてみた。

examples.en: While rearranging my room, I took the opportunity to get rid of all the clothes I no longer wear.

audit.why: ついでに does not require a spontaneous decision; a secondary errand can be planned in advance.

examples.ja: 部屋の模様替えをするついでに、着なくなった服をまとめて処分した。

records.formation: Vる / Vた + ついでに; Nの + ついでに
records.meaning: while one is at it; taking the opportunity of …
records.nuance: Neutral and everyday: adds a secondary action that takes advantage of the main one. Very common in conversation and casual writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜がてら: doing one thing while also doing another, usually with movement like 散歩; slightly literary
〜かたがた: formal, used in letters and business greetings
〜を兼ねて: one trip or action serves two purposes; ついでに treats one action as secondary, whether planned in advance or added on the spot

similar: 〜がてら: doing one thing while also doing another, usually with movement like 散歩; slightly literary

examples.cloze: 子どもではあるまいし
examples.en: You're not a child, so at least tidy your own room yourself.
examples.ja: 子どもではあるまいし、自分の部屋くらい自分で片付けなさい。

examples.en: It's not as if we'll never see each other again, so there's no need to cry like that.
examples.ja: 一生会えなくなるわけではあるまいし、そんなに泣かなくてもいいよ。

examples.cloze: 料理人ではあるまいし
examples.en: I'm not a professional chef, so I can't make such elaborate dishes every day.
examples.ja: プロの料理人ではあるまいし、毎日そんなに手の込んだ料理は作れないよ。

records.formation: N + ではあるまいし / V普通形 + の・わけ + ではあるまいし

examples.en: After agonizing for three whole hours, I ended up choosing the cheapest plan anyway.
examples.ja: 三時間も迷ったあげく、結局いちばん安いプランに決めた。

examples.ja: 交渉は半年に及んだが、さんざんもめたあげく、計画そのものが白紙に戻された。

examples.ja: 長い議論のあげく、会議は何も決まらないまま終わった。

records.formation: Vた形 + あげく(に) / Nの + あげく(に)

examples.cloze: 謝罪せずにはすまない
examples.en: Having caused trouble for an important client, the company president will have to apologise in person.
examples.ja: 大切な取引先に迷惑をかけた以上、社長が直接謝罪せずにはすまないだろう。

examples.en: Having caused this much uproar, they will surely not get away without some form of disciplinary action.
examples.ja: これだけの騒ぎを起こしたのだから、何らかの処分を受けずにはすまないだろう。

examples.ja: 友達に借りた大事な本を汚してしまったので、新しいのを買って返さずにはすまない。

records.formation: Vない形 + ずにはすまない (する → せずにはすまない); also Vない形 + ないではすまない
records.meaning: will have to …; cannot get away without …ing
records.nuance: Says an action is unavoidable given the situation, social norms or one's responsibility, typically apologising, compensating or being punished. Formal in tone; ずにはすまされない is a stronger variant.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずにはおかない: inevitably causes a reaction, or a firm will; ずにはすまない is obligation imposed by circumstances
〜ざるを得ない: forced to do something against one's wishes
〜ないわけにはいかない: cannot avoid doing, for social or moral reasons; more conversational

similar: 〜ずにはおかない: inevitably causes a reaction, or a firm will; ずにはすまない is obligation imposed by circumstances
〜ざるを得ない: forced to do something against one's wishes
〜ないわけにはいかない: cannot avoid doing, for social or moral reasons; more conversational

examples.cloze: セールスに決まってる
examples.en: Someone calling at this hour? It's bound to be a sales call.
examples.ja: こんな時間に電話してくるなんて、どうせセールスに決まってるよ。

examples.cloze: 失敗するに決まっている
examples.en: If you go into the real thing without preparing, you're sure to fail.
examples.ja: 準備もしないで本番に臨んだら、失敗するに決まっている。

examples.en: If we can all go together, of course that'll be more fun!
examples.ja: みんなで一緒に行けるなら、そのほうが楽しいに決まってるじゃない。

records.formation: 普通形（なA語幹・N は だ を付けない）+ に決まっている
records.meaning: definitely …; bound to be …; of course …
records.nuance: Conversational expression of the speaker's strong, often subjective conviction; can sound pushy or dismissive. Usually shortened to 〜に決まってる in speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に違いない: firm inference, more neutral and written
〜はずだ: expectation reasoned from facts or plans
〜に相違ない: formal written counterpart of に違いない

similar: 〜に違いない: firm inference, more neutral and written
〜はずだ: expectation reasoned from facts or plans
〜に相違ない: formal written counterpart of に違いない

examples.en: Queuing from early morning paid off: I managed to get the limited-edition item.
examples.ja: 朝早くから並んだかいがあって、限定品を無事に手に入れることができた。

examples.en: Seeing the spectacular view from the summit, I truly felt the four-hour climb had been worth it.
examples.ja: 山頂からの絶景を目にして、四時間かけて登ったかいがあったと心から思った。

examples.en: Despite intensive treatment, the zoo's long-loved elephant passed away.
examples.ja: 懸命な治療のかいもなく、長年親しまれてきた動物園のゾウが息を引き取った。

records.formation: Vた形 / Nの + かい(甲斐)がある / かいがない / かいもなく
records.meaning: worth …ing; the effort of …ing pays off
records.nuance: Says that an effort was rewarded with the hoped-for result; the negative (かいがない, かいもなく) voices disappointment that it was in vain. Used in conversation and writing, often with 頑張った, 待った or 来た.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけのことはある: the result lives up to the effort or reputation (an evaluation of quality)
〜がい (やりがい, 生きがい): fixed suffix forming a noun 'worth doing / living for'
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite'; かいもなく specifically says an effort failed to bring the hoped-for result

similar: 〜だけのことはある: the result lives up to the effort or reputation (an evaluation of quality)
〜がい (やりがい, 生きがい): fixed suffix forming a noun 'worth doing / living for'
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite'; かいもなく specifically says an effort failed to bring the hoped-for result

examples.en: Reading the victim's written account, I could not help feeling deep sympathy.
examples.ja: 被害者の手記を読み、深い同情を禁じ得なかった。

examples.en: I cannot suppress my anger that public money was wasted to this extent.
examples.ja: 公金がこれほど無駄に使われていたことには、怒りを禁じ得ない。

examples.en: I could not suppress my astonishment at the superb playing of a boy of just ten.
examples.ja: わずか十歳の少年の見事な演奏には、驚きを禁じ得なかった。

records.formation: N（感情名詞：怒り・同情・涙・驚きなど）+ を禁じ得ない
records.meaning: cannot help feeling …; cannot suppress (an emotion)
records.nuance: A very formal written expression for an emotion welling up that the speaker cannot hold back, usually in response to news or a moving scene. It takes an emotion noun, normally describes the speaker's own feeling, and is rare in casual speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずにはいられない: attaches to verbs and is the common, less formal way to say 'cannot help doing'
〜てならない: a feeling that is unbearably strong, used for one's own inner state
〜を隠せない: the emotion shows on the outside in spite of oneself; less stiff and freely used about other people (驚きを隠せない)

similar: 〜ずにはいられない: attaches to verbs and is the common, less formal way to say 'cannot help doing'
〜てならない: a feeling that is unbearably strong, used for one's own inner state
〜を隠せない: the emotion shows on the outside in spite of oneself; less stiff and freely used about other people (驚きを隠せない)

examples.cloze: 五十人といったところだ
examples.en: The new shop gets about fifty customers a day on weekdays, and that's it.
examples.ja: 新しい店の客の入りは、平日で一日五十人といったところだ。

examples.cloze: 色づき始めといったところです
examples.en: It's still too early for peak autumn color; the leaves have only just begun to turn.
examples.ja: 紅葉はまだ見頃には早く、ようやく色づき始めといったところです。

examples.cloze: 千二百円といったところ
examples.en: This job probably pays twelve hundred yen an hour at most.
examples.ja: この仕事の時給は、せいぜい千二百円といったところだろう。

records.formation: N（数量・程度） / V辞書形 + といったところだ
records.meaning: about …; at most …
records.nuance: Gives a rough figure or describes a stage while implying it is not much, roughly 'that's about it'. Conversational to semi-formal, often with せいぜい.

relatedReferences.text: 〜くらいだ／〜程度だ: neutral 'about', with no 'only that much' feeling
〜にすぎない: 'merely', more strongly dismissive
〜というところだ: near-identical variant

similar: 〜くらいだ／〜程度だ: neutral 'about', with no 'only that much' feeling
〜にすぎない: 'merely', more strongly dismissive
〜というところだ: near-identical variant

examples.en: Just as I was about to go out, a parcel arrived.
examples.ja: 出かけようとしているところに、宅配便が届いた。

examples.en: Just as I was preparing for the meeting, an urgent call came in from the department head.
examples.ja: 会議の準備をしているところへ、部長から急な電話が入った。

examples.en: Just as I'd finally finished tidying up, the kids brought their toys out again.
examples.ja: やっと片付けが終わったところに、子どもたちがまたおもちゃを持ち出してきた。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vている / Vた + ところに／ところへ
records.meaning: just when …, (something or someone arrives)
records.nuance: Something arrives or happens at exactly that moment, often interrupting or changing the situation. Narrative register; the main clause typically has 来る, 届く or 電話が入る.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ところを: the moment itself is acted upon (seen, caught, interrupted)
〜最中に: 'right in the middle of', stresses being mid-action
〜たとたん: 'the instant after', sudden change following an action

similar: 〜ところを: the moment itself is acted upon (seen, caught, interrupted)
〜最中に: 'right in the middle of', stresses being mid-action
〜たとたん: 'the instant after', sudden change following an action

examples.en: The house next door seems to be empty; no matter how many times I ring the bell, there is no answer.
examples.ja: 隣の家は留守とみえて、何度チャイムを鳴らしても返事がない。

examples.en: The new smartphone must be extremely popular, as it remains sold out at every shop.
examples.ja: 新型のスマホはよほど人気があるとみえて、どの店でも品切れが続いている。

examples.en: Judging from the puddles all over the road, it appears to have rained during the night.
examples.ja: 道路のあちこちに水たまりができているところを見ると、夜のうちに雨が降ったとみえる。

records.formation: 普通形（Na・Nは「だ」省略可）+ とみえる / とみえて、〜
records.meaning: it appears that …; seemingly …
records.nuance: Somewhat literary. The speaker infers a situation from visible evidence; often used as とみえて to give the inferred reason before the observed fact.

relatedReferences.text: 〜らしい: inference from hearsay or evidence; more conversational
〜ようだ: general inference from the speaker's own impression
〜に違いない: strong conviction rather than an appearance-based guess

similar: 〜らしい: inference from hearsay or evidence; more conversational
〜ようだ: general inference from the speaker's own impression
〜に違いない: strong conviction rather than an appearance-based guess

examples.en: After three months of talks, the two companies finally reached an agreement.
examples.ja: 三か月に及ぶ話し合いの末、両社はようやく合意に至った。

examples.en: A small wiring mistake can sometimes escalate into a large-scale blackout.
examples.ja: 小さな配線ミスから、大規模な停電に至ることもある。

examples.en: As residents' opposition spread, things reached the point where the city withdrew the plan.
examples.ja: 住民の反対運動が広がり、市は計画を撤回するに至った。

records.formation: N + に至る / V辞書形 + に至る
records.meaning: to reach …; to end up …; to come to …
records.nuance: Formal: reaching a point or outcome at the end of a process (合意に至る, 結論に至る, 死に至る). V辞書形 + に至った means 'it got to the point where …' and is common in news reports.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に達する: reach a quantity, level or figure
〜に至るまで: 'all the way to', marking the far end of a range
〜ようになる: everyday 'come to (do)'

similar: 〜に達する: reach a quantity, level or figure
〜に至るまで: 'all the way to', marking the far end of a range
〜ようになる: everyday 'come to (do)'

examples.en: Undaunted by the heavy rain, the athletes ran all out to the very end.
examples.ja: 選手たちは激しい雨をものともせず、最後まで全力で走り抜いた。

examples.en: Undeterred by the danger of aftershocks, the rescue team kept searching for residents trapped under the rubble.
examples.ja: 救助隊は余震の危険をものともせずに、がれきの下に取り残された住民を捜し続けた。

examples.en: Undaunted by the opposition of those around them, the owner opened a café in a village of just two hundred people.
examples.ja: その店主は周囲の反対をものともせず、人口二百人の村でカフェを開いた。

records.formation: N + をものともせず（に）
records.meaning: undaunted by …; in defiance of …
records.nuance: Describes someone pressing on in spite of hardship, danger or opposition, and carries the writer's admiration. Written and news register; it is used about others rather than about oneself.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をよそに: carries on ignoring others' worry or a situation, often with a critical tone
〜を顧みず: acts without regard for risk or sacrifice, can sound reckless
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite', with no admiration built in

similar: 〜をよそに: carries on ignoring others' worry or a situation, often with a critical tone
〜を顧みず: acts without regard for risk or sacrifice, can sound reckless
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite', with no admiration built in

audit.why: じゃない／でない belongs only after nouns and na-adjectives here; already-negative verbs and i-adjectives connect directly to ことはない／こともない.

examples.en: If we hurry it's not impossible to make it, but it will be tight.

audit.why: じゃない／でない belongs only after nouns and na-adjectives here; already-negative verbs and i-adjectives connect directly to ことはない／こともない.

examples.ja: 急げば間に合わないことはないが、少し厳しい。

examples.en: It's not that I can't eat spicy food, but I'm not really fond of it.

audit.why: じゃない／でない belongs only after nouns and na-adjectives here; already-negative verbs and i-adjectives connect directly to ことはない／こともない.

examples.ja: 辛いものは食べられないこともないけど、あまり得意じゃない。

examples.en: I can sort of understand that feeling, but rules are rules.

audit.why: じゃない／でない belongs only after nouns and na-adjectives here; already-negative verbs and i-adjectives connect directly to ことはない／こともない.

examples.ja: その気持ちもわからなくもないが、ルールはルールだ。

records.formation: Vない形 + ことはない／こともない；いAくない + ことはない／こともない；なA・N + じゃない（でない）+ ことはない／こともない（Vない → Vなくもない）
records.meaning: it is not that … not …; it is not impossible to …
records.nuance: A double negative giving a weak, hedged yes: possible, but without enthusiasm. Conversational, often used to soften or qualify.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ことはない: 'there's no need to …'
〜わけではない: 'it's not that …', partial denial
〜ざるを得ない: 'have no choice but to', strong obligation

similar: 〜ことはない: 'there's no need to …'
〜わけではない: 'it's not that …', partial denial
〜ざるを得ない: 'have no choice but to', strong obligation

examples.en: Isn't there something that can be done about this traffic? I waste a whole hour every morning.
examples.ja: この渋滞、何とかならないものか。毎朝一時間も無駄にしている。

examples.en: Wondering whether there was an easier way to convey the region's appeal, young staff members started making videos.
examples.ja: もっと手軽に地方の魅力を伝えられないものかと、若手職員たちが動画制作を始めた。

examples.cloze: 晴れてくれないものか
examples.en: A rain forecast for the long weekend, of all times. If only it would somehow clear up.
examples.ja: せっかくの連休なのに雨予報か。どうにか晴れてくれないものかなあ。

records.formation: Vない形（可能形が多い）+ ものか／ものだろうか
records.meaning: is there no way to …?; if only somehow …
records.nuance: Voices a strong wish for something hard to bring about, often with なんとか or どうにか. Slightly literary; ものだろうか is softer and more reflective.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ものか (V辞書形 + ものか): emphatic refusal, 'as if I would'
〜たいものだ: states one's own heartfelt wish outright, not a search for some way to make it happen
〜ないだろうか: polite request or tentative suggestion

similar: 〜ものか (V辞書形 + ものか): emphatic refusal, 'as if I would'
〜たいものだ: states one's own heartfelt wish outright, not a search for some way to make it happen
〜ないだろうか: polite request or tentative suggestion

examples.en: Even though it was a weekday morning, there was a long line outside the new café.
examples.ja: 平日の朝にもかかわらず、新しいカフェの前には長い行列ができていた。

examples.cloze: あったにもかかわらず
examples.en: Despite repeated warnings, there has again been no end to mountain accidents this year.
examples.ja: 再三の注意喚起があったにもかかわらず、山での遭難事故は今年も後を絶たない。

examples.en: In spite of the unfortunate rain, a huge number of fans turned out at the stadium for us.
examples.ja: あいにくの雨にもかかわらず、大勢のファンがスタジアムに駆けつけてくれた。

records.formation: 普通形 + にもかかわらず（なA語幹・N は そのまま／である）/ N + にもかかわらず
records.meaning: despite …; in spite of …; even though …
records.nuance: A formal, written-leaning 'despite' that presents an outcome running against what the first fact would lead one to expect, often with surprise or mild criticism. The second clause cannot be a command, request or intention; also used sentence-initially as それにもかかわらず.

relatedReferences.text: 〜のに: conversational and more emotional (complaint, regret); にもかかわらず is more objective and formal
〜ものの: concedes the first fact before a softer contrast ('although')
〜にかかわらず (no も): 'regardless of' (天候にかかわらず), a completely different meaning

similar: 〜のに: conversational and more emotional (complaint, regret); にもかかわらず is more objective and formal

examples.en: This rain doesn't look like it will stop any time soon, so let's call a taxi.
examples.ja: この雨はしばらくやみそうにないから、タクシーを呼ぼう。

examples.en: I have a mountain of work, so it doesn't look like I'll make the last train tonight.
examples.ja: 仕事が山積みで、今夜は終電に間に合いそうもない。

examples.en: The two countries' positions remain far apart, and the negotiations seem unlikely to reach agreement any time soon.
examples.ja: 両国の主張は平行線をたどっており、交渉は当面まとまりそうにない。

records.formation: Vます形 + そうにない／そうもない（そうにもない）
records.meaning: not likely to …; does not look as if …
records.nuance: The speaker judges from the present situation that something is unlikely to happen; そうもない sounds a little more emphatic. Conversational and very common.

relatedReferences.text: 〜なさそうだ: 'looks like it isn't / won't', softer and often about states
〜わけがない: categorical 'there's no way', much stronger certainty
〜まい: literary negative conjecture

similar: 〜なさそうだ: 'looks like it isn't / won't', softer and often about states
〜わけがない: categorical 'there's no way', much stronger certainty
〜まい: literary negative conjecture

examples.en: We will contact you again as soon as the details are settled.
examples.ja: 詳細が決まり次第、改めてご連絡いたします。

examples.en: Whether you succeed or not depends on how hard you work in the first year.
examples.ja: 成功するかどうかは、最初の一年の頑張り次第だ。

examples.en: Depending on the weather, the fireworks festival may be postponed.
examples.ja: 天候次第では、花火大会が延期になる可能性もあります。

records.formation: Vます形 + 次第 (as soon as) / N + 次第で / N + 次第だ (depending on)
records.meaning: as soon as …; depending on …
records.nuance: Vます + 次第 is a formal, business-style 'as soon as', used for promised future actions; the main clause cannot be past. N + 次第 says the outcome is determined by N.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たらすぐ: casual 'as soon as', usable in everyday speech
〜とたん(に): 'the moment …', for past, often unexpected events; 次第 is for planned future actions
〜によって: 'varies by …', neutral; 次第 stresses that N decides the outcome

similar: 〜たらすぐ: casual 'as soon as', usable in everyday speech
〜とたん(に): 'the moment …', for past, often unexpected events; 次第 is for planned future actions

audit.why: The presence or absence of は does not distinguish the two senses of に(は)及ばない. Also, までもない generally means an action is unnecessary; only expressions such as 言うまでもない mean that something goes without saying.

examples.en: It's only a mild cold, so there's no need to worry.

audit.why: The presence or absence of は does not distinguish the two senses of に(は)及ばない. Also, までもない generally means an action is unnecessary; only expressions such as 言うまでもない mean that something goes without saying.

examples.ja: 軽い風邪ですから、ご心配には及びません。

examples.en: We'll send the documents by email, so there's no need to come all the way to pick them up.

audit.why: The presence or absence of は does not distinguish the two senses of に(は)及ばない. Also, までもない generally means an action is unnecessary; only expressions such as 言うまでもない mean that something goes without saying.

examples.ja: 資料はメールでお送りしますので、わざわざ取りに来ていただくには及びません。

examples.en: For a repair this small, there's no need to call in a contractor. You can easily do it yourself.

audit.why: The presence or absence of は does not distinguish the two senses of に(は)及ばない. Also, までもない generally means an action is unnecessary; only expressions such as 言うまでもない mean that something goes without saying.

examples.ja: この程度の修理なら業者を呼ぶには及ばない。自分でも十分できる。

records.formation: V辞書形 / N + には及ばない（丁寧: には及びません）
records.meaning: there is no need to …
records.nuance: Politely tells someone they need not go to the trouble, often with ご心配, お礼 or わざわざ. Slightly formal and considerate in tone.

relatedReferences.text: 〜までもない: 'there is no need to go so far as …'; the action is unnecessary or excessive
〜ことはない: plain 'there's no need to'; more casual
〜に及ばない: also means 'there is no need to'; with a comparison target, に(は)及ばない means 'cannot match' (彼の実力には及ばない)

similar: 〜までもない: 'there is no need to go so far as …'; the action is unnecessary or excessive

examples.en: Ignoring his parents' worries, the son quit university and set off on a trip around the world.
examples.ja: 親の心配をよそに、息子は大学を辞めて世界一周の旅に出た。

examples.en: Paying no heed to residents' opposition, the city is steadily pushing ahead with its plan to build a waste-processing facility.
examples.ja: 住民の反対をよそに、市はごみ処理施設の建設計画を着々と進めている。

examples.en: In contrast to all the talk of an economic slump, sales of luxury brands hit a record high.
examples.ja: 景気低迷の声をよそに、高級ブランドの売り上げは過去最高を記録した。

records.formation: N + をよそに
records.meaning: ignoring …; in disregard of …; in contrast to …
records.nuance: Someone carries on as if a worry, criticism or surrounding situation had nothing to do with them. Often critical of the person who ignores others, but in news it can also mark a neutral contrast with the general mood. Written register.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をものともせず: overcomes hardship or danger, with admiration rather than criticism
〜を顧みず: disregards risks or sacrifices, usually to oneself or one's family
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite', without the sense of brushing something aside

similar: 〜をものともせず: overcomes hardship or danger, with admiration rather than criticism
〜を顧みず: disregards risks or sacrifices, usually to oneself or one's family
〜にもかかわらず: neutral 'despite', without the sense of brushing something aside

examples.en: With a partner of many years, your feelings get across even without putting them into words.
examples.ja: 長年連れ添った相手なら、言わずとも気持ちは伝わるものだ。

examples.en: For paperwork of this kind, you can finish it online without going all the way to the counter.
examples.ja: この程度の手続きなら、わざわざ窓口に行かずとも、オンラインで済ませられる。

examples.en: Even someone who is not an expert would see at once that this plan is unrealistic.
examples.ja: 専門家ならずとも、この計画に無理があることはすぐにわかるだろう。

records.formation: Vない形 + ずとも (する → せずとも); N + ならずとも
records.meaning: even without …ing; even if one does not (or is not) …
records.nuance: A literary, formal equivalent of 〜なくても, often followed by わかる, いい or 構わない, with 言わずとも as the most familiar set phrase. With nouns it appears as ならずとも ('even if not …'), as in 専門家ならずとも.

relatedReferences.text: 〜なくても: the everyday 'even if not'; ずとも sounds literary
〜ずして: 'without doing', describing how something happened rather than a concessive condition
〜までもない: 'there is no need to go as far as …', stressing that the action is unnecessary

similar: 〜なくても: the everyday 'even if not'; ずとも sounds literary
〜ずして: 'without doing', describing how something happened rather than a concessive condition
〜までもない: 'there is no need to go as far as …', stressing that the action is unnecessary

examples.en: The degree may differ, but every industry is struggling with a serious labour shortage.
examples.ja: 程度の差こそあれ、どの業界も深刻な人手不足に悩んでいる。

examples.en: Looking back now, I feel nothing but gratitude for my parents' harsh words, and have no reason at all to resent them.
examples.ja: 親の厳しい言葉には、今となっては感謝こそすれ、恨む理由など一つもない。

examples.en: If anything, this deregulation will be a blow to local retailers; it is unlikely to be a tailwind.
examples.ja: 今回の規制緩和は、地方の小売店にとって打撃になりこそすれ、追い風にはならないだろう。

records.formation: N + こそあれ (差こそあれ) ; Aな語幹 / N + でこそあれ ; Aい語幹 + くこそあれ ; Vます形 / する動詞の語幹 + こそすれ + 〜ない
records.meaning: even if there is …, (still) …; if anything …, but never …
records.nuance: Concedes or affirms one thing in order to firmly deny the other; こそすれ is usually followed by a negative, as in 'one might X, but never Y'. Formal and written; set phrases include 程度の差こそあれ and 感謝こそすれ.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ことはあっても〜ない: plain equivalent of こそすれ 'might X but never Y'
〜とはいえ: 'although'; a general concession without the emphatic contrast
〜こそ: simple emphasis 'precisely'; no concessive meaning on its own

similar: 〜ことはあっても〜ない: plain equivalent of こそすれ 'might X but never Y'
〜とはいえ: 'although'; a general concession without the emphatic contrast
〜こそ: simple emphasis 'precisely'; no concessive meaning on its own

examples.en: When I went to try the new bakery by the station, there was already a long line before it had even opened.
examples.ja: 駅前の新しいパン屋に行ってみたところ、開店前から長い行列ができていた。

examples.en: When I enquired at the city office, I was told the application deadline had already passed.
examples.ja: 市の窓口に問い合わせたところ、申請の締め切りはすでに過ぎているとのことだった。

examples.en: When the company ran an internal survey, it found that more than half of staff wanted to keep working from home.
examples.ja: 社内でアンケートを実施したところ、半数以上が在宅勤務の継続を希望していることがわかった。

records.formation: Vた形 + ところ
records.meaning: when I did …, (I found that) …
records.nuance: Somewhat formal and common in reports and news: an action is presented as the trigger, and the main clause states what was found or what happened, often unexpected. The main clause reports an outcome, never the speaker's own intention or request.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たら (discovery use): broader and conversational; たところ is more formal and limited to past outcomes
〜たところだ: aspect, 'have just done', with no trigger-result link
〜たところで: 'even if one does', leading to a futile or unimportant result

similar: 〜たら (discovery use): broader and conversational; たところ is more formal and limited to past outcomes
〜たところだ: aspect, 'have just done', with no trigger-result link
〜たところで: 'even if one does', leading to a futile or unimportant result

examples.en: If you're even a minute late to a meeting, the department head yells at you.
examples.ja: 会議に一分でも遅れようものなら、部長に大声で怒鳴られる。

examples.en: Let your guard down even slightly during a race and the runners behind you will overtake you in no time.
examples.ja: レース中に少しでも油断しようものなら、すぐに後続に抜かれてしまう。

examples.en: If you dare leave food in front of my grandmother, a long lecture begins.
examples.ja: 祖母の前で食べ物を残そうものなら、長い説教が始まる。

records.formation: V意向形 + ものなら
records.meaning: if one so much as dared to …
records.nuance: Warns that even a small action would bring a severe or unpleasant result. Often exaggerated, and used to complain about strict people or touchy situations.

relatedReferences.text: V可能形 + ものなら: 'if one could', wishful or challenging, not a warning
〜たら: neutral 'if', with no sense of dire consequence
〜が最後: 'once you do X, it's over', stresses irreversibility

similar: V可能形 + ものなら: 'if one could', wishful or challenging, not a warning
〜たら: neutral 'if', with no sense of dire consequence
〜が最後: 'once you do X, it's over', stresses irreversibility

examples.en: The damage if a major earthquake struck directly beneath the capital late at night is frightening even to imagine.
examples.ja: 首都直下地震が深夜に起きた場合の被害は、想像するだに恐ろしい。

examples.en: The palace guard did not move a muscle, even when surrounded by tourists.
examples.ja: 宮殿の衛兵は、観光客に囲まれても微動だにしなかった。

examples.en: The city paid not the slightest heed to the residents' urgent appeals.
examples.ja: 住民たちの切実な訴えを、市は一顧だにしなかった。

records.formation: V辞書形 (想像する / 考える / 聞く) + だに; N + (に)だに + 否定 (微動だにしない / 一顧だにしない / 夢にだに思わない)
records.meaning: even (just) …ing (e.g. to imagine or think of); not even …
records.nuance: A literary particle surviving mainly in fixed expressions: 考えるだに恐ろしい, 想像するだに, 微動だにしない, 一顧だにしない. It stresses that even the slightest act triggers a feeling, or that not even the minimum happens.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでも: the everyday 'just …ing is enough to …'
〜さえ: 'even', in general modern use
〜すら: written 'even', with broader use than だに

similar: 〜だけでも: the everyday 'just …ing is enough to …'
〜さえ: 'even', in general modern use
〜すら: written 'even', with broader use than だに

examples.en: Three months after joining the company, I haven't even been paid proper overtime, let alone a bonus.
examples.ja: 入社して三か月、ボーナスはおろか、まともな残業代すら支払われていない。

examples.en: That village doesn't have a single traffic light, let alone a convenience store.
examples.ja: その村には、コンビニはおろか信号機さえ一つもない。

examples.en: I broke my leg and can't even walk on my own, let alone run.
examples.ja: 足を骨折してしまい、走ることはおろか、一人で歩くこともできない。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + こと + はおろか（後に も・さえ・すら・まで）
records.meaning: let alone …; to say nothing of …
records.nuance: Names the case where the statement obviously holds first, then a more basic or extreme one marked by も, さえ or すら ('not even B, let alone A'), usually in a negative sentence. Carries surprise or exasperation, so it is not used with requests, commands or the speaker's intentions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜どころか: more conversational, and can also flip expectations ('far from X, actually Y')
〜ばかりか: neutral 'not only', positive or negative
〜はもちろん: neutral 'of course X, and Y too', without the exasperated tone

similar: 〜どころか: more conversational, and can also flip expectations ('far from X, actually Y')
〜ばかりか: neutral 'not only', positive or negative
〜はもちろん: neutral 'of course X, and Y too', without the exasperated tone

examples.en: This film is based on an incident that actually happened.
examples.ja: この映画は、実際に起きた事件をもとに作られている。

examples.en: We plan to review next year's services based on the survey results.
examples.ja: アンケートの結果をもとに、来年度のサービス内容を見直す予定です。

examples.en: A picture book based on stories the author heard from their grandmother is popular among children.
examples.ja: 作者が祖母から聞いた話をもとにした絵本が、子どもたちの間で人気を集めている。

records.formation: N + をもとに(して) / N + をもとにした + N
records.meaning: based on …; drawing on … (as source material)
records.nuance: Marks the material, data or experience something is built from and then reworked into a new product (a film, a plan, a report). Neutral and common in news, business and everyday explanation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に基づいて: grounds or standards followed faithfully (rules, law, data); をもとに is raw material that gets reshaped
〜をきっかけに: the trigger that started something, not its source material
〜を踏まえて: taking a prior discussion or situation into account before acting

similar: 〜に基づいて: grounds or standards followed faithfully (rules, law, data); をもとに is raw material that gets reshaped
〜をきっかけに: the trigger that started something, not its source material
〜を踏まえて: taking a prior discussion or situation into account before acting

examples.en: Only after becoming a parent did I understand what my own parents went through.
examples.ja: 親になって初めて、自分の両親の苦労がわかった。

examples.en: Many people only realise how precious good health is after falling ill.
examples.ja: 病気をして初めて、健康のありがたさに気づく人は多い。

examples.en: Only when I actually visited the area did I truly grasp the scale of the damage.
examples.ja: 実際に現地を訪れて初めて、被害の大きさを実感した。

records.formation: Vて形 + 初めて
records.meaning: only after … (does one realise or manage something)
records.nuance: The main clause is a realisation or state that comes only after the experience, typically 〜て初めて〜がわかる / 気づく. Neutral register, common in essays and interviews.

relatedReferences.text: 〜てこそ: evaluative, 'only by doing it is it worthwhile'
〜てからでないと: precondition with a negative main clause
〜てようやく: 'finally, after …', stressing the long wait

similar: 〜てこそ: evaluative, 'only by doing it is it worthwhile'
〜てからでないと: precondition with a negative main clause
〜てようやく: 'finally, after …', stressing the long wait

examples.en: This restaurant uses only local products, from the seasonings all the way to the tableware.
examples.ja: この店では、調味料から食器に至るまで、すべて地元産のものを使っている。

examples.en: The new school rules lay down everything in detail, from hairstyles right down to the color of socks.
examples.ja: 新しい校則は、髪型から靴下の色に至るまで細かく定めている。

examples.en: The cause of the accident has still not been determined to this day.
examples.ja: 事故の原因については、現在に至るまで明らかになっていない。

records.formation: N + に至るまで (often Nから + Nに至るまで)
records.meaning: all the way to …; right down to …; even …
records.nuance: Stresses how far a range extends, with the end point being surprising or extreme (from big things down to tiny details). Somewhat formal; common in descriptions, advertising and news.

relatedReferences.text: 〜まで: plain 'until / as far as', without the emphasis
〜にわたって: over a span of time or area, neutral
〜をはじめ: 'starting with' a representative example

similar: 〜まで: plain 'until / as far as', without the emphasis
〜にわたって: over a span of time or area, neutral
〜をはじめ: 'starting with' a representative example

examples.cloze: 手といわず足といわず
examples.en: At the campsite I got bitten by mosquitoes all over, on my hands, my legs, everywhere.
examples.ja: キャンプ場で手といわず足といわず、全身あちこち蚊に刺されてしまった。

examples.cloze: 平日といわず週末といわず
examples.en: Weekdays or weekends alike, that café in front of the station is full whenever you go.
examples.ja: 平日といわず週末といわず、駅前のあのカフェはいつ行っても満席だ。

examples.cloze: 壁といわず天井といわず
examples.en: Walls and ceiling alike, the inside of the shop is plastered with old film posters.
examples.ja: 壁といわず天井といわず、店内には古い映画のポスターがびっしり貼られている。

records.formation: N1 + といわず + N2 + といわず
records.meaning: … and … alike; both … and … (and everywhere else); without distinction
records.nuance: Written or formal narrative style. Names two representative items to say that something applies everywhere or all the time, often with a sense of excess or being overwhelmed.

relatedReferences.text: 〜といい〜といい: picks two examples to evaluate a single thing; not 'everywhere alike'
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether A or B'; a neutral either-way condition
〜も〜も: plain 'both A and B', with no emphasis on totality

similar: 〜といい〜といい: picks two examples to evaluate a single thing; not 'everywhere alike'
〜にしろ〜にしろ: 'whether A or B'; a neutral either-way condition
〜も〜も: plain 'both A and B', with no emphasis on totality

examples.en: Our shop will close at the end of this month. Thank you very much for your many years of patronage.
examples.ja: 当店は今月末をもって閉店いたします。長年のご愛顧、誠にありがとうございました。

examples.en: We will inform you of the selection results in writing at a later date.
examples.ja: 選考の結果につきましては、後日書面をもってお知らせいたします。

examples.en: With characteristic tenacity, the newly appointed representative brought the stalled negotiations to a conclusion.
examples.ja: 新任の担当者は持ち前の粘り強さをもって、難航していた交渉をまとめ上げた。

records.formation: N + をもって（丁寧：をもちまして）
records.meaning: with …, by means of … (formal); as of …, at … (marking an end point)
records.nuance: A formal replacement for で, used for the means or quality with which something is done and for the point at which something ends. Typical of announcements, official notices and speeches; in daily conversation it sounds stiff.

relatedReferences.text: 〜で: the everyday particle for means and time limits, with no formality
〜を限りに: stresses that something ongoing stops after this point, often a personal decision
〜をもってすれば: praises a means that makes something possible, not just names it

similar: 〜で: the everyday particle for means and time limits, with no formality
〜を限りに: stresses that something ongoing stops after this point, often a personal decision
〜をもってすれば: praises a means that makes something possible, not just names it

examples.en: A book collecting the legends surrounding this castle has become a quiet hit locally.
examples.ja: この城にまつわる伝説を集めた本が、地元で静かなブームになっている。

examples.en: The program is inviting viewers to send in stories of their money-related blunders.
examples.ja: 番組では、お金にまつわる失敗談を視聴者から募集している。

examples.en: Superstitions surrounding the number four still influence room numbering in hospitals and hotels.
examples.ja: 数字の四にまつわる迷信は、今も病院やホテルの部屋番号に影響を与えている。

records.formation: N + にまつわる + N
records.meaning: connected with …; surrounding … (stories, legends, rumours)
records.nuance: Used attributively for stories, legends, superstitions, rumours, episodes or history that cling to a subject. Found in writing, broadcasting and feature articles; it suggests lore that has gathered around something.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に関する: general, neutral 'about/concerning'; まつわる suggests tales or episodes attached to the subject
〜をめぐる: about something contested (a dispute, debate or competition)
〜にちなんだ: named after or inspired by something

similar: 〜に関する: general, neutral 'about/concerning'; まつわる suggests tales or episodes attached to the subject
〜をめぐる: about something contested (a dispute, debate or competition)
〜にちなんだ: named after or inspired by something

examples.en: The moment the store opened, the customers poured onto the sales floor as if they had been waiting for this.
examples.ja: 開店と同時に、客たちは待ってましたとばかりに売り場へなだれ込んだ。

examples.en: The cat rubbed against my feet as if to say, 'Feed me, quick.'
examples.ja: 猫は「早くご飯をちょうだい」とばかりに足元にすり寄ってきた。

examples.en: As soon as they saw the opponent's mistake, the team launched a fierce attack, seizing the moment.
examples.ja: 相手のミスを見るや、チームはここぞとばかりに猛攻を仕掛けた。

records.formation: 普通形 / 命令形 / 意向形 / 引用（「〜」）+ とばかりに
records.meaning: as if to say …; as though …
records.nuance: Written and descriptive. Describes someone's (or an animal's) attitude or action as if it were saying the quoted words, though nothing is actually said; used about others, not oneself.

relatedReferences.text: 〜んばかりに: 'almost to the point of …'; describes degree, attaches to Vない stem
〜かのように: 'as if' in general, without the implied unspoken words
〜と言わんばかりに: near-synonym, more explicitly 'as if about to say'

similar: 〜んばかりに: 'almost to the point of …'; describes degree, attaches to Vない stem
〜かのように: 'as if' in general, without the implied unspoken words
〜と言わんばかりに: near-synonym, more explicitly 'as if about to say'

examples.en: With a promotion and a wedding, this year has been nothing but good news.
examples.ja: 今年は昇進に結婚と、いいことずくめの一年だった。

examples.en: The person caught on the security camera was reportedly a man dressed in black from head to toe.
examples.ja: 防犯カメラに映っていたのは、全身黒ずくめの男だったという。

examples.en: The new students are already feeling stifled by dorm life, where everything is governed by rules.
examples.ja: 規則ずくめの寮生活に、新入生たちは早くも息苦しさを感じている。

records.formation: N + ずくめ (黒ずくめ・いいことずくめ・規則ずくめ・異例ずくめ)
records.meaning: nothing but …; … from top to bottom; full of …
records.nuance: Says something is entirely made up of or surrounded by one thing; works with good things (いいことずくめ) as well as bad. Used in conversation and journalism, with a limited set of nouns.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だらけ: full of, usually bad or messy things (間違いだらけ)
〜まみれ: covered in something sticky or dirty (泥まみれ, 汗まみれ)
〜一色: completely dominated by one mood or theme (お祭り一色)

similar: 〜だらけ: full of, usually bad or messy things (間違いだらけ)
〜まみれ: covered in something sticky or dirty (泥まみれ, 汗まみれ)
〜一色: completely dominated by one mood or theme (お祭り一色)

examples.en: Only by experiencing failure yourself can you learn in the true sense.
examples.ja: 自分で失敗を経験してこそ、本当の意味で学ぶことができる。

examples.en: Laws only mean something when they are obeyed.
examples.ja: 法律は、守られてこそ意味がある。

examples.en: Cooking is only truly rewarding when you get to see the smiles of the people eating.
examples.ja: 料理は、食べる人の笑顔を見てこそ作りがいがあるというものだ。

records.formation: Vて形 + こそ
records.meaning: only by …ing (does it count or have value)
records.nuance: Emphatic: only through the stated action does the main clause become true or worthwhile. Typical of persuasive speech, essays and interviews; the main clause is usually a positive evaluation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜て初めて: 'only after', more neutral and about when a realisation happens
〜からこそ: emphasises a reason rather than a required action
〜ばこそ: literary 'precisely because'

similar: 〜て初めて: 'only after', more neutral and about when a realisation happens
〜からこそ: emphasises a reason rather than a required action
〜ばこそ: literary 'precisely because'

examples.en: Maybe because I was on my phone until late last night, my head has felt heavy since this morning.
examples.ja: 昨夜遅くまでスマホを見ていたせいか、朝から頭が重い。

examples.en: Perhaps because the temperature dropped suddenly, many students have been absent with colds this week.
examples.ja: 気温が急に下がったせいか、今週は風邪で欠席する生徒が多い。

examples.en: Maybe it's my age, but lately I've started waking up several times during the night.
examples.ja: 年のせいか、最近は夜中に何度も目が覚めるようになった。

records.formation: 普通形（ナAな、Nの） + せいか
records.meaning: perhaps because of …; maybe due to …
records.nuance: The speaker tentatively attributes a result, usually a negative one, to a cause they are not sure about. Neutral register, common in conversation and writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜せいで: a definite cause of a bad result, often with blame
〜おかげか: a tentative cause of a good result
〜からか / 〜ためか: neutral tentative reason with no negative coloring

similar: 〜せいで: a definite cause of a bad result, often with blame
〜おかげか: a tentative cause of a good result
〜からか / 〜ためか: neutral tentative reason with no negative coloring

examples.cloze: 賛成にしろ反対にしろ
examples.en: Whether you are for it or against it, you should state your opinion clearly.
examples.ja: 賛成にしろ反対にしろ、自分の意見をはっきり言うべきだ。

examples.cloze: 進学するにしろ就職するにしろ
examples.en: Whether you go on to further study or get a job, it's better to start preparing early.
examples.ja: 進学するにしろ就職するにしろ、早めに準備を始めたほうがいい。

examples.en: Whether by train or by car, you have to be ready for crowds when travelling over the holidays.
examples.ja: 電車にせよ車にせよ、連休中の移動は混雑を覚悟しなければならない。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + にしろ + N / V辞書形 + にしろ（にせよ〜にせよ）
records.meaning: whether … or …
records.nuance: Lists two alternatives, often opposites, and says the conclusion is the same for both. Somewhat formal; にせよ〜にせよ is more written.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にしても〜にしても: more conversational equivalent
〜であれ〜であれ: literary, mainly with nouns
〜といい〜といい: picks examples to praise or criticize, not alternatives

similar: 〜にしても〜にしても: more conversational equivalent
〜であれ〜であれ: literary, mainly with nouns
〜といい〜といい: picks examples to praise or criticize, not alternatives

examples.en: With the deadline closing in, a trip is out of the question.
examples.ja: 締め切りが迫っていて、旅行どころではない。

examples.en: The rain was far too heavy for any cherry-blossom viewing.
examples.ja: 雨が強すぎて、花見どころではなかった。

examples.en: I'm so swamped with moving preparations that resting is out of the question.
examples.ja: 引っ越しの準備に追われて、ゆっくり休むどころじゃない。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + どころではない（どころじゃない）
records.meaning: this is no time for …; … is out of the question
records.nuance: Says the current situation makes something impossible to think about or enjoy. Conversational, usually with a note of complaint or stress.

relatedReferences.text: 〜どころか: 'far from', denial plus the opposite reality
〜場合ではない: 'this isn't the time to …', often an admonition
〜わけにはいかない: cannot for moral or social reasons

similar: 〜どころか: 'far from', denial plus the opposite reality
〜場合ではない: 'this isn't the time to …', often an admonition
〜わけにはいかない: cannot for moral or social reasons

examples.en: Because of the typhoon, heavy rain continues to fall, mainly in Kyushu.
examples.ja: 台風の影響で、九州を中心に大雨が降り続いている。

examples.en: The new product's sales are growing, mainly among young women.
examples.ja: 新製品は若い女性を中心に売り上げを伸ばしている。

examples.en: The redevelopment plan centred on the station has finally got under way.
examples.ja: 駅を中心とした再開発計画が、ようやく動き出した。

records.formation: N + を中心に(して) / N + を中心として / N + を中心とした + N
records.meaning: centring on …; mainly in/among …
records.nuance: Names the core area, group or topic around which something spreads or is organised. Very frequent in weather reports, market news and descriptions of plans.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をめぐって: about / surrounding (a dispute or debate), not a physical or organisational centre
〜をはじめ(として): 'starting with' one representative example in a list
〜を軸に: with … as the axis or guiding principle, more abstract

similar: 〜をめぐって: about / surrounding (a dispute or debate), not a physical or organisational centre
〜をはじめ(として): 'starting with' one representative example in a list
〜を軸に: with … as the axis or guiding principle, more abstract

examples.en: As the sun went down, the streets grew more and more crowded.
examples.ja: 日が暮れるにつれて、通りの人出はますます増えていった。

examples.en: As I've grown older, I've come to see the hardships my parents went through that I couldn't understand when I was young.
examples.ja: 年齢を重ねるにつれて、若い頃には分からなかった親の苦労が見えてきた。

examples.en: As the yen continues to weaken, the number of tourists from abroad is surging.
examples.ja: 円安が進むにつれ、海外からの観光客が急増している。

records.formation: V辞書形 / N + につれ(て)
records.meaning: as …, gradually …; in proportion as …
records.nuance: Describes proportional change: as one thing changes, another changes along with it step by step. Both clauses express a gradual change, so it does not suit one-off events or a request or intention in the second clause.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に伴って: more formal, and can link a single event to its consequence (移転に伴い); につれて needs ongoing, gradual change
〜にしたがって: nearly the same for proportional change, but can also mean 'in accordance with' rules or instructions
〜とともに: broader 'along with / at the same time as', including simple coincidence or 'together with a person'

similar: 〜に伴って: more formal, and can link a single event to its consequence (移転に伴い); につれて needs ongoing, gradual change
〜にしたがって: nearly the same for proportional change, but can also mean 'in accordance with' rules or instructions
〜とともに: broader 'along with / at the same time as', including simple coincidence or 'together with a person'

audit.why: Remove ない before adding んがために (勝たんがために, not 勝たないんがために); the stated する → せんがために exception remains correct.
