audit.why: 普通形 is too broad: verbs can connect directly in the dictionary form, but the rule does not freely accept all plain verb or adjective forms.

examples.ja: この新型電池は、電気自動車への応用にとどまらず、家庭用蓄電池としての活用も期待されている。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + にとどまらず
records.meaning: not stopping at …; going beyond …
records.nuance: Formal, common in news and reports. Says the scope of an effect, activity or popularity extends past X, often followed by 〜にも / 〜まで.

relatedReferences.text: 〜のみならず: 'not only'; more literary, adds rather than extends
〜だけでなく: plain 'not only'
〜に限らず: 'not limited to'; about category membership

similar: 〜のみならず: 'not only'; more literary, adds rather than extends
〜だけでなく: plain 'not only'
〜に限らず: 'not limited to'; about category membership

examples.en: We have done all the preparation we could. Now all that is left is to wait for the result.
examples.ja: やれるだけの準備はしてきた。あとはただ結果を待つのみだ。

examples.en: Right now, all we can do is pray for the safety of the missing climbers.
examples.ja: 行方不明の登山者たちの無事を、今はただ祈るのみです。

examples.en: In this event, the only thing that counts is the recorded result.
examples.ja: この競技で評価されるのは、ただ記録のみである。

records.formation: ただ + N / V辞書形 + のみ (〜のみだ / 〜のみである)
records.meaning: only …; solely …; nothing but …
records.nuance: A formal, written equivalent of ただ〜だけ, common in speeches, news and resolute statements such as ただ祈るのみだ. It stresses that there is nothing else to do or nothing else involved.

relatedReferences.text: ただ〜だけ: the everyday 'only', with no formal tone
〜のみならず: 'not only … but also', adding rather than limiting
〜に尽きる: 'it all comes down to …', used to sum up or praise

similar: ただ〜だけ: the everyday 'only', with no formal tone
〜のみならず: 'not only … but also', adding rather than limiting
〜に尽きる: 'it all comes down to …', used to sum up or praise

examples.en: I'm sorry to disturb you on your day off, but could I have a moment of your time?
examples.ja: お休みのところを申し訳ありませんが、少しお時間よろしいでしょうか。

examples.en: Thank you for coming today despite the bad weather.
examples.ja: 本日はお足元の悪いところをお越しいただき、ありがとうございます。

examples.en: The man was restrained by a security guard as he tried to slip merchandise into his bag.
examples.ja: 男は商品をかばんに入れようとしたところを、警備員に取り押さえられた。

records.formation: Vている / Vた / いA / なAな / Nの + ところを
records.meaning: at a time when … (despite the inconvenience; caught in the act)
records.nuance: Mostly appears in polite apologies and thanks (お忙しいところを) acknowledging the listener's inconvenience; also in news-style 'caught in the act' sentences (〜ところを見つかる／取り押さえられる).

relatedReferences.text: 〜ところに: something arrives at that moment, rather than acting on it
〜のに: plain 'even though', no polite framing
〜にもかかわらず: formal 'despite', for facts in general

similar: 〜ところに: something arrives at that moment, rather than acting on it
〜のに: plain 'even though', no polite framing
〜にもかかわらず: formal 'despite', for facts in general

examples.en: Studying abroad let me see my own country from the outside.
examples.ja: 留学を通して、自分の国を外から見ることができた。

examples.en: This region is mild all year round and never short of tourists.
examples.ja: この地域は一年を通じて温暖で、観光客が絶えない。

examples.en: The negotiations were conducted through lawyers, and the parties never met face to face.
examples.ja: 交渉は弁護士を通じて行われ、当事者同士が顔を合わせることはなかった。

records.formation: N + を通じて / N + を通して
records.meaning: through … (as a means or go-between); throughout … (a whole period or area)
records.nuance: Two uses: the medium or go-between through which something happens, and an unbroken span of time or space (一年を通じて). The two are largely interchangeable; を通して leans a little more toward a means used on purpose, を通じて sounds slightly more formal and suits channels and networks (メディアを通じて).

relatedReferences.text: 〜によって: general 'by means of / because of', without the sense of passing through a medium
〜にわたって: stresses how widely a range extends (三日間にわたって), not continuity through it
〜を経て: passing through stages or places in a process

similar: 〜によって: general 'by means of / because of', without the sense of passing through a medium
〜にわたって: stresses how widely a range extends (三日間にわたって), not continuity through it
〜を経て: passing through stages or places in a process

examples.en: Only three days left until the deadline. I can't afford to take it easy.
examples.ja: 締め切りまであと三日だ。のんびりしてはいられない。

examples.en: With rivals launching one new product after another, we can't just stand by and watch.
examples.ja: 他社が次々と新製品を出している以上、うちも黙って見てはいられない。

examples.en: I can't keep dwelling on the mistake forever. The next match is already next week.
examples.ja: 失敗をいつまでも引きずってはいられない。次の試合はもう来週だ。

records.formation: Vて形 + はいられない (casual: 〜ちゃいられない)
records.meaning: cannot afford to keep …ing; can't just …
records.nuance: Conveys urgency: the situation does not allow one to stay in a state such as waiting, relaxing or worrying, and it often leads into a resolve to act.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずにはいられない: can't help doing (compelled to act, the opposite direction)
〜わけにはいかない: can't do it for social or moral reasons
〜ている場合ではない: 'this is no time to …', a blunt judgement that the situation rules it out

similar: 〜ずにはいられない: can't help doing (compelled to act, the opposite direction)
〜わけにはいかない: can't do it for social or moral reasons
〜ている場合ではない: 'this is no time to …', a blunt judgement that the situation rules it out

examples.en: After three years of research, they finally succeeded in developing a new material.
examples.ja: 三年に及ぶ研究の末に、ついに新しい素材の開発に成功した。

examples.en: After talking it over with my family many times, I decided to move to the countryside.
examples.ja: 家族と何度も話し合った末に、地方への移住を決めた。

examples.en: After the game dragged into extra time, the home team pulled off a dramatic win.
examples.ja: 延長戦までもつれ込んだ末に、地元チームが劇的な勝利を収めた。

records.formation: Vた形 + 末(に) / Nの + 末(に)
records.meaning: after (a long process of) …; at the end of …
records.nuance: Presents a result reached only after long effort, deliberation or struggle; the outcome can be good or bad. Slightly formal, common in news and narrative.

relatedReferences.text: 〜あげく: after a frustrating process, usually a bad result and the speaker's exasperation; 末に is more neutral
〜結果: 'as a result of', a plain consequence with no long struggle implied
〜てはじめて: 'only after …', stressing that a realisation needed that experience

similar: 〜あげく: after a frustrating process, usually a bad result and the speaker's exasperation; 末に is more neutral
〜結果: 'as a result of', a plain consequence with no long struggle implied
〜てはじめて: 'only after …', stressing that a realisation needed that experience

examples.en: Thanks to the internet, you can tour museums all over the world without leaving home.
examples.ja: ネットのおかげで、自宅に居ながらにして世界中の美術館を見て回れる。

examples.en: The victim's family, in tears, described what happened on the day of the accident.
examples.ja: 被害者の家族は、涙ながらに事故当日の様子を語った。

examples.en: Every person is born with equal rights.
examples.ja: 人は誰でも、生まれながらにして平等な権利を持っている。

records.formation: N / Vます形 + ながらに（して）　※「生まれながら」「涙ながら」「居ながら」「昔ながら」など限られた語
records.meaning: while still …; as one is (unchanged); from the state of …
records.nuance: Written and somewhat fixed. Means an action or state occurs while a condition stays unchanged; mostly found in set phrases such as 生まれながらにして, 涙ながらに and 居ながらにして.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ながら（も）: concessive 'although'; works with many more words
〜まま: everyday 'while remaining in that state'
昔ながらの: adjectival form 'as in the old days, traditional'

similar: 〜ながら（も）: concessive 'although'; works with many more words
〜まま: everyday 'while remaining in that state'
昔ながらの: adjectival form 'as in the old days, traditional'

examples.en: This film isn't just for children; adults can thoroughly enjoy it too.
examples.ja: この映画は子どもに限らず、大人が見ても十分楽しめる内容になっている。

examples.en: These days cashless payments are spreading rapidly, not only in cities but in rural areas as well.
examples.ja: 最近は都市部に限らず、地方でもキャッシュレス決済が急速に広がっている。

examples.en: Lack of sleep is a serious problem not only for students preparing for exams but for working people too.
examples.ja: 睡眠不足は、受験生に限らず、働く世代にとっても深刻な問題だ。

records.formation: N + に限らず
records.meaning: not limited to …; not just … but more widely
records.nuance: Presents X as a typical case and extends the statement to a wider group, often followed by も, 誰でも or 幅広く. Neutral to formal; common in news and advertising.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでなく: plain 'not only … but also'; に限らず implies a broader category
〜はもちろん: X is the obvious case, included as a matter of course
〜に限って: singles out one case, the opposite direction

similar: 〜だけでなく: plain 'not only … but also'; に限らず implies a broader category
〜はもちろん: X is the obvious case, included as a matter of course
〜に限って: singles out one case, the opposite direction

examples.en: This region's festival is popular with visitors from overseas, not to mention local residents.
examples.ja: この地域の祭りは、地元の住民はもとより、海外からの観光客にも人気がある。

examples.cloze: ドライバーはもとより
examples.en: Safe driving is expected of every driver, not just professional ones.
examples.ja: 安全運転は、プロのドライバーはもとより、すべての運転者に求められる。

examples.en: This product is highly rated for its refined design, not to mention its performance.
examples.ja: 本製品は、性能はもとより、洗練されたデザインでも高く評価されている。

records.formation: N + はもとより、〜も
records.meaning: not to mention …; to say nothing of … (formal)
records.nuance: The formal, written counterpart of はもちろん: X is self-evident and Y extends the claim. Common in speeches, news and official or corporate writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はもちろん: same meaning, more conversational
〜はおろか: 'let alone' with a negative; even the easier thing is not achieved
〜のみならず: formal 'not only … but also', without the 'obviously' nuance

similar: 〜はもちろん: same meaning, more conversational
〜はおろか: 'let alone' with a negative; even the easier thing is not achieved
〜のみならず: formal 'not only … but also', without the 'obviously' nuance

examples.en: A cut this small isn't worth going to the hospital for.
examples.ja: この程度の傷なら、病院に行くまでもない。

examples.en: Needless to say, safety comes before everything.
examples.ja: 言うまでもなく、安全はすべてに優先する。

examples.en: The result is obvious, so there's probably no need to bother checking.
examples.ja: 結果は分かりきっているので、わざわざ確認するまでもないだろう。

records.formation: V辞書形 + までもない / までもなく
records.meaning: there is no need to …; it goes without saying
records.nuance: Says an action is unnecessary because the matter is too obvious or too minor. Common in writing and formal speech, and in the set phrase 言うまでもない / 言うまでもなく.

relatedReferences.text: 〜には及ばない: 'no need to', more formal and often used to politely decline an offer
〜ことはない: 'no need to', conversational and reassuring toward the listener
〜までだ: 'will simply …', a statement of resolve, not of unnecessity

similar: 〜には及ばない: 'no need to', more formal and often used to politely decline an offer
〜ことはない: 'no need to', conversational and reassuring toward the listener
〜までだ: 'will simply …', a statement of resolve, not of unnecessity

examples.en: I was so wrapped up in work that I neglected time with my family.
examples.ja: 仕事にかまけて、家族との時間をおろそかにしていた。

examples.en: I kept putting off my homework because I was absorbed in games, and summer vacation ended.
examples.ja: ゲームにかまけて宿題を後回しにしていたら、夏休みが終わってしまった。

examples.en: I've let being busy take over, and I haven't been to the gym in half a year.
examples.ja: 忙しさにかまけて、もう半年もジムに行っていない。

records.formation: N + にかまけて
records.meaning: too absorbed in … (neglecting something else)
records.nuance: Expresses regret or criticism that one thing took all one's attention so that something important was neglected. Often followed by a negative or おろそかにする.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にかこつけて: 'using X as a pretext'
〜に追われて: 'pressed by'; not by choice, so less blame
〜に夢中になって: 'engrossed in'; neutral, with no sense of neglecting something else

similar: 〜にかこつけて: 'using X as a pretext'
〜に追われて: 'pressed by'; not by choice, so less blame
〜に夢中になって: 'engrossed in'; neutral, with no sense of neglecting something else

examples.en: In my experience, this kind of trouble tends to happen at the start of the week.
examples.ja: 経験上、こういうトラブルは週明けに起きることが多い。

examples.en: Even if there is no legal problem, that does not mean it is ethically acceptable.
examples.ja: 法律上は問題がなくても、倫理的に許されるとは限らない。

examples.en: For safety reasons, entry to this area is prohibited.
examples.ja: 安全上の理由から、このエリアへの立ち入りは禁止されています。

records.formation: N + 上 / N + 上の + N (経験上・法律上・安全上・立場上・健康上・仕事上)
records.meaning: from the standpoint of …; in terms of …; for … reasons
records.nuance: A compact suffix, read じょう, that frames a statement from a particular field or point of view. Formal and written in feel, but set phrases like 経験上 and 立場上 are common in speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜の面で／〜の点で: 'in terms of', more neutral and flexible
〜からすると: judging from a viewpoint, often a personal assessment
〜的に: '…-ly / -wise', looser and more conversational

similar: 〜の面で／〜の点で: 'in terms of', more neutral and flexible
〜からすると: judging from a viewpoint, often a personal assessment
〜的に: '…-ly / -wise', looser and more conversational

examples.en: Even experts cannot accurately predict future stock prices.
examples.ja: 専門家といえども、将来の株価を正確に予測することはできない。

examples.en: However small a company may be, it is still responsible for obeying the law.
examples.ja: いかに小さな会社といえども、法律を守る責任があることに変わりはない。

examples.en: Not even a single yen of tax money may be wasted.
examples.ja: たとえ一円といえども、税金を無駄に使うことは許されない。

records.formation: N / 普通形 + といえども（いかに・たとえ 〜といえども）
records.meaning: even …; even granting …
records.nuance: Concedes a status or fact, then states that the usual expectation still does not apply. Stiff, written style, common in editorials and formal speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とはいえ: 'although', concedes a fact; slightly less stiff
〜ても: plain 'even if', everyday register
〜にしても: 'even granting', more conversational

similar: 〜とはいえ: 'although', concedes a fact; slightly less stiff
〜ても: plain 'even if', everyday register
〜にしても: 'even granting', more conversational

examples.en: I was so busy I didn't even have time to eat lunch.
examples.ja: 忙しすぎて、昼ご飯を食べる時間すらなかった。

examples.en: That illness is said to be hard to diagnose even for specialist doctors.
examples.ja: その病気は、専門の医師ですら診断が難しいと言われている。

examples.en: Quite a few people have lived somewhere for years without even knowing their neighbour's name.
examples.ja: 長年住んでいるのに、隣の人の名前すら知らないという人も少なくない。

records.formation: N(+助詞) + すら ; Nで + すら ; Vます形 + すら + しない
records.meaning: even … (citing an extreme example)
records.nuance: Cites an extreme or minimal case to imply that everything else follows, usually with a negative or critical sense. More written and emphatic than さえ; frequent in news, essays and serious conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜さえ: nearly the same and more common; さえ also forms 'if only' (〜さえ〜ば), which すら cannot
〜まで: 'even' that adds to an extent, often surprising rather than minimal
〜だに: literary 'even', mostly with 想像する or 夢にも

similar: 〜さえ: nearly the same and more common; さえ also forms 'if only' (〜さえ〜ば), which すら cannot
〜まで: 'even' that adds to an extent, often surprising rather than minimal
〜だに: literary 'even', mostly with 想像する or 夢にも

examples.en: This hot-spring town is lively with tourists on weekdays, not to mention weekends.
examples.ja: この温泉街は、週末はもちろん、平日も観光客でにぎわっている。

examples.en: Apparently that interpreter speaks Chinese and Spanish, not to mention English.
examples.ja: あの通訳は、英語はもちろん、中国語やスペイン語も話せるらしい。

examples.cloze: 試合の日はもちろんのこと
examples.en: Many residents visit the new stadium on days with no game, to say nothing of match days.
examples.ja: 新しいスタジアムには、試合の日はもちろんのこと、試合のない日も多くの市民が訪れている。

records.formation: N + はもちろん(のこと)、〜も
records.meaning: not to mention …; to say nothing of …
records.nuance: X is the obvious case that goes without saying, and Y is added as an extension. Neutral and very common in both speech and writing; はもちろんのこと is a little more formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はもとより: same meaning, more formal and written
〜に限らず: stresses a wider scope rather than an obvious case
〜ばかりか: adds a surprising or escalating second element

similar: 〜はもとより: same meaning, more formal and written
〜に限らず: stresses a wider scope rather than an obvious case
〜ばかりか: adds a surprising or escalating second element

examples.en: Just because I overslept, I was late for an important interview.
examples.ja: 寝坊したばかりに、大事な面接に遅れてしまった。

examples.cloze: 使い回していたばかりに
examples.en: Simply because I had reused my password, several of my accounts were hijacked.
examples.ja: パスワードを使い回していたばかりに、複数のアカウントが乗っ取られた。

examples.en: Because I was so eager to get home early, I skipped the checks and made a big mistake.
examples.ja: 早く帰りたいばかりに、確認を怠って大きなミスをしてしまった。

records.formation: V普通形(主にた形) / い形容詞普通形 / な形容詞語幹な・である / Nである + ばかりに
records.meaning: simply because …; just because of … (with a bad result, regret)
records.nuance: Blames a single cause for an unwanted outcome, carrying regret or frustration. 〜たいばかりに means 'only because one wanted … so badly', explaining an extreme effort or a rash act.

relatedReferences.text: 〜せいで: blames a cause for a bad result, without the 'that one thing alone' sense of regret
〜ために: neutral cause or purpose
〜おかげで: cause of a good result

similar: 〜せいで: blames a cause for a bad result, without the 'that one thing alone' sense of regret
〜ために: neutral cause or purpose
〜おかげで: cause of a good result

examples.en: I am deeply honored to receive such a prestigious award.
examples.ja: このような栄誉ある賞をいただき、光栄の至りでございます。

examples.en: Looking back, going to a job interview with flashy hair in my student days was a youthful indiscretion.
examples.ja: 学生時代に派手な髪色で面接に行ったのは、今思えば若気の至りだった。

examples.en: I misread your name in front of so many people, and I am thoroughly embarrassed.
examples.ja: 大勢の前でお名前を読み間違えてしまい、赤面の至りです。

records.formation: N（光栄・感激・赤面・若気 など） + の至り
records.meaning: the utmost …; deeply (honored, embarrassed, etc.)
records.nuance: Highly formal and ceremonial, used in greetings, acceptance speeches and apologies to express the speaker's own feeling. Largely limited to set phrases; 若気の至り ('youthful indiscretion') is the one heard in everyday talk.

relatedReferences.text: 〜の極み: takes a wider range of nouns, positive or negative, and appears in ordinary writing
〜極まりない: follows a Na-adjective (失礼極まりない) and is used mainly for criticism
〜に堪えない: formal 'cannot help feeling' (感謝に堪えない), also ceremonial

similar: 〜の極み: takes a wider range of nouns, positive or negative, and appears in ordinary writing
〜極まりない: follows a Na-adjective (失礼極まりない) and is used mainly for criticism
〜に堪えない: formal 'cannot help feeling' (感謝に堪えない), also ceremonial

examples.cloze: 考えすぎるきらいがある
examples.en: He tends to be overly pessimistic about things, but that makes him all the more thorough in his preparation.
examples.ja: 彼は物事を悲観的に考えすぎるきらいがあるが、そのぶん準備は周到だ。

examples.cloze: 信用していないきらいがある
examples.en: This director's films explain too much and tend to show little trust in the audience's imagination.
examples.ja: この監督の作品は説明が多く、観客の想像力を信用していないきらいがある。

examples.cloze: 優先するきらいがある
examples.en: Japanese meetings are said to have a tendency to put everyone's agreement ahead of reaching a conclusion.
examples.ja: 日本の会議は、結論よりも全員の合意を優先するきらいがあると言われる。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vない形 / Vている + きらいがある ; Nの + きらいがある
records.meaning: have a (bad) tendency to …; be inclined to …
records.nuance: Points out an undesirable habit or tendency in a person, group or work, in a measured, critical tone. Written and formal, common in commentary and reviews; not used for good traits.

relatedReferences.text: 〜傾向がある: neutral 'tend to'; can describe good, bad or statistical trends
〜がちだ: 'apt to', more conversational and about frequency rather than character
〜嫌いだ: simply 'dislike'; unrelated despite the same kanji

similar: 〜傾向がある: neutral 'tend to'; can describe good, bad or statistical trends
〜がちだ: 'apt to', more conversational and about frequency rather than character
〜嫌いだ: simply 'dislike'; unrelated despite the same kanji

examples.en: In a situation where prices keep rising, many households are being forced to economize.
examples.ja: 物価が上がり続ける状況にあって、多くの家庭が節約を強いられている。

examples.en: Even in a harsh business environment, the company did not cut its investment in research and development.
examples.ja: 厳しい経営環境にあっても、同社は研究開発への投資を減らさなかった。

examples.en: In today's world, overflowing with information, the ability to judge what to believe is indispensable.
examples.ja: 情報があふれる現代にあっては、何を信じるかを見極める力が欠かせない。

records.formation: N + にあって（は / も）
records.meaning: in (a situation, era); being in …
records.nuance: Formal and written. Stresses that one is in a special situation, period or position; にあっては shows what follows from it, にあっても what holds despite it.

relatedReferences.text: 〜において: neutral formal 'in / at', without the sense of a special situation
〜に際して: 'on the occasion of', tied to a single event
〜の中で: plain 'amid'

similar: 〜において: neutral formal 'in / at', without the sense of a special situation
〜に際して: 'on the occasion of', tied to a single event
〜の中で: plain 'amid'

examples.en: When the match ended, the players waved to the crowd still in their mud-covered uniforms.
examples.ja: 試合が終わると、選手たちは泥まみれのユニフォームのまま観客に手を振った。

examples.en: Moving house in midsummer left everyone drenched in sweat.
examples.ja: 真夏の引っ越し作業で、全員が汗まみれになった。

examples.en: Hooked on gambling, before he knew it he was living buried in debt.
examples.ja: ギャンブルにのめり込み、気づけば借金まみれの生活になっていた。

records.formation: N + まみれ（泥・汗・血・油・ほこり・借金 など）; 〜まみれになる / 〜まみれの + N
records.meaning: smeared all over with …; covered in …
records.nuance: Describes a surface thickly coated with something unpleasant, usually liquid or fine particles. Used figuratively for being buried in debt or scandal. Carries a sense of mess or distaste.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だらけ: 'full of', many scattered items (mistakes, scratches), not only a surface coating
〜ずくめ: 'entirely, nothing but', often neutral or positive (黒ずくめ, いいことずくめ)

similar: 〜だらけ: 'full of', many scattered items (mistakes, scratches), not only a surface coating
〜ずくめ: 'entirely, nothing but', often neutral or positive (黒ずくめ, いいことずくめ)

examples.en: As society ages, the shortage of care workers is becoming serious.
examples.ja: 高齢化に伴って、介護の担い手不足が深刻になっている。

examples.en: Due to the relocation of our head office, our main phone number will change from next month.
examples.ja: 本社移転に伴い、来月から代表電話番号が変更になります。

examples.en: There are fears that supply may not keep pace with the rise in electricity demand that comes with higher temperatures.
examples.ja: 気温の上昇に伴う電力需要の増加に、供給が追いつかない恐れがある。

records.formation: N / V辞書形(の) + に伴って / に伴い / に伴うN
records.meaning: accompanying …; along with …; as … changes
records.nuance: Formal: when one change or event occurs, another follows from or with it. Common in news, official notices and business writing, and unlike につれて it can tie a single event to its consequence (移転に伴い).

relatedReferences.text: 〜につれて: gradual, proportional change and more conversational; に伴って also covers one-off events
〜とともに: broad 'along with', including 'together with a person'; less tied to cause and consequence
〜にしたがって: 'as …' for proportional change, or 'in accordance with' instructions

similar: 〜につれて: gradual, proportional change and more conversational; に伴って also covers one-off events
〜とともに: broad 'along with', including 'together with a person'; less tied to cause and consequence
〜にしたがって: 'as …' for proportional change, or 'in accordance with' instructions

examples.en: It's always when I'm in a hurry that the train is late or I hit every red light.
examples.ja: 急いでいる時に限って、電車が遅れたり信号に引っかかったりするんだよね。

examples.en: It's always the day I go out without an umbrella that it starts pouring in the evening.
examples.ja: 傘を持たずに出かけた日に限って、夕方から土砂降りになる。

examples.en: Many parents convince themselves that 'my child, of all children, would never do such a thing.'
examples.ja: 「うちの子に限って、そんなことをするはずがない」と思い込んでしまう親は多い。

records.formation: N + に限って
records.meaning: … of all (times, people); precisely when …; only … in particular
records.nuance: Mostly used with frustration: something bad happens at exactly the worst moment (急いでいる時に限って). With a negative, it expresses trust that a particular person would never do something (うちの子に限って…ない).

relatedReferences.text: 〜に限り: formal 'limited to/only' in notices, with no frustration
〜に限らず: 'not limited to', widens the scope instead of singling out
〜だけ: plain 'only', without the ironic 'of all times' sense

similar: 〜に限り: formal 'limited to/only' in notices, with no frustration
〜に限らず: 'not limited to', widens the scope instead of singling out
〜だけ: plain 'only', without the ironic 'of all times' sense

examples.en: Whether the factory survives will depend on how the coming negotiations go.
examples.ja: 今後の交渉のいかんで、工場の存続が決まる。

examples.cloze: 検査結果のいかんによっては
examples.en: Depending on the test results, surgery may be necessary in some cases.
examples.ja: 検査結果のいかんによっては、手術が必要になる場合もあります。

examples.cloze: 説明のいかんによっては
examples.en: Depending on how the authorities explain it, the residents' opposition movement could spread even further.
examples.ja: 行政の説明のいかんによっては、住民の反対運動がさらに広がりかねない。

records.formation: N(の) + いかんで / いかんによって / いかんによっては / N + いかんだ
records.meaning: depending on …; in some cases, depending on …
records.nuance: A stiff, written equivalent of 次第; いかんによっては highlights that in certain cases a particular, often unwelcome, outcome may follow. Used in official notices, contracts and news.
records.pattern: 〜いかんで／〜いかんによっては

relatedReferences.text: 〜次第で: same meaning, less formal
〜によって(は): neutral 'depending on', fine in conversation
〜いかんにかかわらず: the opposite, 'regardless of'

similar: 〜次第で: same meaning, less formal
〜によって(は): neutral 'depending on', fine in conversation
〜いかんにかかわらず: the opposite, 'regardless of'

examples.en: Now that it's March, the sunlight has become quite spring-like.
examples.ja: 三月に入り、日差しもすっかり春めいてきた。

examples.en: The boss said it in a joking tone, but his eyes weren't smiling.
examples.ja: 上司は冗談めいた口調で言ったが、目は笑っていなかった。

examples.en: The poster carried only one cryptic sentence, and it became a talking point on social media.
examples.ja: ポスターには謎めいた一文だけが書かれ、SNSで話題になった。

records.formation: N + めく（春めく・冗談めく・謎めく・皮肉めく など）; 〜めいた + N / 〜めいている
records.meaning: take on the air of …; show signs of …; -ish
records.nuance: Says something has the feel of the noun without fully being it. Works with a limited set of nouns, especially seasons and words like joke, riddle or irony. Literary but common in set expressions.

relatedReferences.text: 〜らしい: 'typical of, genuinely like', implies the real thing rather than a hint of it
〜っぽい: casual '-ish', productive with almost any noun
〜じみる: 'smacks of', usually negative (子どもじみた, 年寄りじみた)

similar: 〜らしい: 'typical of, genuinely like', implies the real thing rather than a hint of it
〜っぽい: casual '-ish', productive with almost any noun
〜じみる: 'smacks of', usually negative (子どもじみた, 年寄りじみた)

examples.cloze: 教えてくれたばかりか
examples.en: The shop clerk not only told me the way but even went to the trouble of taking me to my destination.
examples.ja: その店員は道を教えてくれたばかりか、わざわざ目的地まで案内してくれた。

examples.en: Because of the typhoon, not only did the trains stop, but some areas also lost power.
examples.ja: 台風の影響で、電車が止まったばかりか、一部の地域では停電も発生した。

examples.en: This medicine is not only ineffective; reportedly some people even fall ill from its side effects.
examples.ja: この薬は効果がないばかりか、かえって副作用で体調を崩す人もいるという。

records.formation: V普通形 / い形容詞普通形 / な形容詞語幹な・である / N + ばかりか、〜も・まで・さえ
records.meaning: not only … but (even) …
records.nuance: Adds a second, more surprising or extreme point to the first, for good or bad outcomes alike. Somewhat formal; the second clause cannot be a request, command or invitation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでなく: neutral 'not only … but also', without the escalation
〜ばかりでなく: close, slightly less emphatic
〜どころか: reverses expectation ('far from X, actually Y')

similar: 〜だけでなく: neutral 'not only … but also', without the escalation
〜ばかりでなく: close, slightly less emphatic
〜どころか: reverses expectation ('far from X, actually Y')

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ざるを得ない (認めない → 認めざるを得ない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.en: With raw material costs still soaring, our shop has no choice but to revise its prices from next month.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ざるを得ない (認めない → 認めざるを得ない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: 原材料費の高騰が続き、当店も来月から価格を改定せざるを得ない状況です。

examples.cloze: 中止せざるを得なかった
examples.en: With a typhoon approaching, the organizers had no choice but to cancel the event.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ざるを得ない (認めない → 認めざるを得ない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: 台風の接近により、主催者はイベントを中止せざるを得なかった。

examples.en: With this much evidence against him, he will have no choice but to admit the facts.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding ざるを得ない (認めない → 認めざるを得ない); attaching it to the full negative form gives an incorrect connection.

examples.ja: これだけ証拠がそろっていては、彼も事実を認めざるを得ないだろう。

records.formation: Vない形から「ない」を除く + ざるを得ない（する→せざるを得ない）
records.meaning: cannot avoid doing; have no choice but to
records.nuance: Formal; the speaker reluctantly does something because circumstances leave no alternative. Common in news, business announcements and editorials.

relatedReferences.text: 〜しかない: conversational 'there's nothing for it but', less sense of reluctance
〜ないわけにはいかない: obligation for social or moral reasons
〜ずにはいられない: an irresistible inner urge, not pressure from circumstances

similar: 〜しかない: conversational 'there's nothing for it but', less sense of reluctance
〜ないわけにはいかない: obligation for social or moral reasons
〜ずにはいられない: an irresistible inner urge, not pressure from circumstances

examples.en: Just because something is expensive doesn't mean it is good quality.
examples.ja: 値段が高いからといって、品質がいいとは限らない。

examples.cloze: 失敗したからといって
examples.en: Failing once doesn't mean you have to give up on your dream.
examples.ja: 一度失敗したからといって、夢をあきらめる必要はない。

examples.en: Working from home doesn't mean it's fine to spend all day in your pajamas.
examples.ja: 在宅勤務だからといって、一日中パジャマで過ごしていいわけではない。

records.formation: 普通形 + からといって (+ 〜わけではない / 〜とは限らない / 〜てはいけない)
records.meaning: just because … does not mean …
records.nuance: Rejects the assumption that a reason automatically leads to a certain conclusion; almost always followed by a negation or partial denial. Used in conversation and argument, often when giving advice.

relatedReferences.text: 〜からって: casual spoken contraction of the same pattern
〜としても: 'even if', a hypothetical concession
〜わけではない: the ending that typically completes からといって, not a substitute for it

similar: 〜からって: casual spoken contraction of the same pattern
〜としても: 'even if', a hypothetical concession
〜わけではない: the ending that typically completes からといって, not a substitute for it

audit.why: The ichidan alternative attaches まい after removing ない from the negative form (食べまい), not after the complete ない-form.

examples.en: The food at that restaurant was awful. I made up my mind never to go there again.

audit.why: The ichidan alternative attaches まい after removing ない from the negative form (食べまい), not after the complete ない-form.

examples.ja: あの店の料理はひどかった。もう二度と行くまいと心に決めた。

examples.en: With rain this light, the match probably won't be called off.

audit.why: The ichidan alternative attaches まい after removing ない from the negative form (食べまい), not after the complete ない-form.

examples.ja: この程度の雨なら、試合が中止になることはあるまい。

examples.en: Not wanting to worry the people around her, she told no one that she was feeling unwell.

audit.why: The ichidan alternative attaches まい after removing ない from the negative form (食べまい), not after the complete ない-form.

examples.ja: 周りに心配をかけまいと、彼女は体調が悪いことを誰にも話さなかった。

records.formation: V辞書形 + まい（一段動詞は Vない形の「ない」を除いた形 + まい も可: 食べまい；する → するまい / すまい / しまい；来る → 来るまい / 来まい（こまい））
records.meaning: probably not (negative guess); will not, determined not to (negative resolve)
records.nuance: A literary negative that works like 〜ないだろう (guess) or 〜ないつもりだ (resolve). Common in writing and set phrases such as 二度と〜まい and 〜まいと思う; it sounds firm and a little old-fashioned in speech.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ないだろう: everyday negative guess, softer and more conversational
〜ないつもりだ: everyday negative intention, without the literary firmness
〜ではあるまいか: 'isn't it perhaps …?', a tentative positive guess despite the negative form

similar: 〜ないだろう: everyday negative guess, softer and more conversational
〜ないつもりだ: everyday negative intention, without the literary firmness
〜ではあるまいか: 'isn't it perhaps …?', a tentative positive guess despite the negative form

examples.en: Once the year-end comes around, every department store is packed with shoppers.
examples.ja: 年末ともなると、デパートはどこも買い物客でごった返す。

examples.en: Apparently, once you become company president, work calls keep coming even on your days off.
examples.ja: 社長ともなれば、休日でも仕事の電話が鳴りやまないらしい。

examples.en: When you have three children, getting ready every morning is like a battle.
examples.ja: 子どもが三人ともなると、毎朝の支度はまるで戦争のようだ。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + ともなると／ともなれば
records.meaning: once it comes to (a higher level) …; when it reaches the point of …
records.nuance: Formal to neutral. Raises a situation, age or status that is a step above the ordinary and states what naturally follows at that level.

relatedReferences.text: 〜となると: plainer 'if it comes to'; no strong sense of reaching a higher stage
〜ともあろう: also cites status, but to criticise unworthy behaviour
〜になると: neutral 'when it becomes'

similar: 〜となると: plainer 'if it comes to'; no strong sense of reaching a higher stage
〜ともあろう: also cites status, but to criticise unworthy behaviour
〜になると: neutral 'when it becomes'

examples.cloze: 悲観するには当たらない
examples.en: Just because the rookie lost the first match, there is no reason to be pessimistic.
examples.ja: 新人が初戦で負けたからといって、悲観するには当たらない。

examples.en: Experts say price rises of this size have happened many times before and are nothing to be surprised about.
examples.ja: この程度の値上がりは過去にも何度もあり、驚くには当たらないと専門家は話す。

examples.en: The company's position is that the clerk acted according to the rules and does not deserve criticism.
examples.ja: 店員の対応は規則どおりで、非難には当たらないというのが会社の見解だ。

records.formation: V辞書形 + には当たらない / N(する名詞) + には当たらない
records.meaning: there is no need to …; (a reaction) is not warranted
records.nuance: Formal and evaluative: the speaker calmly judges that a reaction such as surprise, alarm, praise or blame is not called for. Typical partners are 驚く, 悲観する, 嘆く, 非難する, 賞賛する; common in commentary, editorials and expert remarks.

relatedReferences.text: 〜までもない: no need because it is too obvious or trivial to bother; には当たらない says the reaction itself is unwarranted
〜には及ばない: no need to go to that trouble (often a polite 'don't bother'), or 'is no match for'
〜ことはない: everyday 'there's no need to', reassuring and conversational

similar: 〜までもない: no need because it is too obvious or trivial to bother; には当たらない says the reaction itself is unwarranted
〜には及ばない: no need to go to that trouble (often a polite 'don't bother'), or 'is no match for'
〜ことはない: everyday 'there's no need to', reassuring and conversational

examples.en: Now that I have taken it on, I intend to see it through to the end.
examples.ja: 引き受けた上は、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げるつもりだ。

examples.en: Now that it has come to this, there is nothing for it but to tell the whole truth.
examples.ja: こうなった上は、正直にすべてを話すしかない。

examples.en: Once the contract is signed, the deadline must be met whatever the circumstances.
examples.ja: 契約を結んだ上は、どんな事情があっても期日は守らなければならない。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 + 上は
records.meaning: now that …; since … (so one must)
records.nuance: Stiff and formal: now that a situation or decision is fixed, the speaker accepts what must follow. The second clause states resolve or obligation (〜しかない, 〜なければならない, 〜つもりだ).

relatedReferences.text: 〜以上(は): same 'since', more common and also used in logical argument
〜からには: same, more conversational and emotional
〜上で: 'after doing', with no sense of resolve

similar: 〜以上(は): same 'since', more common and also used in logical argument
〜からには: same, more conversational and emotional
〜上で: 'after doing', with no sense of resolve

examples.cloze: 荷造りやら役所の手続きやら
examples.en: Before the move, what with packing and paperwork at the city office, I was dizzyingly busy.
examples.ja: 引っ越しの前は、荷造りやら役所の手続きやらで目が回るほど忙しかった。

examples.cloze: うれしいやらほっとするやら
examples.en: When I heard I'd passed, I was so happy and relieved that tears came to my eyes.
examples.ja: 合格の知らせを聞いて、うれしいやらほっとするやらで涙が出てきた。

examples.cloze: 止まるやら道路は渋滞するやら
examples.en: With the weekend's heavy snow, what with trains stopping and roads jammed, the whole city was in chaos.
examples.ja: 週末の大雪で、電車は止まるやら道路は渋滞するやらで、街中が大混乱だった。

records.formation: N / V辞書形 / い形容詞 + やら、N / V辞書形 / い形容詞 + やら（で）
records.meaning: what with … and …; … and … and so on
records.nuance: Lists a couple of examples from a larger jumble, suggesting the situation was hectic, overwhelming or full of mixed feelings. Used in conversation and light writing; it often ends in で大変だった or a similar comment.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とか〜とか: casual listing of examples with no sense of chaos
〜や〜など: neutral, non-exhaustive noun list, mostly written
〜たり〜たり: lists representative actions, without the overwhelmed feeling

similar: 〜とか〜とか: casual listing of examples with no sense of chaos
〜や〜など: neutral, non-exhaustive noun list, mostly written
〜たり〜たり: lists representative actions, without the overwhelmed feeling

examples.en: It was precisely because I experienced failure that I came to understand other people's pain.
examples.ja: 失敗を経験したからこそ、人の痛みが分かるようになった。

examples.en: It is precisely because you are busy that you should make a point of setting aside time to rest.
examples.ja: 忙しいからこそ、意識して休む時間を作るべきだ。

examples.cloze: 期待しているからこそ
examples.en: The only reason I'm being strict is that I expect a lot from you.
examples.ja: 厳しく言うのは、あなたに期待しているからこそなんですよ。

records.formation: 普通形 + からこそ
records.meaning: precisely because …; it is because … that …
records.nuance: Singles out the stated reason as the real one, often a reason that might seem surprising or paradoxical. Used in conversation and essays, frequently closed with 〜のだ / 〜んです.

relatedReferences.text: 〜から / 〜ので: plain reason without emphasis
〜ばこそ: literary, formal equivalent (N1)
〜だけに: 'precisely because … (as one would expect / all the more)', with an evaluative tone

similar: 〜から / 〜ので: plain reason without emphasis
〜ばこそ: literary, formal equivalent (N1)
〜だけに: 'precisely because … (as one would expect / all the more)', with an evaluative tone

examples.en: My phone started ringing right in the middle of an important meeting, and I broke into a cold sweat.
examples.ja: 大事な会議の最中に、携帯電話が鳴り出して冷や汗をかいた。

examples.en: Right in the middle of my shower, the hot water suddenly stopped.
examples.ja: シャワーを浴びている最中に、突然お湯が出なくなった。

examples.en: A violent thunderstorm broke out in the middle of the final, and the match was temporarily suspended.
examples.ja: 決勝戦の最中に激しい雷雨となり、試合は一時中断された。

records.formation: Vている + 最中に / Nの + 最中に
records.meaning: right in the middle of …; at the height of …
records.nuance: Marks the peak of an ongoing activity, usually when something unexpected or disruptive happens at that exact moment. Neutral register; often carries a note of bad timing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜間に: 'during', a neutral time span with no sense of interruption
〜うちに: 'while (a state lasts)', often 'before it changes'
〜途中で: 'partway through', a point in a process rather than its peak

similar: 〜間に: 'during', a neutral time span with no sense of interruption
〜うちに: 'while (a state lasts)', often 'before it changes'
〜途中で: 'partway through', a point in a process rather than its peak

examples.en: Back then, we couldn't possibly have hoped for a life as convenient as today's.
examples.ja: あの頃の私たちには、今日のような便利な生活など望むべくもなかった。

examples.en: The equipment at a small rural clinic cannot possibly compare with that of a state-of-the-art university hospital.
examples.ja: 地方の小さな診療所の設備は、最新鋭の大学病院とは比べるべくもない。

examples.en: There is no way now of knowing what was written in that letter, lost a hundred years ago.
examples.ja: 百年前に失われたその手紙に何が書かれていたのか、今となっては知るべくもない。

records.formation: V辞書形 + べくもない（する → すべくもない）
records.meaning: there is no way to …; cannot possibly …

relatedReferences.text: 〜ようがない: neutral 'there is no means to'

similar: 〜ようがない: neutral 'there is no means to'

examples.en: The fishermen hauled up a tuna of at least two metres, three of them pulling together.
examples.ja: 漁師たちは、二メートルからあるマグロを三人がかりで引き上げた。

examples.en: He opened a wine costing no less than 100,000 yen a bottle without a second thought.

examples.en: Apparently they walked a mountain road of a good ten kilometres each way to school every day.

records.formation: 数量詞 + からある (size, weight, length) / 数量詞 + からする (price) / 数量詞 + からの + N
records.meaning: as much as …; no less than … (size, weight, price)

relatedReferences.text: 〜も: plain emphasis on a large amount, more casual
〜もの: 'as many as', for counts (何千ものファン)
〜に及ぶ: 'reaching (up to)', formal and used for totals or durations

similar: 〜も: plain emphasis on a large amount, more casual
〜もの: 'as many as', for counts (何千ものファン)
〜に及ぶ: 'reaching (up to)', formal and used for totals or durations

examples.en: It is not hard to imagine how shocked fans were by the sudden announcement that the group was breaking up.
examples.ja: 突然の解散発表にファンがどれほど衝撃を受けたかは、想像に難くない。

examples.en: The feelings of elderly people leaving the place they have lived in for so many years are not hard to understand.
examples.ja: 長年住み慣れた土地を離れる高齢者の心情は、察するに難くない。

examples.en: If prices keep rising, it is easy to predict that spending by young people will cool even further.

examples.ja: 安定した水の確保は、この地域にとって最大の課題だと言っても過言ではないだろう。

records.formation: 普通形（Na・Nは「だ」省略可）+ と言っても過言ではない
records.meaning: it is no exaggeration to say …
records.nuance: Formal, typical of essays, speeches and news commentary. Makes a strong claim while signalling that it is justified, often to stress importance or scale.

relatedReferences.text: 〜と言ってもいい: softer 'one could say'; less emphatic

examples.ja: この店は料理の味もさることながら、接客の丁寧さでも評判だ。

examples.cloze: 性能もさることながら

examples.cloze: 努力もさることながら

records.formation: N + もさることながら
records.meaning: … of course, but even more so …; not only … but also
records.nuance: Grants the first item its importance, then puts the weight on the second. Formal and written, frequent in reviews, speeches and commentary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜はもとより: 'X goes without saying, and also Y', stresses X as the obvious case rather than the weight on Y

examples.en: Building on the lessons of last time, this year we doubled the number of staff.

examples.en: We will consider concrete measures after taking the survey results into account.

examples.en: Based on users' feedback, the app's screen design was greatly improved.

records.formation: N + を踏まえて / を踏まえた + N / を踏まえた上で
records.meaning: based on …; building on …; taking … into account

relatedReferences.text: 〜に基づいて: follows a fixed basis such as rules or data more strictly

examples.en: Unless drastic measures are taken, the decline in the birth rate is unlikely to stop.
examples.ja: 抜本的な対策を取らない限り、少子化の流れは止まらないだろう。

examples.en: Unless the person concerned is convinced, it's pointless no matter how much others say.
examples.ja: 本人が納得しない限り、いくら周りが言っても無駄だよ。

records.formation: Vない形 / Aくない / Naでない / Nでない + 限り
records.meaning: unless …; as long as … not
records.nuance: Names the one condition that must change for the outcome to change; the main clause is often negative or a firm prediction. Common in rules, warnings and editorials.

relatedReferences.text: 〜限り (affirmative): 'as long as …' a condition continues
〜なければ: plain 'if not', less emphatic
〜ないことには: 'unless … first'; the main clause is always negative

examples.en: Please follow the staff's instructions and evacuate calmly.

records.formation: V辞書形 / N + にしたがって（にしたがい）
records.meaning: as … (so …); in accordance with …

relatedReferences.text: 〜につれて: proportional change only, cannot mean 'follow instructions'

records.formation: N（の）/ N・ナA + である / イA・V普通形 + ゆえ（に）; 〜がゆえ（に）; 〜ゆえの + N
records.meaning: because of …; owing to … (archaic-formal)
records.nuance: A classical way of stating a cause, used in formal writing, essays and set phrases like 若さゆえ. It sounds weighty and literary.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ため(に): 'because of', the neutral everyday written form

examples.en: Work depends on your health, so if you push yourself and ruin your body, you lose everything.

records.formation: N1 + あっての + N2
records.meaning: … exists only because of …; … cannot exist without …
records.nuance: Stresses that N2 is possible only thanks to N1, often expressing gratitude or humility (お客様あっての商売). Formal; common in speeches, business mottos and interviews.

relatedReferences.text: 〜からこそ: 'precisely because', emphasizing a reason rather than dependence

examples.en: A new hire signed the contract without even reporting to their boss, and the office was thrown into an uproar.
examples.ja: 上司への報告もなしに新人が契約を結んでしまい、社内は大騒ぎになった。

examples.en: There are probably very few people who have achieved their dreams without making an effort.
examples.ja: 努力することなしに夢をかなえた人など、ほとんどいないだろう。

records.formation: N + なしに（は）/ V辞書形 + ことなしに（は）
records.meaning: without …; (with a following negative) cannot … without …
records.nuance: Somewhat formal, though set phrases like 予告なしに or 断りなしに are common in speech. Plain なしに means 'without X / without doing'; なしには is followed by a negative or impossibility to say X is an indispensable condition.

examples.en: Driving without enough sleep could easily cause a serious accident.

records.formation: Vます形 + かねない

relatedReferences.text: 〜おそれがある: formal, official 'there is a risk of', typical of reports and forecasts
〜かもしれない: neutral 'may', for good or bad outcomes
〜かねる: 'cannot (bring oneself to)', a polite refusal; different meaning despite the similar form

similar: 〜おそれがある: formal, official 'there is a risk of', typical of reports and forecasts

examples.cloze: 考え込ませずにはおかない

records.formation: Vない形 + ずにはおかない (する → せずにはおかない); also Vない形 + ないではおかない
records.meaning: cannot fail to (cause); will inevitably …; will definitely … (strong resolve)
records.nuance: A formal, assertive expression with two uses: something naturally and inevitably provokes a reaction (often with a causative, as in 感動させずにはおかない), or someone is firmly determined to do something. Common in reviews, editorials and official statements.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずにはいられない: the speaker cannot hold back their own urge; ずにはおかない is about a thing that inevitably causes a reaction, or a firm will
〜ずにはすまない: an obligation that circumstances or social norms make unavoidable
〜ないではおかない: the same meaning in a slightly less literary form

examples.en: Even if we hurry now, we probably won't make the last train.

examples.en: Even supposing it's technically possible, it would be hard to realise on cost grounds.

records.formation: 普通形 + としても
records.meaning: even if we suppose …; even if …
records.nuance: Grants a hypothetical premise and asserts the outcome stays the same. Often with たとえ or 仮に; neutral to formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ても: plain 'even if', less explicitly hypothetical
〜としたら: supposition leading to a consequence
〜にしても: also used for actual facts, more conversational

similar: 〜ても: plain 'even if', less explicitly hypothetical

examples.en: However expensive a camera is, if you can't make good use of it, it's worthless.

examples.en: All the money you worked to save is gone the moment you fall for a scam.

examples.en: Precious photos and documents are lost for good once your computer breaks. Back up often.

records.formation: Vば（Vなければ・Vてしまえば を含む） / Aければ + それまでだ
records.meaning: if …, it is all over; once …, that's the end of it
records.nuance: Says that one event makes everything else pointless, often after a concessive どんなに or せっかく. Tone is resigned or cautionary, frequently used to warn or to justify a precaution.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たらおしまいだ: casual spoken equivalent

audit.why: としては can present another person's standpoint as well as the speaker's own (e.g. 彼としては), so the contrast wrongly restricts its subject.

records.formation: N（人・立場）+ にしたら／にすれば
records.meaning: from …'s point of view; for …
records.nuance: The speaker imagines another party's feelings or position, often to explain why they might see things differently. Conversational to neutral; にすれば is slightly more formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にとって: neutral 'for'; states importance or value, not imagined feelings
〜からすると／からすれば: a judgment made from a standpoint, which may be one's own

similar: 〜にとって: neutral 'for'; states importance or value, not imagined feelings

examples.ja: 三連休の初日とあって、高速道路は各地で大渋滞となった。

records.formation: N / 普通形（N・Naは「だ」なし） + とあって
records.meaning: given that … (special circumstance)
records.nuance: Explains that because of a special, noteworthy circumstance, a natural reaction followed, such as crowds or excitement. Common in news reports; not used for the speaker's own intentions or requests.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけあって: 'as you'd expect of', praises a quality matching a status

similar: 〜だけあって: 'as you'd expect of', praises a quality matching a status
〜ので／〜から: neutral reason, no sense of a special occasion

examples.en: This year's new hires are even more motivated than in previous years.

examples.en: On the first day of the long weekend, the expressway was more congested than ever.

examples.en: For families raising children, the safety of their home is a concern above all else.

records.formation: N + にもまして / 疑問詞(何・誰・いつ) + にもまして
records.meaning: even more than …; above …
records.nuance: Formal and written: X is already considerable, and the main clause goes even further. Fixed phrases いつにもまして ('more than ever') and 何にもまして ('above all') are very common in news and speeches.

relatedReferences.text: 〜以上に: plain 'more than', without implying X was already high
〜にまさる: 'surpass', usually in sayings such as 健康にまさるものはない

similar: 〜以上に: plain 'more than', without implying X was already high

examples.cloze: 散乱していたことから

records.formation: 普通形（ナAな／である、Nである） + ことから
records.meaning: from the fact that …; because …; which is why …
records.nuance: Formal and objective, typical of news and explanations. It states the evidence behind a judgment or the origin of a name or custom (〜ことから〜と呼ばれる).

relatedReferences.text: 〜から: plain reason, conversational
〜ことだから: a guess based on someone's known character, not objective evidence

similar: 〜から: plain reason, conversational
〜ことだから: a guess based on someone's known character, not objective evidence

records.formation: N / 普通形（Naである・Nである） + のみならず
records.meaning: not only … (but also)
records.nuance: Formal, written counterpart of だけでなく, common in news, reports and speeches; the second clause usually carries も or まで. Can also open a sentence as a conjunction (のみならず、…).

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでなく: the neutral everyday equivalent

examples.en: On the occasion of the new store's opening, a commemorative ceremony was held with local residents as guests.
examples.ja: 新店舗のオープンに際して、地元の方々を招いた記念式典が行われた。

examples.en: The information session will explain in detail the procedures and costs involved in studying abroad.

records.formation: N / V辞書形 + に際して / に際し / に際しての + N
records.meaning: on the occasion of …; when (undertaking) …
records.nuance: A formal 'at the time of', used for special, one-off events such as openings, departures or contracts. Typical of speeches, announcements and business documents.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にあたって: very close, but leans toward preparation and resolve before a new undertaking

similar: 〜にあたって: very close, but leans toward preparation and resolve before a new undertaking

examples.en: This article is based on interviews with people involved and on publicly available documents.
examples.ja: この記事は、関係者への取材と公開資料に基づいて書かれている。

examples.en: Under the law, fines will be imposed on businesses that break the rules.
examples.ja: 法律に基づき、違反した事業者には罰金が科される。

examples.en: Advice grounded in years of experience proved more useful than any textbook.
examples.ja: 長年の経験に基づいたアドバイスは、どんな教科書よりも役に立った。

records.formation: N + に基づいて / に基づき / に基づくN / に基づいたN

relatedReferences.text: 〜をもとに(して): uses something as raw material or a source (実話をもとにした映画); に基づいて stresses grounds for a judgement or rule

examples.en: The government unveiled new childcare support measures in order to halt the falling birthrate.
examples.ja: 政府は少子化に歯止めをかけるべく、新たな子育て支援策を打ち出した。

examples.en: The company is pursuing partnerships with local firms in order to strengthen its competitiveness in overseas markets.
examples.ja: 同社は海外市場での競争力を高めるべく、現地企業との提携を進めている。

examples.en: To open the bakery I had always dreamed of, I quit my job and went to France to train.
examples.ja: 夢だったパン屋を開業すべく、会社を辞めてフランスへ修業に出た。

records.formation: V辞書形 + べく（する → すべく／するべく）
records.meaning: in order to … (formal)
records.nuance: Formal, written 'in order to', typical of news reports and corporate announcements. The purpose is the subject's own deliberate aim, and the main clause is not a request or command.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ために: the neutral everyday way to state a purpose

examples.en: I could have helped if you'd come to me sooner, so why did you carry it all alone?
examples.ja: 早めに相談してくれれば手伝えたものを、どうして一人で抱え込んだのか。

examples.ja: 素直に謝ればすむものを、言い訳ばかりするから話がこじれるのだ。

examples.en: If only I'd left home five minutes earlier, I'd have made it.
examples.ja: あと五分早く家を出ていれば間に合ったものを。

records.formation: V・イA普通形 / ナA + な + ものを; often 〜ば〜ものを / 〜ばいいものを
records.meaning: if only …, but …; and yet … (regret or reproach)

similar: 〜のに: 'even though / if only', the everyday equivalent with similar disappointment

examples.en: The children make a mess as fast as I tidy up, so the room never gets clean.

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 + そばから

examples.ja: 薬を飲み続けても、祖母の症状は悪くなるばかりだった。

examples.en: Despite repeated talks, the rift between the two sides only deepens, and there is no solution in sight.
examples.ja: 話し合いを重ねても、両者の溝は深まるばかりで、解決の糸口は見えない。

records.formation: V辞書形 + ばかりだ

examples.en: Since you are a professional, excuses won't wash.
examples.ja: プロである以上、言い訳は通用しない。

examples.en: Once you have made a promise, you should keep it no matter what.

examples.cloze: 改ざんされていた以上

relatedReferences.text: 〜からには: same meaning, more emotional and focused on personal resolve

similar: 〜からには: same meaning, more emotional and focused on personal resolve

examples.en: I can cook, but only simple dishes.
examples.ja: 料理ができるといっても、簡単なものしか作れません。

examples.en: It may be close to the station, but it's still at least a 15-minute walk.
examples.ja: 駅から近いといっても、歩いて15分はかかる。

examples.en: It's a price increase, but apparently only a few dozen yen per item.
examples.ja: 値上げといっても、一品あたり数十円程度だそうだ。

records.formation: N / 普通形（なAだ・Nだ は「だ」を省略可） + といっても

similar: 〜とはいえ: more formal concession

examples.en: It may be spring by the calendar, but we are still having days when the mornings and evenings turn cold.
examples.ja: 暦の上では春とはいえ、朝晩はまだ冷え込む日が続いている。

records.formation: 普通形（Na・Nは「だ」省略可）+ とはいえ / 文頭で「とはいえ、〜」

relatedReferences.text: 〜といっても: plainer; often downplays the degree of the first statement

similar: 〜といっても: plainer; often downplays the degree of the first statement

examples.cloze: 直しようがありません

examples.en: Ahead of the new film's nationwide release, a special preview screening was held in Tokyo.
examples.ja: 新作映画の全国公開に先駆けて、都内で特別試写会が開かれた。

examples.en: Ahead of the rest of the industry, the company stopped giving out free plastic bags at all its stores.
examples.ja: 同社は業界に先駆けて、全店舗でレジ袋の無料配布をやめた。

examples.en: This town was the first in the country to install solar panels on the roofs of its public buildings.
examples.ja: この町は全国に先駆けて、公共施設の屋根に太陽光パネルを設置した。

records.formation: N + に先駆けて / N + に先駆け
records.meaning: ahead of …; before anyone else in …
records.nuance: Formal, typical of news and press releases: doing something before others or before a scheduled event, with a sense of being the first or a pioneer (業界に先駆けて, 全国に先駆けて, 発売に先駆けて).

relatedReferences.text: 〜に先立って: before an event as preparation, with no pioneering sense

〜を皮切りに: starting with X, then spreading to others

similar: 〜に先立って: before an event as preparation, with no pioneering sense

examples.en: Answering the fans' passionate cheers, the players ran flat out right to the end.
examples.ja: ファンの熱い声援に応えて、選手たちは最後まで全力で走り抜いた。

examples.en: In response to users' requests, the library extended its opening hours until 9 p.m.
examples.ja: 利用者の要望に応え、図書館は夜九時まで開館時間を延長した。

examples.en: In response to the applause that would not die down, the band played one more song as an encore.
examples.ja: 鳴りやまない拍手に応えて、バンドはアンコールでもう一曲演奏した。

records.formation: N + に応えて / に応え / に応えるN
records.meaning: in response to …; living up to …
records.nuance: Used with nouns like 期待, 要望, 声援 or 拍手: someone acts to meet the expectations, wishes or cheers of others. Positive in tone and fairly formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に応じて: adjusts to varying conditions or simply complies with a request; に応えて means living up to what others hope for

similar: 〜に応じて: adjusts to varying conditions or simply complies with a request; に応えて means living up to what others hope for

〜を受けて: 'in light of / following' an event, a neutral cause

examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.
examples.ja: ベルが鳴るが早いか、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。

examples.en: No sooner had sales of the limited-edition items begun than customers surged toward the counter all at once.
examples.ja: 限定品の販売が始まるが早いか、客が一斉に売り場へ押し寄せた。

examples.en: The child had barely got home before tossing aside the school bag and running off to play.
examples.ja: その子は家に帰るが早いか、ランドセルを放り出して遊びに行った。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 + が早いか
records.meaning: no sooner had … than …; the instant …
records.nuance: A literary, narrative expression for a second action that follows the first almost simultaneously, often surprisingly fast. Describes observed events, usually of others; it is not used for the speaker's own intentions, commands or requests.

relatedReferences.text: 〜や否や: almost the same meaning, even more written and formal

similar: 〜や否や: almost the same meaning, even more written and formal

examples.en: The fee changes according to how long you use it, so let's check beforehand.
examples.ja: 料金は利用時間に応じて変わるので、事前に確認しておこう。

examples.en: This gym puts together a training plan for each person suited to their fitness level.
examples.ja: このジムでは、体力に応じたトレーニングメニューを一人ひとりに組んでくれる。

examples.en: In response to requests from the disaster-hit areas, local governments across the country sent staff to help.
examples.ja: 被災地からの要請に応じて、全国の自治体が応援の職員を派遣した。

records.formation: N + に応じて / に応じ / に応じたN
records.meaning: according to …; in proportion to …; in response to (a request)
records.nuance: Means that something varies or is adjusted to fit changing conditions such as age, ability, time or need; it can also mean complying with a request or call (要請に応じて). Neutral to formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に応えて: living up to expectations or cheers, emotionally positive

records.formation: Vない形 + ことには / いAく / なAで / Nで + ないことには

audit.why: The alternative connection for ichidan verbs and する requires removing ない before adding まい: 信じまい / しまい, not 信じないまい / しないまい.

examples.ja: 信じようが信じまいが、これは実際に起きた話だ。

examples.cloze: 売れようが売れまいが
examples.en: Whether it sells or not, his way is to make what he wants to make.

audit.why: The alternative connection for ichidan verbs and する requires removing ない before adding まい: 信じまい / しまい, not 信じないまい / しないまい.

examples.ja: 売れようが売れまいが、作りたいものを作るのが彼のやり方だ。

records.meaning: whether one … or not

relatedReferences.text: 〜ても〜なくても: plain 'whether or not', neutral
〜かどうかにかかわらず: 'regardless of whether', formal and neutral

similar: 〜ても〜なくても: plain 'whether or not', neutral

examples.en: Nearly half the participants were late, and the organizer, of all people, didn't show up at all and never called.
examples.ja: 参加者の半数近くが遅刻し、幹事に至っては連絡もなく欠席した。

examples.en: Gasoline is getting pricier in this region too, but kerosene has gone up by a full 30 percent in one year.
examples.ja: この地域ではガソリン代も上がっているが、灯油に至っては一年で三割も値上がりした。

examples.en: My child hates vegetables, and as for green peppers, just seeing one is enough to bring on tears.
examples.ja: うちの子は野菜が苦手で、ピーマンに至っては見ただけで泣き出す。

records.formation: N + に至っては
records.meaning: as for … (the most extreme case); when it comes to …
records.nuance: Singles out the most extreme example in a series, usually negative, after milder cases have been mentioned. It conveys the speaker's exasperation or astonishment; used in writing and conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に関しては: neutral topic marking, with no sense of an extreme
〜さえ: 'even', marking an extreme within a single clause
〜まで: 'even (to the extent of)', less emphatic about ranking

similar: 〜に関しては: neutral topic marking, with no sense of an extreme
〜さえ: 'even', marking an extreme within a single clause
〜まで: 'even (to the extent of)', less emphatic about ranking

examples.en: I went out leaving the window open, and the whole room got soaked by the rain.
examples.ja: 窓を開けっぱなしで出かけたら、部屋中が雨で濡れていた。

examples.en: I was on my feet for a whole hour on a packed train, so my legs are worn out.
examples.ja: 満員電車で一時間立ちっぱなしだったので、もう足がくたくただ。

examples.en: Apparently a surprising number of people fall asleep with the TV left on.
examples.ja: テレビをつけっぱなしにして寝てしまう人は意外に多いという。

records.formation: Vます形 + っぱなし（だ / にする / の N）
records.meaning: leaving … as it is; keep …ing without a break
records.nuance: Colloquial and usually critical: something is left in a state that should have been dealt with (lights on, door open), or a state goes on too long (立ちっぱなし, 負けっぱなし).

relatedReferences.text: 〜まま: neutral 'as it is', with no criticism implied
〜ておく: deliberate preparation, not neglect
〜続ける: actively keep doing something

similar: 〜まま: neutral 'as it is', with no criticism implied
〜ておく: deliberate preparation, not neglect
〜続ける: actively keep doing something

examples.en: This app is free to use, but in exchange, ads appear on the screen frequently.
examples.ja: このアプリは無料で使えるかわりに、画面に広告が頻繁に表示される。

examples.en: This summer, instead of traveling abroad, I decided to relax at a nearby hot spring.
examples.ja: 今年の夏休みは海外旅行に行くかわりに、近場の温泉でのんびり過ごすことにした。

examples.en: Today I will chair the meeting in place of the department manager.
examples.ja: 部長のかわりに、本日は私が会議の進行を務めさせていただきます。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 / イAい / ナAな / Nの + かわりに
records.meaning: instead of …; in exchange for …; in place of …
records.nuance: Neutral and common in both speech and writing. It marks a substitute (doing B instead of A), a trade-off (B in return for A), or acting on someone's behalf (Nのかわりに).

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずに: simply 'without doing'; no sense of substitution or trade-off

examples.cloze: 勇気でなくてなんだろう
examples.en: Jumping into a winter river to save a total stranger: if that is not courage, what is?
examples.ja: 見ず知らずの人を助けるために冬の川に飛び込む、これが勇気でなくてなんだろう。

examples.cloze: 運命でなくてなんだろう
examples.en: Meeting again after ten years at a tiny station far from home: if that isn't fate, what is?
examples.ja: 十年ぶりに旅先の小さな駅で再会するなんて、これが運命でなくてなんだろう。

examples.cloze: 矛盾でなくてなんであろう
examples.en: While some people suffer from hunger, huge amounts of food are thrown away every day. If that is not a contradiction, what is?
examples.ja: 飢えに苦しむ人がいる一方で、毎日大量の食品が捨てられている。これが矛盾でなくてなんであろうか。

records.formation: N + でなくてなんだろう（か） / でなくてなんであろう
records.meaning: if this is not …, what is it?
records.nuance: A rhetorical question that asserts with strong emotion that something is exactly X. Literary and dramatic, found in essays, speeches and commentary, usually after これが or それが.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にほかならない: 'is nothing other than', a flat, logical assertion

examples.en: The young cooks are undergoing rigorous training under the head chef of a renowned restaurant.
examples.ja: 若手の料理人たちは、名店の料理長のもとで厳しい修業を積んでいる。

examples.en: Under a perfectly clear blue sky, the sports day was held in grand style for the first time in three years.
examples.ja: 澄み切った青空のもとで、三年ぶりの運動会が盛大に開かれた。

examples.en: The two countries resumed negotiations on the basis of an agreement to respect each other's sovereignty.
examples.ja: 両国は、互いの主権を尊重するという合意のもとに、交渉を再開した。

records.formation: N + のもとで / のもとに (〜の下で / 〜の下に)
records.meaning: under (the guidance, influence or condition of) …
records.nuance: Formal and mostly written. のもとで typically marks being under a person's guidance or within an environment; のもとに marks a principle, agreement, name or premise (合意のもとに, 〜の名のもとに).

relatedReferences.text: 〜によって: marks a means or agent, with no sense of being under someone's authority
〜の下(した)で: physical position underneath
〜をもとに: based on source material, not under guidance or conditions

similar: 〜によって: marks a means or agent, with no sense of being under someone's authority

〜をもとに: based on source material, not under guidance or conditions

examples.en: I was so nervous that I completely forgot the speech I had prepared.
examples.ja: 緊張のあまり、用意していたスピーチの内容をすっかり忘れてしまった。

examples.en: Quite a few parents worry so much about their children's future that they decide everything for them in advance.
examples.ja: 子どもの将来を心配するあまり、何でも先回りして決めてしまう親も少なくない。

examples.en: Management is being criticized for focusing so heavily on efficiency that it left the voices of frontline workers behind.
examples.ja: 経営陣は効率を重視するあまり、現場の声を置き去りにしたと批判されている。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 / Nの / な形容詞語幹な + あまり
records.meaning: so much … that …; out of excessive …
records.nuance: States that an excess of a feeling or state caused an undesirable or abnormal result. Usually paired with emotion words (緊張, 心配, 喜び); slightly formal and common in writing and news.

relatedReferences.text: 〜すぎて: casual 'too much', any cause; あまり stresses an emotional excess leading to an unusual result

examples.en: At this inn you can enjoy fresh seafood that only a local fishing port can provide.
examples.ja: この旅館では、地元の漁港ならではの新鮮な海の幸が楽しめる。

examples.en: The careful finish, with no corners cut even in the details, is something only a true craftsman could achieve.
examples.ja: 細部まで手を抜かない丁寧な仕上がりは、さすが職人ならではだ。

examples.en: This year many tourists from abroad also came to the winter festival unique to snow country.
examples.ja: 雪国ならではの冬祭りに、今年は海外からも多くの観光客が訪れた。

records.formation: N + ならでは（の N / だ）

records.nuance: Positive evaluation praising something that only that place, person or thing can offer. Common in advertising, travel writing and reviews.

relatedReferences.text: 〜らしい: 'typical of'; can be neutral or negative and does not stress uniqueness
〜に特有の: 'peculiar to'; neutral, descriptive or scientific

similar: 〜らしい: 'typical of'; can be neutral or negative and does not stress uniqueness
〜に特有の: 'peculiar to'; neutral, descriptive or scientific

examples.en: Application documents must be submitted to the secretariat by the end of this month.

examples.en: Producing a picture like this in just a few seconds — the latest AI is truly formidable.

records.formation: V辞書形 + べし（する → すべし／するべし）
records.meaning: should; must (classical)
records.nuance: Classical form of べきだ, used in rules, notices and mottos for a firm instruction. In modern casual writing it is used playfully as a strong recommendation (行くべし) or in the exclamation 恐るべし.

relatedReferences.text: 〜べきだ: the modern everyday equivalent

similar: 〜べきだ: the modern everyday equivalent

examples.en: It is precisely because they care about their children's future that parents deliberately say harsh things.
examples.ja: 子どもの将来を思えばこそ、親はあえて厳しいことを言うのだ。

examples.en: It's precisely because you're healthy that you can throw yourself fully into work you love.
examples.ja: 健康であればこそ、好きな仕事にも思い切り打ち込めるというものだ。

examples.en: It's precisely because I trust you that I want to leave this important job to you.

records.formation: Vば / Aければ / Naであれば / Nであれば + こそ（文末は 〜のだ が多い）
records.meaning: precisely because …; only because …

relatedReferences.text: 〜からこそ: same meaning, more common and conversational

similar: 〜からこそ: same meaning, more common and conversational

examples.en: Working from home is easy because there is no commute, but it is hard to separate work from life.
examples.ja: 在宅勤務は通勤がなくて楽な反面、仕事と生活の区切りがつけにくい。

examples.en: City life is stimulating, but stress also builds up easily.

records.formation: V / Aい 普通形 + 反面 / Aな な・である + 反面 / N である + 反面

examples.en: Not a single yen of tax money may be wasted.

similar: 〜から / 〜ので: neutral reason markers with no apologetic tone
〜ものですから: polite version, used in apologies to superiors or customers
