examples.en: That shop is unpleasant, starting with the staff's attitude, so I don't want to go back.
examples.ja: あの店は店員の態度からして感じが悪いから、もう行きたくない。

examples.en: Judging from the title alone, this film looks scary.
examples.ja: この映画はタイトルからして怖そうだ。

examples.en: The new system is confusing, starting with its very name; one has to say it shows too little consideration for users.
examples.ja: 新しい制度は、名称からして分かりにくく、利用者への配慮が足りないと言わざるを得ない。

records.formation: N + からして
records.meaning: starting with … itself; even (the most basic) …; judging from …
records.nuance: Picks out one basic or obvious element (often the first thing you notice) to imply that the rest is the same, usually in a critical tone; also means 'judging from'. Conversational and essayistic.

relatedReferences.text: 〜からすると: 'judging from / from the viewpoint of', a neutral basis for judgment
〜をはじめ: 'starting with', a neutral lead item in a list of examples
〜さえ: 'even', highlights an extreme case

similar: 〜からすると: 'judging from / from the viewpoint of', a neutral basis for judgment
〜をはじめ: 'starting with', a neutral lead item in a list of examples
〜さえ: 'even', highlights an extreme case

examples.en: The moment the little boy saw his mother's face, he burst into tears.
examples.ja: 男の子は母親の顔を見るなり、わっと泣き出した。

examples.en: As soon as the runner broke the finishing tape, they collapsed on the spot.
examples.ja: その選手はゴールテープを切るなり、その場に倒れ込んだ。

examples.en: My son went out early this morning and still hasn't been in touch, even though it's night.
examples.ja: 息子は朝早く出かけたなり、夜になっても連絡がない。

records.formation: V辞書形 + なり（as soon as）/ Vた形 + なり（and has stayed that way）
records.meaning: as soon as … (and stayed so)
records.nuance: Written and narrative. V辞書形 + なり describes a sudden, often surprising action right after another by the same third-person subject; not used for the speaker's own plans, commands or the future. Vたなり means a state has continued unchanged since then.

relatedReferences.text: 〜やいなや: 'the moment', even more literary; subjects may differ
〜たとたん（に）: 'just as'; more colloquial and often for something unplanned
〜たきり: 'since … and no more'; the conversational counterpart of Vたなり

similar: 〜やいなや: 'the moment', even more literary; subjects may differ
〜たとたん（に）: 'just as'; more colloquial and often for something unplanned
〜たきり: 'since … and no more'; the conversational counterpart of Vたなり

examples.en: Once you start this game, you won't be able to stop until morning.
examples.ja: このゲームは一度始めたが最後、朝までやめられなくなる。

examples.en: Once a photo has been posted online, it is almost impossible to erase it completely.
examples.ja: 写真は一度ネットに載ったが最後、完全に消すことはほぼ不可能だ。

examples.en: Once our cat gets under the kotatsu, it won't come out no matter how much you call it.
examples.ja: うちの猫は、こたつに入ったが最後、いくら呼んでも出てこない。

records.formation: Vた形 + が最後; also Vた形 + ら最後 (〜たら最後)
records.meaning: once … (something irreversible or undesirable inevitably follows)
records.nuance: Says that once a certain thing happens, a situation follows that cannot be stopped or undone, usually an unwelcome one. Used in conversation and writing, often with 一度.

relatedReferences.text: 〜たら最後: the same meaning, slightly more colloquial
〜て以来: 'ever since …', a continuing state without the sense of no return
〜たとたん(に): 'the moment that', a single event right after, not an inevitable consequence

similar: 〜たら最後: the same meaning, slightly more colloquial
〜て以来: 'ever since …', a continuing state without the sense of no return
〜たとたん(に): 'the moment that', a single event right after, not an inevitable consequence

examples.en: This summer, on top of the extreme heat, we were also plagued by frequent sudden downpours.
examples.ja: 今年の夏は猛暑に加えて、たびたびのゲリラ豪雨にも悩まされた。

examples.en: In addition to being close to the station, this hotel is known for its delicious breakfast.
examples.ja: このホテルは駅から近いのに加えて、朝食がおいしいと評判だ。

examples.en: In addition to rising prices, labor shortages are also squeezing small and medium-sized businesses.
examples.ja: 物価高に加え、人手不足も中小企業の経営を圧迫している。

records.formation: N + に加えて / に加え；普通形（なA・N は 〜な／〜である）+ の・こと + に加えて
records.meaning: in addition to …; on top of …
records.nuance: Adds a further element of the same kind to one already mentioned, often stacking up advantages or burdens. Neutral to formal; frequent in news, reports and reviews.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけでなく: 'not only … but also', more conversational
〜うえ(に): 'on top of that', clause-level and usually piling up items with the same evaluation
〜ばかりか: 'not only … but even', stressing a surprising escalation

similar: 〜だけでなく: 'not only … but also', more conversational
〜うえ(に): 'on top of that', clause-level and usually piling up items with the same evaluation
〜ばかりか: 'not only … but even', stressing a surprising escalation

examples.en: Even if we hurry now, we won't make the last train.
examples.ja: 今から急いだところで、最終電車にはもう間に合わない。

examples.en: No matter how much you explain, that person probably won't listen.
examples.ja: いくら説明したところで、あの人は聞く耳を持たないだろう。

examples.cloze: 値上がりしたところで
examples.en: Even if prices go up a little, it will only be by a few dozen yen at most, so the effect on household budgets will be small.
examples.ja: 多少値上がりしたところで、せいぜい数十円程度なので、家計への影響は小さい。

records.formation: Vた形 + ところで (often with いくら / どんなに / 今さら, followed by a negative or minimising judgement)
records.meaning: even if … (it would be no use / it would not amount to much)
records.nuance: The speaker judges that even doing something will not change the outcome, or that its effect would be small. The tone is resigned or dismissive, and the main clause is negative or minimising (〜ない, 無駄だ, せいぜい).

relatedReferences.text: 〜ても: neutral 'even if', with no sense of futility
〜としても: hypothetical 'even supposing that …'
〜たところ: 'when I did …, (I found that)', a completely different meaning

similar: 〜ても: neutral 'even if', with no sense of futility
〜としても: hypothetical 'even supposing that …'
〜たところ: 'when I did …, (I found that)', a completely different meaning

examples.en: We will announce details regarding the new product's price at next month's launch event.
examples.ja: 新製品の価格に関しては、来月の発表会で詳しくお知らせします。

examples.en: The government released new guidelines concerning the handling of personal information.
examples.ja: 政府は、個人情報の取り扱いに関する新しいガイドラインを公表した。

examples.en: The company is declining to comment on this matter for now.
examples.ja: この件に関して、会社側は現時点でコメントを控えている。

records.formation: N + に関して / に関しては / に関しても / に関する + N
records.meaning: concerning …; with regard to …
records.nuance: A formal 'about/regarding', typical of news, business and academic writing. に関する modifies a following noun; に関しまして is the polite spoken form.

relatedReferences.text: 〜について: the general, everyday 'about'; に関して sounds more formal
〜をめぐって: about a contested issue, implying debate or conflict
〜に対して: directed toward a target (attitude or action), not topic

similar: 〜について: the general, everyday 'about'; に関して sounds more formal
〜をめぐって: about a contested issue, implying debate or conflict
〜に対して: directed toward a target (attitude or action), not topic

examples.en: We are very sorry, but we are unable to answer questions concerning personal information.
examples.ja: 恐れ入りますが、個人情報に関するご質問にはお答えしかねます。

examples.en: Each side's argument has a point, so I can't really judge which one is right.
examples.ja: 双方の言い分にはそれぞれ一理あり、どちらが正しいか判断しかねる。

examples.en: As a long-time customer, I find parts of this sudden steep price rise hard to accept.
examples.ja: 突然の大幅な値上げには、長年の利用者として納得しかねる部分がある。

records.formation: Vます形 + かねる / かねます
records.meaning: cannot (quite) …; be unable to … (polite refusal)
records.nuance: A polite, indirect way of saying one cannot do something, typical of business and customer service (〜いたしかねます); also used in writing for 'find it hard to' (判断しかねる, 納得しかねる). Implies the speaker's position or the circumstances do not allow it.

relatedReferences.text: 〜かねない: 'might well (something bad)', not inability
〜にくい: hard to do physically or psychologically, but still possible
〜わけにはいかない: cannot do for social or moral reasons, more personal

similar: 〜かねない: 'might well (something bad)', not inability
〜にくい: hard to do physically or psychologically, but still possible
〜わけにはいかない: cannot do for social or moral reasons, more personal

examples.en: The veteran player announced that they would retire from active play at the end of this season.
examples.ja: そのベテラン選手は、今シーズンを限りに現役を引退すると発表した。

examples.en: I declared that I would quit smoking as of today, but my attempt to quit lasted only three days.
examples.ja: 今日を限りにタバコをやめると宣言したものの、禁煙は三日しか続かなかった。

examples.en: The streetcar line, loved for many years, will be discontinued after today's service.
examples.ja: 長年親しまれてきた路面電車が、本日の運行を限りに廃止される。

records.formation: N（今日・今回・今シーズンなど）+ を限りに
records.meaning: as of …; with … as the last time (after which it ends)
records.nuance: Marks the point after which something that has continued stops, typical of retirement, closure and quitting announcements. Formal; the separate idiom 声を限りに means 'at the top of one's voice'.

relatedReferences.text: 〜をもって: formal end point that also marks means, more official in tone
〜を最後に: the last occurrence, often noticed afterwards rather than announced
〜以降: 'from … onward', with no sense of something ending

similar: 〜をもって: formal end point that also marks means, more official in tone
〜を最後に: the last occurrence, often noticed afterwards rather than announced
〜以降: 'from … onward', with no sense of something ending

examples.en: With the redevelopment around the station, rents just keep going up.
examples.ja: 駅前の再開発が進んで、家賃は上がる一方だ。

examples.en: Because of the falling birth rate, this village's population keeps shrinking.
examples.ja: 少子化の影響で、この村の人口は減る一方だ。

examples.en: Because countermeasures came late, the damage only kept spreading.
examples.ja: 対策が遅れたため、被害は広がる一方だった。

records.formation: V辞書形 + 一方だ (verbs of change: 増える・減る・悪化する・広がる)
records.meaning: keeps on …ing; more and more (in one direction only)
records.nuance: Says a trend is moving only one way and shows no sign of stopping, usually a worrying one. Common in news and serious conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ばかりだ: same 'keeps getting …', slightly more conversational
〜つつある: a change in progress, neutral, with no sense that it cannot be stopped
〜一方で: 'while / whereas', a contrast rather than a trend

similar: 〜ばかりだ: same 'keeps getting …', slightly more conversational
〜つつある: a change in progress, neutral, with no sense that it cannot be stopped
〜一方で: 'while / whereas', a contrast rather than a trend

examples.cloze: 味といい雰囲気といい
examples.en: This restaurant is beyond criticism, both for its food and its atmosphere.
examples.ja: この店は、味といい雰囲気といい、文句のつけようがない。

examples.cloze: デザインといい使いやすさといい
examples.en: In both design and usability, this new smartphone model is remarkably polished.
examples.ja: デザインといい使いやすさといい、今回の新型スマホはかなり完成度が高い。

examples.cloze: 昨日の試合といい今日の試合といい
examples.en: Yesterday's game and today's alike, the conspicuous defensive errors are worrying.
examples.ja: 昨日の試合といい今日の試合といい、守備のミスが目立つのが気になる。

records.formation: N1 + といい + N2 + といい
records.meaning: both … and … (judging)
records.nuance: Picks out two aspects of one subject as evidence for an overall judgment, praising or criticising it. The verdict follows in the main clause; common in reviews and conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にしても〜にしても: 'whether … or …', lists cases rather than judging one subject
〜やら〜やら: lists a messy mix of things, often troubles
〜も〜も: plain 'both … and …', without the evaluative tone

similar: 〜にしても〜にしても: 'whether … or …', lists cases rather than judging one subject
〜やら〜やら: lists a messy mix of things, often troubles
〜も〜も: plain 'both … and …', without the evaluative tone

audit.why: The contrast incorrectly restricts がましい to pushy, imposing behaviour. 言い訳がましい and 未練がましい describe other negatively perceived attitudes or manners.

examples.ja: 上司の話はいつも説教じみていて、若手はうんざりしている。

examples.en: The apology at the press conference felt somehow theatrical, and it didn't seem sincere.

audit.why: The contrast incorrectly restricts がましい to pushy, imposing behaviour. 言い訳がましい and 未練がましい describe other negatively perceived attitudes or manners.

examples.ja: 記者会見での謝罪はどこか芝居じみていて、本心とは思えなかった。

records.formation: N + じみる (じみた + N / じみている)
records.meaning: smacking of …; -ish; tainted with … (negative)
records.nuance: Attaches to a limited set of nouns to say something looks or feels like what it should not, usually critically (子供じみた, 説教じみた, 芝居じみた). Also used literally for stains such as 汗じみた.

relatedReferences.text: 〜めく: 'show signs of' (春めく); neutral or positive, about something emerging

examples.cloze: 彼をおいてほかにいない
examples.en: There is no one but him we could entrust this project to.
examples.ja: このプロジェクトを任せられるのは、彼をおいてほかにいない。

examples.cloze: 京都をおいてほかにない
examples.en: If you want to study traditional Japanese crafts, there's probably no place but Kyoto.
examples.ja: 日本の伝統工芸を学ぶなら、京都をおいてほかにないだろう。

examples.en: With the economy recovering, there is no better moment than now to push ahead with reform.
examples.ja: 景気が回復しつつある今をおいて、改革に踏み切る好機はない。

records.formation: N + をおいて + ほかに〜ない / ほかにいない
records.meaning: no one / nothing but …; … above all others
records.nuance: Singles out one person, place or moment as the only fitting choice, usually as high praise or strong urging. Formal, used in speeches, editorials and recommendations.

relatedReferences.text: 〜以外に〜ない: plain 'nothing except', no sense of praise
〜を除いて: 'except for', neutral exclusion
〜しか〜ない: 'only', everyday and neutral

similar: 〜以外に〜ない: plain 'nothing except', no sense of praise

〜しか〜ない: 'only', everyday and neutral

examples.en: With the latest technology, it is even possible to analyse an entire genome in a few hours.
examples.ja: 最新の技術をもってすれば、数時間で全ゲノムを解析することも可能だ。

examples.en: Even with the world's top supercomputers, accurate earthquake prediction is still difficult.
examples.ja: 世界最高峰のスーパーコンピューターをもってしても、正確な地震予知はいまだに難しい。

examples.en: With that team's all-round strength, winning the championship is by no means just a dream.
examples.ja: あのチームの総合力をもってすれば、優勝も決して夢ではないだろう。

records.formation: N + をもってすれば / をもってしても
records.meaning: with … (something becomes possible) / even with … (it still cannot be done)
records.nuance: Highlights the power of an ability, technology or resource. をもってすれば says that with it even something hard is achievable; をもってしても says that even something that strong is not enough. Formal, common in commentary and news.
records.pattern: 〜をもってすれば／〜をもってしても

relatedReferences.text: 〜をもって: simply names the means or the end point, without the 'it can / even it cannot' judgement

similar: 〜をもって: simply names the means or the end point, without the 'it can / even it cannot' judgement

audit.why: 限り guarantees the statement while the condition holds; it does not assert that the result must cease when the condition ends.

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vている / Vない形 + 限り / Nである + 限り / い形容詞 + 限り / な形容詞な・である + 限り
records.meaning: as long as …; while … holds

similar: 〜うちは: 'while (a state continues)', more colloquial and less of a firm condition

examples.en: Spending more money doesn't automatically produce a good work.
examples.ja: お金をかければいい作品ができるというものではない。

examples.en: Practice isn't just a matter of putting in long hours; quality is what counts.
examples.ja: 練習は長時間やればいいというものではなく、質が大切だ。

examples.en: Having lots of social media followers doesn't necessarily make someone trustworthy.
examples.ja: SNSのフォロワーが多ければ信頼できるというものでもない。

records.formation: 普通形（なAだ・Nだ は「だ」を省略可） + というものではない／というものでもない
records.meaning: it does not necessarily follow that …
records.nuance: Rejects a simplistic assumption that one thing automatically leads to another, often after a conditional (〜ば〜というものではない). Measured, opinion-piece register.

relatedReferences.text: 〜わけではない: 'it's not that …', partial denial of a fact
〜とは限らない: 'not always', about likelihood
〜というものだ: affirmative, states the essence

similar: 〜わけではない: 'it's not that …', partial denial of a fact

examples.en: The team I've supported for years has finally won the title, and as a fan I couldn't be happier.
examples.ja: 長年応援してきたチームがついに優勝し、ファンとしては嬉しい限りだ。

examples.en: I never expected the new recruits to grow so dependable, and as their manager I find it enormously reassuring.
examples.ja: 新人がこれほど頼もしく育ってくれるとは、上司として心強い限りです。

examples.en: The fireworks festival I'd been looking forward to was cancelled because of the typhoon, which is a terrible shame.
examples.ja: 楽しみにしていた花火大会が台風で中止になってしまい、残念な限りです。

records.formation: イ形容詞辞書形 / ナ形容詞な + 限りだ（嬉しい・寂しい・心強い・羨ましい・残念な など感情を表す語）
records.meaning: I feel utterly …; extremely … (of the speaker's feelings)

examples.en: Taking my change of job as an opportunity, I moved from the city centre to a town near the sea.

examples.en: Poor results on my health check prompted me to start jogging every morning.
examples.ja: 健康診断の結果が悪かったのを機に、毎朝ジョギングを始めた。

examples.en: To mark its fiftieth anniversary, the company completely redesigned its logo and website.

records.formation: N + を機に / 普通形 + のを機に（を機として も可）

records.formation: V辞書形 + ことなしに(は)
records.meaning: without …ing (formal); unless one …
records.nuance: A formal 'without doing', often in the frame 'without X, Y is impossible', stressing that X is indispensable. Common in speeches, editorials and written argument.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ずに / 〜ないで: everyday 'without doing'
〜なくして(は): attaches to nouns (努力なくしては) with the same 'impossible without' sense
〜ことなく: very close; ことなく more often states a fact, ことなしには more often a condition

similar: 〜ずに / 〜ないで: everyday 'without doing'
〜なくして(は): attaches to nouns (努力なくしては) with the same 'impossible without' sense
〜ことなく: very close; ことなく more often states a fact, ことなしには more often a condition

examples.en: I would like to call on you soon to pay my respects and thank you for the other day.
examples.ja: 先日のお礼かたがた、近いうちにご挨拶に伺いたいと存じます。

examples.en: Though it is an informal way to do so, allow me to report to you and thank you in writing.
examples.ja: 略儀ながら、書中にてご報告かたがたお礼申し上げます。

examples.en: I went to see my former teacher in hospital, both to wish them well and to report on how my research was going.
examples.ja: 入院中の恩師のお見舞いかたがた、研究の進み具合を報告しに行った。

records.formation: N + かたがた (お礼 / ご挨拶 / ご報告 / お見舞い など)
records.meaning: combining … with …; while also (doing) …
records.nuance: One occasion serves two purposes: the noun before かたがた names one, and the main verb (often 伺う, 訪ねる, 申し上げる) the other. Formal and fixed, found mostly in letters and business visits with a small set of nouns.

relatedReferences.text: 〜がてら: 'while I'm at it', less stiff and usually with going out (散歩がてら); かたがた sounds out of place in casual errands
〜かたわら: pursuing two activities in parallel over a long period (job and side work)
〜ついでに: incidental 'taking the opportunity', everyday register

similar: 〜がてら: 'while I'm at it', less stiff and usually with going out (散歩がてら); かたがた sounds out of place in casual errands
〜かたわら: pursuing two activities in parallel over a long period (job and side work)
〜ついでに: incidental 'taking the opportunity', everyday register

examples.en: Showing up three hours late and not even apologizing is beyond rude.
examples.ja: 三時間も遅れてきて謝りもしないなんて、失礼にもほどがある。

examples.en: Asking 200,000 yen a month for a studio apartment is pushing it way too far.
examples.ja: ワンルームで家賃二十万円とは、強気にもほどがある。

examples.cloze: ふざけるにもほどがある
examples.en: Filming someone's mistake and turning them into a laughingstock goes way beyond a joke.
examples.ja: 人の失敗を動画にして笑いものにするなんて、ふざけるにもほどがある。

records.formation: N / なA語幹 / いA辞書形 / V辞書形 + にもほどがある
records.meaning: there is a limit to …; this is far too …
records.nuance: Conversational and emotional: the speaker protests that something has gone beyond any acceptable limit. It carries exasperation or indignation, as in 冗談にもほどがある or 失礼にもほどがある.

relatedReferences.text: 〜すぎる: neutral 'too much', with no indignation
〜にも限度がある: near-synonym, slightly more restrained
〜といったらない: extreme degree, can be positive or negative and lacks the reproach

similar: 〜すぎる: neutral 'too much', with no indignation
〜にも限度がある: near-synonym, slightly more restrained
〜といったらない: extreme degree, can be positive or negative and lacks the reproach

examples.en: It rained the whole trip, so in the end we never got to see Mount Fuji, which we had been looking forward to.
examples.ja: 旅行中は雨続きで、楽しみにしていた富士山は結局見ずじまいだった。

examples.en: Caught up in being busy, I have never once opened the cookbook I went to the trouble of buying.
examples.ja: せっかく買った料理の本も、忙しさにかまけて一度も開かずじまいになっている。

examples.en: Because the investigation was cut short, the cause of the accident was never found.
examples.ja: 調査が途中で打ち切られたため、事故の原因はわからずじまいだった。

records.formation: Vない形 + ずじまい (する → せずじまい); 〜ずじまいだ / 〜ずじまいで / 〜ずじまいになる
records.meaning: ended up never …ing (though one meant or hoped to)
records.nuance: Expresses regret or disappointment that something one intended or expected never happened before the chance passed. Common in conversation and essays, often with 結局 or とうとう.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ないまま: neutral 'while still not …'; ずじまい adds regret that the chance is now gone
〜そびれる: missed the moment to do something (言いそびれる), focused on a single lost opportunity
〜きり: 'since …, nothing further', describing a state that stopped, not an unrealised intention

similar: 〜ないまま: neutral 'while still not …'; ずじまい adds regret that the chance is now gone
〜そびれる: missed the moment to do something (言いそびれる), focused on a single lost opportunity
〜きり: 'since …, nothing further', describing a state that stopped, not an unrealised intention

examples.en: I did watch that movie, but I fell asleep halfway through and barely remember what happened.
examples.ja: その映画は見たことは見たけど、途中で寝てしまって内容はほとんど覚えていない。

examples.cloze: 便利なことは便利だが
examples.en: The new smartphone is convenient, sure, but it's far too expensive for me to buy.
examples.ja: 新しいスマホは便利なことは便利だが、値段が高すぎて手が出ない。

examples.cloze: 書いたことは書いたが
examples.en: I did technically write the report, but it isn't good enough to show anyone yet.
examples.ja: レポートは一応書いたことは書いたが、まだ人に見せられるレベルではない。

records.formation: V／イA普通形・ナAな + ことは + 同じ語 + が（けど）
records.meaning: it is true that …, but …; (I) did …, but …
records.nuance: Concedes a fact half-heartedly before a reservation; repeating the same word signals that the result falls short of expectations. Conversational and very common.

relatedReferences.text: 〜には〜が: similar repetition (行くには行くが), often about intentions
〜ものの: written concession without the repeated word
〜けれども: plain contrast without the half-hearted nuance

similar: 〜には〜が: similar repetition (行くには行くが), often about intentions
〜ものの: written concession without the repeated word
〜けれども: plain contrast without the half-hearted nuance

examples.en: Given the scale of the damage, there ought to be a formal apology from the company.
examples.ja: これだけの被害が出た以上、会社側から正式な謝罪があってしかるべきだ。

examples.cloze: 評価されてしかるべき
examples.en: The efforts of the volunteers who have supported the community for years surely deserve more recognition.
examples.ja: 長年地域を支えてきたボランティアの努力は、もっと評価されてしかるべきだろう。

examples.cloze: であってしかるべきだ
examples.en: Since it is a public facility, it ought to be designed so that anyone can use it easily.
examples.ja: 公共の施設である以上、誰にとっても使いやすい設計であってしかるべきだ。

records.formation: Vて形 / イAくて / ナA・N + であって + しかるべきだ（しかるべき + N）
records.meaning: ought to …; it is only proper to …
records.nuance: A stiff, formal way of saying something is right and natural to expect, often used to criticise that it has not happened. Common in editorials, commentary and formal complaints.

relatedReferences.text: 〜べきだ: plain 'should'; てしかるべきだ sounds weightier and implies the outcome would be only natural
〜て当然だ: 'it is natural that …', more conversational
〜てもいいはずだ: 'one would think … could', a softer, hedged claim

similar: 〜べきだ: plain 'should'; てしかるべきだ sounds weightier and implies the outcome would be only natural
〜て当然だ: 'it is natural that …', more conversational
〜てもいいはずだ: 'one would think … could', a softer, hedged claim

examples.en: When it comes to cooking skill, nobody can match the manager of our restaurant.
examples.ja: 料理の腕にかけては、うちの店の店長の右に出る者はいない。

examples.en: When it comes to speed, that player is the best on the team, but defense is still a weak point.
examples.ja: あの選手は足の速さにかけてはチームで一番だが、守備には課題が残る。

examples.en: When it comes to perseverance, I'm confident I'm second to none.
examples.ja: 粘り強さにかけては誰にも負けない自信があります。

records.formation: N + にかけては
records.meaning: when it comes to …; in terms of … (second to none)
records.nuance: Singles out a skill or field in which someone excels; the main clause is a strong positive verdict such as 誰にも負けない or 右に出る者はいない. Can be said of oneself with pride.

relatedReferences.text: 〜に関しては: neutral 'regarding', no praise implied
〜にかけて: a span of time or space, a different pattern
〜といえば: brings up an associated topic

similar: 〜に関しては: neutral 'regarding', no praise implied
〜にかけて: a span of time or space, a different pattern
〜といえば: brings up an associated topic

examples.cloze: 理由のいかんにかかわらず
examples.en: Regardless of the reason, fees once paid will not be refunded.
examples.ja: 理由のいかんにかかわらず、一度お支払いいただいた料金は返金いたしません。

examples.cloze: 結果のいかんによらず
examples.en: Regardless of their exam results, all participants will receive a certificate of completion.
examples.ja: 試験結果のいかんによらず、参加者全員に修了証が渡される。

examples.cloze: 国籍のいかんにかかわらず
examples.en: Anyone can apply for this scholarship, irrespective of nationality.
examples.ja: 国籍のいかんにかかわらず、誰でもこの奨学金に応募できる。

records.formation: N(の) + いかんにかかわらず / いかんによらず / いかんを問わず
records.meaning: regardless of …; irrespective of …
records.nuance: A very formal 'regardless of', typical of terms and conditions, official notices and regulations (理由のいかんにかかわらず). Sounds stiff in everyday speech.
records.pattern: 〜いかんにかかわらず／〜いかんによらず

relatedReferences.text: 〜にかかわらず: less formal, often with opposing pairs (晴雨にかかわらず)
〜を問わず: 'regardless of', usually broad categories (年齢を問わず)
〜いかんで: the opposite, 'depending on'

similar: 〜にかかわらず: less formal, often with opposing pairs (晴雨にかかわらず)
〜を問わず: 'regardless of', usually broad categories (年齢を問わず)
〜いかんで: the opposite, 'depending on'

examples.cloze: 起きないとも限らない
examples.en: A major earthquake could strike at any time, so I want to keep emergency food on hand.
examples.ja: 大地震がいつ起きないとも限らないので、非常食は常に備えておきたい。

examples.cloze: 聞かれていないとも限らない
examples.en: Someone might be listening, so let's not talk about that here.
examples.ja: 誰かに聞かれていないとも限らないから、ここでその話はやめておこう。

examples.cloze: つながらないとも限らない
examples.en: A moment's carelessness could lead to an accident. Using a smartphone while driving is strictly forbidden.
examples.ja: ちょっとした油断が事故につながらないとも限らない。運転中のスマホ操作は厳禁だ。

records.formation: Vない形 / Aくない / Naでない / Nでない + とも限らない
records.meaning: it is not impossible that …; there is a chance that …
records.nuance: Cautious and somewhat formal; flags an unlikely but real risk, usually to justify a precaution. Often paired with いつ, 念のため or a following 〜ておこう.

relatedReferences.text: 〜かもしれない: plain possibility, without the precautionary tone
〜とは限らない: 'not necessarily'; denies a general assumption rather than flagging a risk
〜おそれがある: formal, news-style warning that something bad may happen

similar: 〜かもしれない: plain possibility, without the precautionary tone
〜とは限らない: 'not necessarily'; denies a general assumption rather than flagging a risk
〜おそれがある: formal, news-style warning that something bad may happen

examples.en: Rather than being jostled on a packed train for a whole hour, it's better to get up a little earlier and cycle.
examples.ja: 満員電車で一時間も揺られるくらいなら、少し早起きして自転車で行ったほうがいい。

examples.en: If you were going to give up halfway, you shouldn't have taken it on in the first place.
examples.ja: 途中で投げ出すくらいなら、最初から引き受けなければよかったのに。

examples.en: Rather than paying that much at a place like that, I'd be better off cooking it myself at home.
examples.ja: あんな店で高いお金を払うくらいなら、家で自分で作ったほうがましだ。

records.formation: V辞書形 + くらいなら（ぐらいなら）
records.meaning: rather than …; if it comes to …, one would rather …
records.nuance: The speaker strongly rejects the first option as distasteful and names a preferable alternative, often with 〜ほうがいい or 〜ほうがましだ. Conversational and emotionally charged.

relatedReferences.text: 〜よりむしろ: neutral comparison without the strong distaste
〜なら: plain conditional; no rejection of the first option
〜くらいだから: 'given that it is to such an extent', gives a reason rather than rejecting

similar: 〜よりむしろ: neutral comparison without the strong distaste
〜なら: plain conditional; no rejection of the first option
〜くらいだから: 'given that it is to such an extent', gives a reason rather than rejecting

audit.why: Remove ない before adding んばかりに (泣き出さんばかりに, not 泣き出さないんばかりに); the stated する exception remains correct.

examples.en: The moment the championship was decided, the stadium was filled with cheers so loud it seemed about to split apart.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding んばかりに (泣き出さんばかりに, not 泣き出さないんばかりに); the stated する exception remains correct.

examples.ja: 優勝が決まった瞬間、スタジアムは割れんばかりの歓声に包まれた。

examples.en: As if to say 'Hurry up and go home', the staff started tidying up even though there were still customers in the shop.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding んばかりに (泣き出さんばかりに, not 泣き出さないんばかりに); the stated する exception remains correct.

examples.ja: 店員は早く帰れと言わんばかりに、まだ客がいるのに片付けを始めた。

examples.en: When she heard I had passed, my mother was so happy she was almost in tears.

audit.why: Remove ない before adding んばかりに (泣き出さんばかりに, not 泣き出さないんばかりに); the stated する exception remains correct.

examples.ja: 合格の知らせを聞いて、母は泣き出さんばかりに喜んだ。

records.formation: Vない形から「ない」を除いた形 + んばかりに / んばかりの + N / んばかりだ（する → せんばかりに）
records.meaning: as if about to …; almost …; (with to iwan) as if to say …
records.nuance: Vividly describes a state so intense that the action seems about to happen, though it does not. Literary and descriptive, used for other people or scenes; と言わんばかりに shows an attitude that says something without words.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とばかりに: 'as if to say …', the attitude is shown by an actual action
〜かのように: neutral 'as if', for any comparison, not only near-actions
〜そうなほど: plain 'so … that it seems likely to', more conversational

similar: 〜とばかりに: 'as if to say …', the attitude is shown by an actual action
〜かのように: neutral 'as if', for any comparison, not only near-actions
〜そうなほど: plain 'so … that it seems likely to', more conversational

examples.en: The method of forcibly removing protesting residents drew criticism from all quarters.
examples.ja: 抗議する住民を力ずくで排除するやり方には、各方面から批判が集まった。

examples.en: Trying to win people over with money alone is bound to fail.
examples.ja: 金ずくで人の心を動かそうとしても、うまくいくはずがない。

examples.en: These are terms both sides agreed to with full understanding, so there's no complaining now.
examples.ja: 双方が納得ずくで決めた条件なのだから、今さら文句は言えない。

records.formation: N + ずくで / ずくの + N (力ずく・腕ずく・金ずく・納得ずく・計算ずく)
records.meaning: by (sheer) means of (force, money); on the basis of (agreement, calculation)
records.nuance: Limited to a few nouns; 力ずく and 金ずく criticise getting one's way purely by force or money, while 納得ずく and 計算ずく mean 'fully agreed' or 'deliberately calculated'. Conversational and journalistic.

relatedReferences.text: 〜によって: neutral 'by means of', no criticism
〜任せ: 'leaving it to' (力任せ); relying on raw strength without control
〜をもって: formal 'by means of / with', no negative tone

similar: 〜によって: neutral 'by means of', no criticism
〜任せ: 'leaving it to' (力任せ); relying on raw strength without control
〜をもって: formal 'by means of / with', no negative tone

examples.en: Even though I know it's bad for me, I end up eating ramen in the middle of the night.
examples.ja: 体に悪いと分かりつつも、夜中にラーメンを食べてしまう。

examples.en: What is needed is continued economic growth while keeping the burden on the environment down.
examples.ja: 環境への負荷を抑えつつ、経済成長を続けることが求められている。

examples.en: Feeling the arrival of spring, I strolled slowly along the riverside path.
examples.ja: 春の訪れを感じつつ、川沿いの道をゆっくりと歩いた。

records.formation: Vます形 + つつ（も）
records.meaning: while …; even though … (formal)
records.nuance: Written and formal. つつ marks two simultaneous actions, like ながら; つつも (and sometimes plain つつ) is concessive, often admitting a fault (悪いと知りつつも).

relatedReferences.text: 〜ながら: conversational equivalent for simultaneous actions
〜ながらも: concessive, also attaches to adjectives and nouns
〜にもかかわらず: formal concession, attaches to any part of speech

similar: 〜ながら: conversational equivalent for simultaneous actions
〜ながらも: concessive, also attaches to adjectives and nouns
〜にもかかわらず: formal concession, attaches to any part of speech

examples.en: The popular band's national tour will kick off with a show in Sapporo next month and then visit twenty cities.
examples.ja: 人気バンドの全国ツアーは、来月の札幌公演を皮切りに二十都市を回る予定だ。

examples.en: Starting with its first restaurant in Osaka, the chain expanded across the Kansai region.
examples.ja: その飲食チェーンは、大阪の一号店を皮切りに関西各地へ出店を広げた。

examples.en: Starting with the discovery of inspection fraud at one factory, similar problems came to light one after another across the group's companies.
examples.ja: ある工場での検査不正の発覚を皮切りに、グループ各社で同様の問題が次々と明らかになった。

records.formation: N + を皮切りに（して）/ を皮切りとして
records.meaning: starting with …; beginning with … (and continuing on)
records.nuance: Marks the first event in a series that then spreads or continues, such as tours, store openings, product launches or a run of incidents. Neutral, common in news and business writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜を機に: an occasion that triggers a new start, not the first of a series
〜をはじめ（として）: names a representative example in a list, not the first in time
〜から: plain 'from', without the sense of a series being launched

similar: 〜を機に: an occasion that triggers a new start, not the first of a series
〜をはじめ（として）: names a representative example in a list, not the first in time
〜から: plain 'from', without the sense of a series being launched

audit.why: を込めて is not inherently warm (怒りを込めて is valid), and をかけて can also take feelings, as in 愛情をかけて; the original categorical contrast is false.

examples.en: I wrote each member of staff a letter full of gratitude for all they do day to day.

audit.why: を込めて is not inherently warm (怒りを込めて is valid), and をかけて can also take feelings, as in 愛情をかけて; the original categorical contrast is false.

examples.ja: 日頃の感謝の気持ちを込めて、スタッフ全員に手紙を書いた。

examples.en: The children folded a thousand paper cranes, wishing for the disaster area to recover as soon as possible.

audit.why: を込めて is not inherently warm (怒りを込めて is valid), and をかけて can also take feelings, as in 愛情をかけて; the original categorical contrast is false.

examples.ja: 被災地の一日も早い復興への願いを込めて、子どもたちが千羽鶴を折った。

examples.en: Tableware that a craftsman has made with loving care feels more at home in your hand the more you use it.

audit.why: を込めて is not inherently warm (怒りを込めて is valid), and をかけて can also take feelings, as in 愛情をかけて; the original categorical contrast is false.

examples.ja: 職人が心を込めて作った器は、使うほどに手になじんでくる。

records.formation: N + を込めて / N + を込めた + N (気持ち・心・願い・感謝・愛・怒り)
records.meaning: with … (feeling) put into it; full of …
records.nuance: Describes doing something while pouring an emotion or wish into it, as with gifts, letters, songs and handmade work. Often warm and sincere, but also used with negative feelings such as 怒り; common in speeches, ads and everyday talk.

relatedReferences.text: 〜を抱いて: holding a feeling or hope inside oneself (夢を抱いて上京する), not pouring it into something one makes or does
〜をかけて: putting time, money, effort or care into something (時間をかけて作る, 愛情をかけて育てる); を込めて emphasizes the feeling put into an act or object
〜をもって: formal 'with / by means of' (書面をもって, 誠意をもって); the means or attitude one acts with, not a feeling poured into the result

similar: 〜を抱いて: holding a feeling or hope inside oneself (夢を抱いて上京する), not pouring it into something one makes or does
〜をかけて: putting time, money, effort or care into something (時間をかけて作る, 愛情をかけて育てる); を込めて emphasizes the feeling put into an act or object
〜をもって: formal 'with / by means of' (書面をもって, 誠意をもって); the means or attitude one acts with, not a feeling poured into the result

examples.en: Anyone can join this course, regardless of age or experience.
examples.ja: この講座は年齢や経験を問わず、どなたでも参加できます。

examples.en: That shop is never short of customers, day or night.
examples.ja: その店は昼夜を問わず、客が絶えない。

examples.en: With online meetings now widespread, more and more companies are hiring people regardless of whether they are based in Japan or abroad.
examples.ja: オンライン会議の普及で、国内外を問わず人材を採用する企業が増えている。

records.formation: N + を問わず (年齢・性別・経験・昼夜・国内外, or paired opposites such as 男女・有無)
records.meaning: regardless of …; whether … or not
records.nuance: States that a factor makes no difference to who can take part or when something happens. Common in notices, job ads and news; slightly formal.

relatedReferences.text: 〜にかかわらず: also 'regardless', and readily follows verb or adjective pairs (行く行かないにかかわらず); を問わず almost always follows a noun
〜もかまわず: ignoring something one should care about, with a critical tone
〜によらず: 'not depending on', close in meaning but less typical in notices

similar: 〜にかかわらず: also 'regardless', and readily follows verb or adjective pairs (行く行かないにかかわらず); を問わず almost always follows a noun
〜もかまわず: ignoring something one should care about, with a critical tone
〜によらず: 'not depending on', close in meaning but less typical in notices

examples.en: Please watch your step carefully when getting off.
examples.ja: お降りの際は、足元に十分ご注意ください。

examples.en: When travelling abroad, we recommend getting vaccinated in advance.
examples.ja: 海外へ渡航する際には、事前に予防接種を受けておくことをおすすめします。

examples.en: I think I may have left my umbrella when I visited here the other day.
examples.ja: 先日こちらに伺った際に、傘を忘れてしまったようなのですが。

records.formation: V辞書形 / Vた形 + 際(に) / Nの + 際(に)
records.meaning: when …; at the time of … (formal)
records.nuance: A formal counterpart of とき, used in announcements, instructions, notices and polite business speech (お降りの際は, ご利用の際は). Rarely used in casual conversation.

relatedReferences.text: 〜とき: the neutral, everyday 'when'
〜折(に): even more formal, letters and speeches, often 'on the occasion / opportunity'
〜に際して: 'on the occasion of' a significant one-off event, more ceremonial

similar: 〜とき: the neutral, everyday 'when'
〜折(に): even more formal, letters and speeches, often 'on the occasion / opportunity'
〜に際して: 'on the occasion of' a significant one-off event, more ceremonial

examples.en: When I think this might finally be our championship year, I can hardly wait for the season opener.
examples.ja: 今年こそ優勝できるのではないかと思うと、開幕戦が待ち遠しくてならない。

examples.en: I can't stop regretting that I didn't try harder to stop it back then.
examples.ja: あのとき、なぜもっと強く止めなかったのかと悔やまれてならない。

examples.en: I can't shake the feeling that this plan has some serious oversight.
examples.ja: この計画には、何か重大な見落としがあるように思えてならない。

records.formation: Vて形 / Aくて / Naで + ならない
records.meaning: feel terribly …; cannot help feeling …
records.nuance: Expresses a strong, spontaneous feeling the speaker cannot suppress (心配でならない, 思えてならない). Slightly written and mostly about the speaker's own feelings; with verbs it mainly takes spontaneous ones such as 思える, 気になる, 悔やまれる.

relatedReferences.text: 〜てたまらない: unbearable, often physical sensations or desires; more colloquial
〜てしかたがない: can't help it, conversational
〜ずにはいられない: compelled to do an action, not just to feel

similar: 〜てたまらない: unbearable, often physical sensations or desires; more colloquial
〜てしかたがない: can't help it, conversational
〜ずにはいられない: compelled to do an action, not just to feel

examples.en: A half-read novel lay open on the desk.
examples.ja: 机の上には読みかけの小説が開いたまま置いてあった。

examples.en: I put the half-eaten bread in the fridge and completely forgot about it.
examples.ja: 食べかけのパンを冷蔵庫に入れたまま、すっかり忘れていた。

examples.en: A long-established inn that had once nearly gone out of business regained its popularity through its young successor's efforts.
examples.ja: 一度は廃業しかけた老舗の旅館が、若い後継ぎの努力で人気を取り戻した。

records.formation: Vます形 + かけの N / かけだ / かける
records.meaning: half-…ed; started but left unfinished; on the verge of …
records.nuance: Marks an action that was begun and then left incomplete, or a state about to happen (死にかける). Neutral everyday register; very common as 〜かけの + noun.

relatedReferences.text: 〜途中: 'in the middle of', neutral, no sense of being abandoned
〜ている最中: right in the middle of an action that is still going on
〜そうになる: 'nearly …', an event that almost happened (often involuntary); かける also covers an action begun and left unfinished

similar: 〜途中: 'in the middle of', neutral, no sense of being abandoned
〜ている最中: right in the middle of an action that is still going on
〜そうになる: 'nearly …', an event that almost happened (often involuntary); かける also covers an action begun and left unfinished

examples.en: While the population is growing in cities, depopulation is becoming serious in rural areas.
examples.ja: 都市部では人口が増えている一方で、地方では過疎化が深刻になっている。

examples.en: Smartphones are convenient, but the health effects of overuse have also been pointed out.
examples.ja: スマートフォンは便利な一方で、使いすぎによる健康への影響も指摘されている。

examples.en: That writer is a harsh critic, but is also keen on nurturing young talent.
examples.ja: その作家は厳しい批評家である一方で、若手の育成にも熱心だ。

records.formation: V / Aい 普通形 + 一方(で) / Aな な・である + 一方(で) / N である + 一方(で)
records.meaning: while …; whereas …; on the other hand
records.nuance: Sets two facts side by side, either contrasting aspects of one thing or two different subjects. Neutral to formal; very common in news and essays, and also used as 一方 at the start of a sentence.

relatedReferences.text: 〜反面: two opposite sides of the same subject, usually good vs bad
〜に対して: an objective contrast between two different subjects
〜一方だ: 'keeps …ing', a one-way trend

similar: 〜反面: two opposite sides of the same subject, usually good vs bad
〜に対して: an objective contrast between two different subjects
〜一方だ: 'keeps …ing', a one-way trend

audit.why: んばかりに can be figurative exaggeration; it does not assert that the action actually very nearly happens.

examples.en: He calmly carried on working as if nothing had happened.

audit.why: んばかりに can be figurative exaggeration; it does not assert that the action actually very nearly happens.

examples.ja: 彼は何事もなかったかのように、平然と仕事を続けた。

examples.en: Even though it is only May, the heat goes on as if midsummer had already arrived.

audit.why: んばかりに can be figurative exaggeration; it does not assert that the action actually very nearly happens.

examples.ja: まだ五月だというのに、まるで真夏が来たかのような暑さが続いている。

examples.cloze: 知っているかのような
examples.en: The politician answered the reporters' questions in a tone as if he knew everything.

audit.why: んばかりに can be figurative exaggeration; it does not assert that the action actually very nearly happens.

examples.ja: その政治家は、すべてを知っているかのような口ぶりで記者の質問に答えた。

records.formation: 普通形 (Nである / な形容詞である) + かのように / かのような N / かのようだ
records.meaning: as if …; as though …
records.nuance: Compares something to a situation that is not actually true, stressing the 'as if' quality. Somewhat literary; common in descriptions, journalism and narration, often with まるで.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ようだ / 〜ように: general simile or conjecture; かのように stresses that it is not really so
〜みたいに: casual spoken simile
〜んばかりに: 'as if about to …' (N1), often a figurative exaggeration of appearance or intensity; かのように makes a broader 'as if' comparison

similar: 〜ようだ / 〜ように: general simile or conjecture; かのように stresses that it is not really so
〜みたいに: casual spoken simile

examples.en: In front of their children, parents can't very well ignore traffic lights.
examples.ja: 子どもの手前、親が信号無視をするわけにはいかない。

examples.en: Having promised at the shareholders' meeting to return to profit this year, management had no choice but to push through bold cost cuts.
examples.ja: 「今年こそ黒字化する」と株主総会で約束した手前、経営陣は大胆なコスト削減に踏み切らざるを得なかった。

examples.en: Since I've been telling everyone I'm off alcohol, I stuck to oolong tea all through the drinking party.
examples.ja: 禁酒中だと周りに言っている手前、飲み会でもずっとウーロン茶で通した。

records.formation: Nの / V普通形（Vた形・Vている形が多い）/ その + 手前
records.meaning: in front of (others); having said or done …, one cannot back down (out of face)
records.nuance: Says that someone, often the speaker, feels bound to keep up appearances, either in front of certain people or because of something already said or done. Usually followed by 〜わけにはいかない, 〜ざるを得ない or 〜なければならない, it carries a sense of awkward obligation and is used in both conversation and writing.

relatedReferences.text: 〜以上（は）: 'since, now that', a logical obligation after a clause; it never takes 'person + の' and has no idea of saving face
〜からには: 'having done X, see it through', stresses resolve rather than embarrassment
〜上は: formal written cousin of 〜以上は, again without the 'in front of others' angle

similar: 〜以上（は）: 'since, now that', a logical obligation after a clause; it never takes 'person + の' and has no idea of saving face
〜からには: 'having done X, see it through', stresses resolve rather than embarrassment
〜上は: formal written cousin of 〜以上は, again without the 'in front of others' angle

examples.en: Every dish was perfect. It really lives up to ten straight years of holding a star.
examples.ja: どの皿も完璧だった。さすが十年連続で星を獲得している店だけのことはある。

examples.en: True to being the latest model, it takes amazingly clear pictures even in the dark.
examples.ja: 最新モデルだけのことはあって、暗い場所でも驚くほどきれいに撮れる。

examples.en: This view makes it worth getting up early and climbing all the way here.
examples.ja: この景色、早起きして登ってきただけのことはあるね。

records.formation: N / Naな / Aい / V普通形 + だけのことはある
records.meaning: no wonder …; lives up to …; is worth it
records.nuance: Sentence-final evaluation: the speaker acknowledges that the result is worthy of the price, effort or reputation. Often with さすが; the connective form is だけのことはあって.

relatedReferences.text: 〜だけあって: same meaning, but used mid-sentence as a connector
〜わけだ: 'that explains it', neutral reasoning without praise
〜甲斐がある: 'worth the effort', focusing on the reward

similar: 〜だけあって: same meaning, but used mid-sentence as a connector
〜わけだ: 'that explains it', neutral reasoning without praise
〜甲斐がある: 'worth the effort', focusing on the reward

examples.en: I don't know if it's right, but it's a conclusion I reached by thinking it through in my own way.
examples.ja: 正解かどうかはわからないが、自分なりに考えて出した結論だ。

examples.en: Children, in their own way, are keenly aware of changes in the family.
examples.ja: 子どもは子どもなりに、家族の変化を敏感に感じ取っているものだ。

examples.en: If your budget is limited, there are ways to travel that you can enjoy within those limits.
examples.ja: 予算が限られているなら、限られているなりに楽しめる旅の形がある。

records.formation: N / V普通形 / Aい / Na + なりに（N を修飾するときは なりの + N）
records.meaning: in one's own way; within the limits of …; as befits …
records.nuance: Accepts a limit (age, ability, position, budget) while affirming the effort or value that fits it, as in 自分なりに or 子どもなりに. Said of a superior it can sound condescending.

relatedReferences.text: 〜らしく: matches an ideal image of something, no limitation implied
〜なりとも: literary 'even if only a little'
〜のように: 'in the manner of', neutral comparison

similar: 〜らしく: matches an ideal image of something, no limitation implied
〜なりとも: literary 'even if only a little'
〜のように: 'in the manner of', neutral comparison

examples.en: As I was idly gazing out of the window, I saw a big rainbow arching across the sky.
examples.ja: 窓の外をながめるともなくながめていたら、空に大きな虹がかかっていた。

examples.en: While I was half-listening to the radio, a song I often sang in my student days came on.
examples.ja: ラジオを聞くともなしに聞いていると、学生時代によく歌った曲が流れてきた。

examples.en: From somewhere, the toasty smell of freshly baked bread drifted over.
examples.ja: どこからともなく、焼きたてのパンの香ばしいにおいが漂ってきた。

records.formation: V辞書形 + ともなく／ともなしに（+ 同じV）/ 疑問詞（+助詞）+ ともなく
records.meaning: without meaning to; idly; (with a question word) from somewhere / at some point
records.nuance: Literary and descriptive. Portrays an action done absent-mindedly, without clear intent; with question words (どこから, いつ, 誰) it means the source or time is unclear.

relatedReferences.text: 〜ともなると: unrelated in meaning ('once it comes to'); easily confused by form
なんとなく: casual adverb 'somehow, for no particular reason'
〜つもりはなかったが: explicitly 'did not intend to'; not about idle action
